It was a phase in which I felt intensely empathetic, with an openness that allowed me to share the best of myself.
summary: Автор рассказывает о двенадцатилетнем периоде преподавания, где он обнаружил свое призвание, использовал гештальт-подходы и развил сострадательную любовь, особенно проявленную в субтипе самосохранения типа 2.

title: Борьба с авторитетом и ролью учителя
text:
One of my recurring ego traps has been my bipolar relationship with authority. As a teacher, I initially felt compelled to reject my position of authority, striving for a more egalitarian approach. However, this had unintended consequences, as I insisted on being the kind of professor who was “a friend to the students.” I struggled to maintain the functional boundaries of my role as a responsible educator, in part because I had an ingrained resistance to any form of hierarchical submission. When I finally became aware of this, I often found myself oscillating between resentment and authoritarian behavior in class, especially when disruptions occurred that required me to assert my authority.

This enthusiastic phase of teaching eventually reached its peak and subsequent decline. It happened during a course when I felt my passion for academia beginning to wane, as though I had already absorbed all the lessons that experience had to offer me.
summary: Автор анализирует свою амбивалентную позицию по отношению к авторитету как преподавателя: стремление к равенству привело к размыванию границ, что в итоге вылилось в колебания между неприязнью и авторитаризмом, culminating in угасание страсти к преподаванию.

title: Невротические паттерны гордого самосохраняющегося
text:
What’s left to work on

In their neurotic form, a proud self-preserver feels extremely vulnerable to the challenges of the adult world, which demands self-assertion and personal responsibility. They don’t fully trust that their abilities are enough to protect them and allow them to function in the world. Overwhelmed by the complexity of situations, they seek closeness to those who can provide support and ease their insecurity.

As proud individuals who supposedly generate love, our seductive strategy revolves around using charm in exchange for affection. We appeal to people’s maternal and paternal instincts, making them feel compelled to cradle or shelter us. In this sense, our egocentric generosity doesn’t necessarily involve offering something tangible as a means of seduction. Instead, we use a soft voice, a gentle tone, a warm smile, and a relaxed demeanor, offering little more than warmth. Yet, this alone is often enough to be appealing and to weave fantasies of personal importance and self-centeredness.

Perhaps the most damaging effect of this dysfunctional approach to love is the inability to fully enjoy real achievements. Satisfaction always seems tainted by a lurking sense of manipulation and a craving for recognition, distorting perception and leading to a space where false humility and inner lack become entangled.

Breaking free from this dynamic first requires becoming dissatisfied with the humiliating condition of acting incapable when one is not. Developing persistence in one’s intentions is crucial, as is learning to silence the self-critical voices that arise the moment something goes wrong. By persistence, I mean cultivating a deeper sense of consistency.
summary: Автор описывает nevротический паттерн гордого самосохраняющегося (тип 2): уязвимость, стратегия очарования через теплоту, зависимость от внешнего одобрения, невозможность наслаждаться достижениями и путь к исцелению через неудовлетворенность и настойчивость.

title: Принятие радости от собственных достижений
text: It’s essential to accept that there is a legitimate joy in being content with one’s own accomplishments, even when recognizing that, deep down, there’s a desire for them to earn validation from the world. The ego often tries to take possession of our greatest achievements by coating them in feelings of shame and insecurity. This is a trap designed to prevent self-actualization, keeping us bound to the commitment of not growing up.
summary: Обсуждается необходимость принимать радость от собственных достижений, несмотря на скрытое желание получить внешнюю валидацию, и как эго использует стыд и неуверенность, чтобы блокировать самоактуализацию.

title: Ограничения бунта и суть невроза
text:
For the proud, the intense longing for freedom cannot be sustained through defiance alone. While anger generates a surge of energy and creates the illusion of strength, rebellion tends to act more as a form of self-imposed imprisonment.

From a broader perspective, I sense that the core of this neurosis lies in the denial of life itself. All these effects radiate outward from that fundamental refusal. How can life be lived meaningfully if there is a conscious commitment to rejecting it, operating through self-sabotage? Could self-sabotage be nothing more than a child’s rebellious gesture against the arbitrariness of existence?
summary: Анализируется, как бунт и гнев создают иллюзию свободы, но на самом деле ведут к самотюремному заключению, а корень невроза видится в отказе от жизни и самосabotage как форме протеста против существования.

title: Сдача и доверие как путь к трансформации
text:
My goal is to find trust in the phrase “Thy will be done” from the Lord’s Prayer, as it represents a grateful surrender to the understanding that life expects nothing from us other than to be, not to do. As Claudio Naranjo said, embracing and surrendering to this principle is enough for everything else to follow naturally.

And some transformations…

Therapy has brought me insights that, over time, have formed a web of memories, realizations, and images that gain clarity and meaning as I connect the dots.

I’ve come to understand that a gestalt can take years to fully complete, from identifying a delicate issue to balancing it with its counterpart. While it may not be possible to erase the memory of trauma or pain, it is entirely possible to reframe its attributes through new experiences.

One example from my own life is the belief that my birth was an arbitrary event forced upon me. This belief later evolved into the realization that, even while acknowledging my painful experiences, I can fully recognize myself as responsible for the circumstances of my birth, once I begin to see them as motivated by my own choice.

But even more important than this realization is becoming aware of the process that has taken me from a state of resentment, where my vitality was paralyzed, to one where I acknowledge and accept suffering and take responsibility for how I handle it.

Without a doubt, my personal journey has led me to recognize that pain plays a role in the process of maturation. For that reason, it should not be rejected with bitterness and resentment. Pain has given me depth; it has been the raw material for the development of essential qualities such as empathy and sensitivity. Accepted pain grants a sobriety that distances us from superficial frivolity. It creates a greater sense of presence in life and an existential center of gravity. This is not about seeking or desiring pain. Because pain, when truly understood and accepted, has nothing to do with masochistic suffering. On the contrary, it becomes a powerful driving force and a condition for deeper awareness.

I once heard a therapist’s response when asked how he overcame a traumatic experience that nearly took his life. He said: “The very space that the accident opened within me for experiencing pain was the same space from which love emerged.”

On my own path, I’ve realized that transformation happens through continuity. It does not skip steps. I’ve come to understand that the heart can create beautiful melodies composed of both love and pain. And I’ve arrived at the recognition that I like people, and that accepting pain can become a path to growth.
summary: Описывается путь трансформации через сдачу, терапию и осознаниеgestalt, принятие боли как источника роста, эмпатии и присутствия, а также цитата терапевта о боли и любви как совместном пространстве исцеления.

title: Пride и сексуальный инстинкт у Энеаграммы типа 2
text:
BOOK TWO: THE SEXUAL SUBTYPE

Passion in the sphere of instinct: How pride works in the sexual

When pride invades or overtakes the realm of the sexual instinct, the focus shifts to being irresistible, unforgettable. This realm is not only about sexual relationships (understood as one of the deepest and most potentially pleasurable forms of human intimacy) but also about the emotional “I-you” connection. In the case of pride, everything emotional is exaggerated and feeds a sense of superiority. It is in this emotional bond with another person that the natural instinct for intimacy becomes most visibly distorted and redirected toward pleasure. This is the most seductive of all character types, dedicated to securing attention, love, dependence, and… everything.

The passion of pride in the sexual instinct manifests as an emotionally unstable and superficial personality: seductive, sexually provocative, almost always intoxicated by love, dazed, and prone to illogical thinking. Their impulsive behavior and impetuous nature create social problems and turbulent relationships. They are histrionic and hypomanic, tending to be both charming and frivolous, capable of crafting fascinating images that intrigue and seduce the naive.

This character is more commonly found in women. Attractive and dangerous, they embody the archetype of the femme fatale, or the vamp, feeding off others’ desire and excelling at whetting appetites and stirring hunger like no one else. They exhibit many traits of narcissistic personality.

Despite their apparent independence, they pour enormous energy into being seen and recognized as someone special. But this very desire reveals a deep dependency on others, which they try to hide. This dependency traps them in relationships, making them less free, no matter how much they try to project a wild and autonomous attitude.

title: Эротизированное детство и формирование привязанности
text: The root of this lies in having been an eroticized child in their primary relationship with a parent. They received confusing attention, where affection and pleasure blurred together. These two dimensions are naturally linked in children, but for a sexual E2, this natural bond was redirected toward eroticism due to unclear physical and emotional boundaries with their parents. They learned that love is intertwined with sexuality, and that provoking pleasure in another person is a privileged way to receive attention and, ultimately, love.
summary: Объясняет, как у сексуальной двойки в раннем возрасте смешались привязанность и сексуальность из-за размытых границ с родителями, что привело к убеждению, что любовь достигается через провоцирование удовольствия у других.

title: Повторяющиеся паттерны во взрослой жизни
text: In adulthood, this channel becomes exclusive, making it difficult to distinguish between natural sexual desire and the need for loving contact. The sexual instinct takes control, leading them to become slaves to the need to be desired above all else—often at the cost of neglecting or failing to give space to other important aspects of life, such as being cared for or finding fulfillment in social or professional fields.
summary: Описывает, как в зрелом возрасте сексуальная двойка теряет грань между сексуальностью и потребностью в любви, становясь зависимой от чувства желания и игнорируя другие сферы жизни.

title: Подарки, гордость и эмоциональная нестабильность
text: Sexual Twos possess a natural talent for making others feel good. They are generous, indulgent, and flattering. But when their pride is wounded, they can become intolerant and scornful. Always hungry for intimacy and oriented toward romantic relationships, they are passionate and delightful as long as the feeling lasts. However, they are also highly sensitive—quick to anger if they feel their pride has not been adequately reciprocated.

title: Магнитная aura и импульсивность в отношениях
text: They have a magnetic aura, often unconventional, which they use extensively in intimate relationships. They seek emotional highs, fall “madly” in love with ease, and quickly become attached to one person or thing after another. Energetic, effervescent, and animated, they are usually humorous (though their mood is volatile), active, and impulsively expressive. Their body language is lively but mixed with a more or less pronounced shyness, and their facial expressions are varied yet not always decipherable due to their ever-changing and ambivalent attitude.
summary: Описывает харизму, эмоциональную неустойчивость, импульсивность и переменчивость поведения сексуальной двойки в близких отношениях, включая непостоянство выражений лица и языка тела.

title: Отсутствие структуры и склонность к разрывам
text: They break promises and contracts. Lacking internal structure and self-discipline, they succumb to the temptation of new and exciting stimuli.
summary: Констатирует недостаток самоорганизации и дисциплины у сексуальной двойки, из-за чего она легко нарушает обязательства и следует за новыми стимулами.

title: Свидетельства о безусловной преданности и скрытом расчете
text:
As one woman describes:

I want to be the best lover, the best friend, the most creative, the most fun… the best and the greatest for my partner. In return, I want everything from him. And everything means everything! This is what excites me and gives meaning to my life.

But the moment I feel like I’m not getting “everything,” I start doubting the relationship: “It’s not the same anymore… It’s not like before.” I get hurt easily and pull away. I blame the man for not living up to my expectations, and I distance myself, certain that I will find other men who can give me what I deserve. In fact, I always have a secret list of potential candidates I can turn to (or use) to sustain the inflated image I have of myself.

ANONYMOUS

A sexual E2 bases their deeply relational drive on the need to be loved, which they pursue through a relentless generosity—giving and giving with the secret desire of becoming indispensable.

A male sexual E2 describes it like this:

I feel irresistible. Like someone unique and charming who can take control of others forever because they’ll never forget me. I no longer care about what’s sensible, reasonable, logical, or forbidden…

I turn everything into feelings, and protective barriers emerge to shield me from any pain. I can’t stand frustration, so I avoid the possibility of rejection by pre-selecting my targets. Sometimes, when I seek immediate gratification, people might give me a dumb excuse or say no. That’s when I get pissed off. I puff up my chest, act cocky, and play the part of the strong, confident, sexy man who does whatever he wants. It doesn’t last long, though. I quickly (immediately) shift my focus toward other, more promising, pleasurable alternatives. And, of course, to those who said “no,” I respond, “We’ll see about that, sweetheart,” so I can dismiss them while keeping my beloved emotions intact.

You can trust me. That’s what I signal (and it’s true), but deep down, it’s just another way to attract “fans” who admire the excellence of my charm.

I don’t need elaborate tricks to make an impact in a relationship. I don’t do anything overly complicated.

Even though I consider myself a committed partner, I love feeling love—wherever it comes from, in all its intensity. My need to be loved in proportion to my grandiosity (which sometimes happens with my wife) makes me jealous. It worries me; I need to know what’s going on with the other person, where she is. And depending on the situation, I intervene. I invade her space to influence her, to redirect her toward my well-being.

ANONYMOUS

title: Перфекционизм в работе и отношениях
text:
This eagerness can also spill over into work, as one sexual E2 explains:

I want to be “the best” at my job too, and I chase an unattainable level of perfection that keeps me from meeting deadlines. For example, I struggle to finish reports because there is always room for improvement. Or in bodywork therapy sessions, I keep pushing my clients for “just a little more.” There are no limits. It’s always “a little more,” and it’s never enough. When I reach one level, I raise the bar again. I don’t like “half measures.”

ANONYMOUS

title: Гордыня как маска страха зависимости
text:
A sexual E2 finds meaning in life by manipulating others’ needs, inflating their own ego with pride, and hiding their deep-seated fear of dependency. They commit to relationships in pursuit of love, but their devotion comes with calculated flattery and ego-stroking strategies.

My pride was in feeling irresistible, as a lover and as a partner. She could never have been happier with anyone else but me. And if we broke up, I was convinced that she, grateful, would carry my mark forever.

She also considered me an exemplary father, unlike my own. I was better than him.

LUIS HERNÁNDEZ

This dynamic creates the illusion that they have found what they seek: love and admiration—but only from those who adore them in return.
summary: Обобщает мотивацию сексуальной двойки: использование гордости и лести для скрытия страха зависимости, иллюзия достижения любви через контроль и восхищение избранных людей.

title: Contradictory need for freedom and validation in sexual E2
text: Although deeply relational, a sexual E2 also harbors a strong and contradictory need for freedom, demanding to feel independent and unattainable. However, their desire for autonomy is more of an appearance than a reality, as they are highly dependent on external validation. What they truly want is a free pass to seek out the highest levels of gratification from as many people as possible. They even adjust their personality depending on who they’re with, justifying this by believing they possess many different sides: “With each person, I bring out a different part of myself.” This is why they generally prefer one-on-one relationships.
summary: This chunk describes the sexual E2's paradoxical desire for both freedom and deep relational validation, emphasizing their adaptive persona in relationships and preference for one-on-one dynamics to maximize gratification.

title: Contrast with E8 independence
text: This sets them apart from E8s, who are truly independent to the point of not needing anyone’s approval. Feeling less emotional attachment, an 8 believes they have every right to exercise their personal freedom, and since they don’t crave external validation, they take that freedom without resorting to seductive theatrics.
summary: This chunk contrasts the sexual E2's performative independence with the genuine autonomy of E8s, highlighting that E8s do not rely on seduction or external validation to assert their freedom.

title: Testimony of a male sexual E2 on sexual pursuit and control
text:
To close, here’s a long testimony from a male sexual E2:

Watching my own behavior, I can map out the different phases I go through.

Whether there’s an external stimulus or not, when I feel the need for sex, I scan my surroundings for the best available option. (If I’m in a relationship, I look to my partner. If not, I consider all possible candidates around me.)

Once I’ve chosen someone from my mental shortlist, simply gaining their attention is enough to cancel out my initial need. Not because my sexuality has been satisfied, but because of the interaction itself. The moment contact is made, I shift into a mode of dazzling them, pulling them in, and generating intense attraction.

My initial desire for sex then takes a backseat to a bigger goal: “I will make you want me.” Once I’ve confirmed this—through kisses, caresses, or other pre-libidinal signals—the drive that originally fueled my instinct gets anesthetized.

When a conquest does lead to sex, my fundamental priority is to be the best lover. If my partner experiences pleasure through me, I tend to get caught up in it as well. But for me, the real gratification starts long before we even take our clothes off—the act itself is just the cherry on top.

If no one from my shortlist is available, or those who are don’t reciprocate, I tell myself to wait for the next opportunity. But let’s be clear: I get pissed. My frustration makes my jaw clench, my teeth grind. I get angry at myself for failing to secure a release and start looking for alternatives: masturbation, impersonal sex with strangers, etc.

At the same time, I’m hyper-aware of anything that threatens my sense of control. This creates an internal conflict between my sexual instinct and my personal will, which I resolve by suppressing my spontaneous impulses. Instead, I take a more structured approach, methodically setting up the conditions that will satisfy my unmet desires.

During the rare phases of my life when I wasn’t in love or in a relationship, I even had sex with women I wasn’t attracted to, just to meet the need. When my pride takes over, I focus so much on satisfying it (How can I charm them? How can I leave them speechless?) that I distract myself from my actual physical urges. Compared to everything else I do in order to get to sex, the act itself isn’t that significant. It lasts however long the other person needs, and it’s great while it’s happening.

I love sex and couldn’t go without it, but… I also can’t go without a dinner across from cleavage with a pair of crossed legs, discreet fondling at the bar of a music club, the buzz of champagne behind lingering gazes that make you moisten your lips with the flick of a tongue.

In fact, sex is just like everything else. I thrive on getting it, not just having it. I’m used to doing in order to achieve. This specialization ends up overshadowing what my instinct actually craves. My tamed animal impulse is only allowed to take the lead when it’s convenient, easy, and without risk. Otherwise, it fades into the background, making way for the deeper pleasure—the thrill of the chase itself.
summary: This detailed testimony outlines the sexual E2's psychological phases in sexual pursuit: from scanning for partners, to seeking validation through seduction, prioritizing the 'thrill of the chase' over physical gratification, and using control and structure to manage frustration and maintain ego satisfaction.

title: Seduction as existential compensation in sexual E2
text:
The characteristic neurotic need

Seduction, the word that defines their passion, is, for a sexual E2, a desperate attempt to fill an existential void by attaining an idealized, unattainable love. Their core belief is: “I’m not desired for who I am; I have to make myself desirable. I must be irresistible, use every tool at my disposal.” But the emotional emptiness never fills; nothing is ever enough. This fuels their relentless pursuit of ever-intensifying experiences.

A sexual E2 pushes seduction to its limits, embodying both meanings of secum ducere: leading themselves toward another to capture them, while simultaneously pulling the other person into their own orbit. They develop a keen awareness of every detail in the relationship… constantly evaluating whether they are loved, how much, and whether they are considered special. Warm, engaging, and indulgent, they anticipate the other person’s needs, sometimes even before the other is aware of them. They are always welcoming and forgiving, even when criticizing their romantic interest (though they can be ruthless when they feel distance creeping in).

However, they end up trapped in the very web they weave, often incapable of saying no to anyone who shows them appreciation, leading them into relationships they never actively chose.

Tolerant to the point of self-sacrifice, they tenaciously pursue their dream of love. Yet beneath this lies a deep arrogance and a sense of superiority over their partner, rooted in their ability to recognize and fulfill their partner’s most vulnerable needs, coupled with the firm belief that they alone can satisfy (or even change) them like no one else.

title: Sexual E2's pursuit of unavailable partners and preference for taken lovers
text:
The fact that a man was married or in a relationship was never an relationship was never an obstacle. title: Sexual E2's belief in being the ideal partner and source of their lover's success
text:
ANONYMOUS

Indeed, this sexual subtype carries a deep conviction of being the ideal partner who heals their lover’s wounds, the muse who fuels their creativity and success. They struggle to recognize just how demanding and full of unspoken conditions they are with others. As a result, they fail to see how manipulative their warmth can be—designed to provoke desire and confirm that they are unconditionally loved.

When I’m in a relationship, I want to leave an indelible mark on their very being. I want to be that unforgettable person they will remember with a smile and gratitude… forever.

I feed off their happiness and take credit for it—it’s all thanks to me. Being the one who leaves a lasting impression. Thanks to me. My presence in their soul is eternal; I know (and eventually, so will they) how special I was…

Secretly, I take pride in their growth. I know they succeeded because they were with me, because they passed through my hands. Their achievements are, in some way, mine too.

I want them to recognize how important I was to them, how unforgettable. Like in the song ‘Recuérdame’: “Remember me when you sleep, and I can guess what you dream / When you’re far from our bed, let it be me you think of / Remember me when you look into the eyes of the past / When the morning no longer rises in your arms / Remember me loving you, looking into your eyes / Tying myself to your life / Because my soul has been tattooed on your skin.”
summary: This chunk conveys the sexual E2's deep belief in their irreplaceable role in their partner's life, seeing themselves as essential to their lover's healing, creativity, and success, and desiring eternal recognition for their influence.

title: Sexual E2's need for admiration, sensitivity to criticism, and use of humor to deflect pain
text:
ANONYMOUS

Fascinated with themselves and their supposed ability to pour out endless streams of love, sexual E2s carry the belief that they can always bring a smile to others, securing an image of charm and sensuality. This image fuels their constant drive to elevate their seductive power.

They seduce, yes, but only those they deem worthy of their attention, those who are interesting enough. And to seduce, they flatter, offering excessive praise in the hope that the other will return the favor, reinforcing their inflated self-image.

At the same time, they are highly sensitive to humiliation and prone to strong reactions when criticized. Rather than taking feedback constructively, their pride is easily wounded by any suggestion that they are not exceptional. When this happens, anger takes center stage, often expressed as cynical disdain for those who, in that moment, no longer deserve their attention.

One anonymous account illustrates this:

We had known each other for years and met up in a foreign city. After a few drinks, I walked him back to his hotel, and we had a brief fling. At dawn, he told me he wanted to sleep alone. With all the dignity I could muster, I replied: “I may not be queen here, but I am a queen.” Then, grabbing my boots and clothes, I finished dressing in the hallway of his luxurious hotel (I wouldn’t even give him the satisfaction of watching me get dressed). Later, I repackaged this story as just another anecdote from my repertoire, a “drama queen” moment with a comedic twist, but the resentment remained. It took us eight years to finally talk about it and admit how I had truly felt.

I tend to spin sad or painful situations, pushing them out of my consciousness by turning them into trivialities I can laugh about, selling a positive image no matter the adversity.
summary: This chunk explores how sexual E2s maintain an inflated self-image through selective seduction and flattery, react with wounded pride to criticism, and use humor to mask emotional pain, illustrated by a personal account of prideful retaliation after rejection.

title: Sexual E2's bitter farewell and projection of self-worth onto former partner
text:

I’m pleased to inform you that I’ve deleted you as a contact. And now I finally understand why you took those relationship books with you. Looks like you really needed them. I feel like letting you know that I, too, have decided to turn the page, in your very own style—clean break, no looking back (I learned from the best, after all. I’m young and a quick study). Enjoy your tiny little prison. It suits you perfectly. And go ahead, sweeten your impotence and dissatisfaction in life with French toasts and a revolving door of lovers. Let’s see if this “new one” also enjoys the cold and the gray… at least for a while. Oh, and by the way, spinning the same tired sob story about your ex, your kid you don’t see, your miserable life… makes for a solid hook with women, I’ll give you that. But it’s so predictable… it might as well be straight out of a manual!

Maybe you don’t shine as brightly as I thought. Maybe what I saw in you was just the reflection of my own light. Meanwhile, those of us with wings will keep flying, keep building… because life has a way of giving everyone exactly what they deserve. Now, at last, I can sleep peacefully. Goodbye.

text:
First, seduce. Then, cut down.

Their generosity, though seemingly boundless, is often insincere. All E2s have a compulsive urge to give, but in sexual E2s, this is especially pronounced. They see themselves as benefactors, which makes them feel powerful. In reality, they fear they’re nothing if they’re not needed. text:
I needed to be admired, chosen, desired, especially by women, whose conquest was the ultimate goal. title: Стратегия сексуального E2: ловушка и контроль через соблазн
text:
A distinct seduction strategy of the sexual E2 is entrapment. Their prey is isolated from the rest, caught in their web—not devoured or destroyed, but slowly entangled in its silk, stuck there until they decide otherwise. They string their target along, feed them flattery and desire while never fully giving themselves, all the while spinning new webs for fresh conquests without letting go of the old ones.

The predator seduces by narrowing the victim’s field of vision. They attempt to influence the way the other thinks, feels, and acts, molding them into someone who fits their expectations. But this doesn’t mean they want a pushover. On the contrary, that would bore them. The paradox is: “Be exactly what I want you to be, while still being yourself, so that you remain interesting to me.”

Seduction is linked to an internal sense of power, of being able to do whatever I want. Everyone is “seducible”; it’s just a matter of finding the right tools to break them.

This ability to command, this feeling of being the center of the universe, is upheld by the belief that I have to be everything—or I am nothing.
summary: Описывается стратегия сексуального E2 — ловля партнеров в эмоциональную сеть через лесть и манипуляцию восприятием, сохраняя контроль и ощущение центральной значимости, основанное на убеждении, что их ценность зависит от способности быть «всем» для других.

title: Личный рассказ сексуальной E2: раны, стратегии и проявления соблазна
text:
A sexual E2 describes the nuances of her seduction style:

I have an entire arsenal of strategies and methods, ranging from bold confidence to understated elegance.

My wound is: “Look at me... because I don’t feel seen... or loved.” I longed for my father’s attention, but when I did receive it, it felt sexualized, and I was ashamed to feel his pride in me. From that place, I learned to activate all my charms to ensure people see me in the best possible light.

It’s a constant, insatiable search for love (in the form of the need to be seen, accepted, and valued in every way). I crave attention and want to be the center of it all. The worst thing is to be invisible, to feel “neutral.” I want to captivate, to leave an indelible mark. To impress.

Seduction involves my entire body, emotions, and psyche, and it comes out naturally and automatically. While I do tend to focus on attracting men, I don’t discriminate; it happens with women, children… even objects. Anything and anyone can be seduced; it’s a skill I can activate at any time.

Relationships are the most important thing in my life, and I distinguish between two types of seduction:

a) Targeted seduction. This is directed at someone specific, someone I find interesting and worthy of my attention. I want to draw them in, conquer them, and ignite mutual infatuation (fall in love and make them fall for me). Here, my focus is on being intriguing in their eyes. I become enamored with how they look at me.

b) Indiscriminate seduction. This is directed at anyone, as long as it feeds my self-image and fuels my own self-admiration. The goal is to feel amazing and see myself as desirable.

These are usually fleeting interactions, where I use relationships as fuel to uplift myself.

My signature is my smile, which is also my mask. Years ago, before today’s cosmetic advancements, I used to think the worst thing that could happen to me was losing my front teeth (the ones I brush most carefully).

I project an image of joy, playfulness, youthfulness, and fresh energy. I radiate enthusiasm, optimism, and fun. I’m constantly making little jokes.

I sell the idea of freedom and confidence in myself. I’m rebellious but agreeable at the same time.

I offer: Attention, time, energy, humor, a critical mind, understanding, exclusivity, companionship, genuine interest in you and your world (at least in the moment when I want to).

I flatter with sweet words (my grandfather used to call me “flatterer”).

Warm, welcoming, kind. I have a nice word for everyone, a knowing gesture, a piece of advice, or a personalized message. I aim to make people feel comfortable in close interactions.

I’m exceptionally detail-oriented, meticulous in planning surprises, and an excellent hostess. I love to shower others with gifts. I remember people’s names.

I like my body, my features. I move gracefully, walk with ease, swaying lightly, hips loose and fluid. Physically engaged (leaning slightly forward when listening, nodding constantly to show I’m paying attention), expressive with gestures and playful facial expressions, bright-eyed. I whistle and hum effortlessly.

Mentally: quick-witted, articulate, naturally conversational, fluid in expression. I speak with spontaneity.

Visually, I appear open, light, flexible—innocent but alternative (not mainstream or trendy), hippie chic. My style is natural; I don’t need embellishments. Just wearing earrings makes me feel fabulous.

According to a friend I asked to describe me, my attractive qualities are: “Fair, soft skin; generous, healthy curves; an aura of sensuality; bright, mischievous eyes; expressive hand gestures; a natural tendency to get physically close; boldness in speech and a daring attitude (I go for things without hesitation, even when I don’t know what I’m stepping into); curious and affectionate.” He also highlighted my warrior spirit: strong-willed, confrontational, nonconformist, free.

Another friend once told me, “There’s nothing more seductive than veiled embarrassment.” That’s when I realized even shyness could be used as a seduction strategy.
summary: Сексуальная E2 делится личным опытом: её рана — чувство незаметности и отсутствия любви, что привело к развитию арсенала соблазнительных стратегий. Она описывает два типа соблазна (целевого и indiscriminate), свою внешность, манеру поведения, ментальные и физические проявления, а также то, как даже застенчивость может стать инструментом соблазна.

title: Соблазнение в отношениях с женщинами и мужчинами
text:
With women: We met during a training session the day before, and I immediately liked her. She had to leave for a few days, so I pulled out all the stops—making her a variety of carefully prepared sandwiches for her trip, calculating and smoothing out the logistics. She was so touched by my thoughtfulness that, to this day, we are close friends.

With psychopaths: A friend of mine used to say she was terrified of encountering a potential psychopath. My mindset, on the other hand, was: “At the end of the day… they’re just human beings.” I trusted my personal charm to disarm them, even imagining I could redeem them in five minutes of conversation (“Bring the psychopaths to me…”). This same friend once reminded me of a moment when she saw me chatting casually with a woman. As we parted ways, I apparently said, “Next time you see me… don’t mug me.” It turns out she had approached me with malicious intentions, likely planning to rob me, but I instinctively defused the situation using my charm and seduction skills.

These days, I practice “conscious seduction” in my job, using it to diffuse tension when conflicts arise with angry clients. I’m pretty good at it… I always have a witty remark, a compliment, a joke, or some charming courtesy up my sleeve to transform their frustration into a smile.

With men: I either put them on a pedestal—idealized, the object of my desire—or I bury them and erase them from my world.
summary: Описывает, как автор использует очарование и соблазнение в различных социальных контекстах: с женщинами (забота и внимание), с потенциально опасными людьми (нейтрализация через charme), в работе (разрешение конфликтов) и с мужчинами (чередование идеализации и отторжения).

title: Механизм притяжения и потребность в полном внимании
text:
Attraction mechanism: When I’m in the presence of a man I’m attracted to, I automatically switch into “hunter mode.” A radar locks onto him, and even if he’s turned away or far away, there’s an invisible thread that connects us, an energy that intertwines. It’s an instinct where all my senses activate, focus, and reach out toward the person who has become my target.

I follow their trail, like a predator, concentrating fully on them while going about my day. I don’t need to look directly. I just know. And I’m extremely discreet when there are others around.

I want them to crave contact with me—laughter, glances, an irresistible urge for romance and skin-on-skin closeness…

Once contact is established, I want to tighten the thread that keeps us connected. I become fully receptive, attuned to every signal, and fixate exclusively on that person; my whole life orbits around them. I try to anchor a strong energetic thread between us, binding myself to their body.

Example: We slept in adjacent rooms, but I barely got any sleep. Between the summer heat and my own body burning with excitement from his presence, I was restless. I longed for contact; I was attracted to him, his body. Even two weeks later, I kept torturing myself with the question: “Why didn’t I sleep with him?”

I want someone who adores me and is very available to me (who gives me unlimited attention). Like the song says: “I just want a little bit of your whole life.” I have zero tolerance for a lack of full attention. Example: someone who pulls out their phone and looks at it while they’re with me, doesn’t meet my eyes when I speak, or fails to show they’re actively listening.
summary: Детально описывает инстинктивный механизм притяжения к мужчинам: состояние «охотника», гиперфокус на объекте желания, потребность в полном эмоциональном и физическом присутствии партнера, а также реакцию на недостаток внимания как на личное оскорбление.

title: Контраст в отношениях: зависимость, доминирование и месть
text:
But there’s a fine line. If you’re too available, I’ll label you as dependent, strip you of your power in my mind, and reject you. If you ignore me or aren’t fully present, I act out my anger: I challenge you, belittle you, or dismiss you with cutting remarks, picking apart your flaws. I can be ruthless and biting.

Example: He was attentive to me, but I saw him as weak, someone I could easily “devour” and bend to my will. I punished him by sleeping with his best friend, sending the message: “I’m not yours exclusively.” In another case, when he wasn’t showing enough sexual interest in me, out of spite, I went to bed with his friend.

I have chased romantic love relentlessly, idealizing both the person and the relationship. The feeling of being in love is like fuel to me; when I fall, I cling to the fantasy of how perfect it’s going to be. In a relationship: “With you, I don’t need anything else; the whole world is this, it’s now, it’s you. I make your life easier, support your goals. But in return, I need constant proof and reassurance that you’re fully invested in me. If I don’t get that, I’ll demand it… or find someone else to provide it.”

I’m attracted to a man with power. But not so much power that I can’t dominate (and manipulate) him a little. In a therapy session, I once said something that stuck with me: “If a powerful man falls in love with me, I have more power than the one who holds power. My power is that I control the man who has the most power.
summary: Исследует парадоксальную динамику в отношениях: отвержение тех, кто слишком доступен (воспринимается как слабость), месть за недостаток внимания через измены, идеализацию любви как источник энергии и стремление к контролю над могущественными мужчинами через сексуальную и эмоциональную власть.

title: Сексуальность как пространство власти и самопознания
text:
Culturally, power belongs to men. For me, sex is the space where I can take control and feel powerful. I’ve used my sex life as currency, acting out unresolved issues and “settling scores” in bed—if necessary, by withholding pleasure to frustrate the man.

Men are also objects of desire. And through sexuality, I feel loved. I crave being desired, but I’m insecure about my own desire and sometimes struggle to connect with it. I need the other person to awaken it in me.

Without my desire switched on, I can let myself be used in a way, but still take satisfaction in knowing I’m the one giving pleasure. I can also fall into a victim mindset, seeing men as enemies, invaders—rejecting and blaming them as aggressors, as violent forces, championing the “no” of women, the idea of “not selling ourselves to men.”

When my desire is active, I compete for pleasure, taking on a more dominant, traditionally masculine role.

Physical intimacy and connection are my greatest weaknesses. Eroticism and sensuality serve the purpose of seduction. Sex isn’t always the end goal, even when there’s sexual provocation and flirtation.

It’s been relatively easy for me to cross the line from friendship to something more intimate with my male friends; sleeping together has been a way to stay connected.

SONIA GOMÁ
summary: Рассматривает секс как arena для восстановления власти и работы с внутренними конфликтами, описывает колебания между чувством жертвы и доминирующей ролью, связывает физическую близость с эмоциональной уязвимостью и использует интимность как способ поддерживать связь даже с друзьями.

title: Само-любовь как центральная потребность сексуального E2
text: A person with this personality, more than wanting the other person, wants themselves as a lover—and the experience of love, the intense sensation of being in love. Of course, as long as the emotion is strong, because otherwise, they don’t even know what they’re feeling.
summary: Сексуальный E2 в первую очередь стремится ощущать себя как объект любви и переживать интенсивное чувство влюбленности, а не просто желать другого человека; без сильной эмоции они не осознают своих чувств.

title: Амбивалентность как основа соблазнения у сексуального E2
text:
Seduction comes naturally to this subtype of E2 because it thrives on deep ambivalence. They reveal and conceal, say “yes” and “no” at the same time, give and take, appear and disappear, kiss and bite, love and destroy. This is the ambiguity of seduction, the root of their shifting attitudes, volatility, and tendency to push things to the point of inauthenticity—surfacing in sexual E2s as a way of expressing a defensive conflict.

There’s also another ambivalence at play: the contrast between activity and passivity. Among the three subtypes, only the self-preservation E2 shows a degree of passivity (manifesting as a more explicit dependence on having their survival needs met), whereas the other two appear more active and independent. But this is just a mask. Beneath it, both the social E2 and, even more intensely, the sexual E2, rely on the validation they receive. Their exhibitionism (whether expressed in intimacy or social settings, aimed at one person or many) can actually be seen as a form of passivity: “Look at me” instantly translates to “Love me.” So rather than independence, it’s ambivalence at play.
summary: Сексуальный E2 проявляет глубокую амбивалентность в соблазнении — simultaneous раскрытие и сокрытие, давание и взятие, что отражает внутренний конфликт. Их внешняя активность маскирует зависимость от валидации, где демонстративность становится формой пассивной просьбы о любви.

title: Мужское и женское в динамике сексуального E2: влияние родительской модели
text:
In the sexual E2, this polarity between activity and passivity also finds further expression in the interplay between the masculine and the feminine. The sexual E2 woman, no matter how feminine and receptive she appears, is stimulated by the freedom to take what she wants (something socially coded as masculine) because she doesn’t tolerate limitations either. Often, in her childhood, there was a model of a relationship with distinctly marked roles: a masculine-aggressive figure and a feminine-passive or, at the very least, highly accommodating one.

This can be seen in the following account:

My father’s fiery anger was a constant presence in our home; he believed that strictness was the only valid way to raise children. My mother set no boundaries for him, nor did her submission have any limits: she obeyed his every order and put him above all else.

I couldn’t understand how she could so calmly hand us over to this aggressive and distant man my father had become. I felt torn between love, rage, and rebellion toward both of them.

ALBA CHARTROUX
summary: Сексуальная E2-женщина проявляет стимуляцию от принятия социально мужской роли (взять what she wants), несмотря на женственную внешность, часто из-за детской модели отношений с доминирующим отцом и пассивной матерью, что приводит к внутреннему конфликту между любовью, гневом и бунтом.

title: Мстительная амбивалентность к власти и модели мести в сексуальном E2
text:
This model of relationships has survived in her psyche, alongside a proud sense of revenge against authority—an authority that is culturally masculine, envied and rejected at the same time, in that characteristic ambivalence. She may appear to enjoy giving, but in reality, she demands to receive—challenging their target with the motto: “Si je t’aime, prends garde à toi!”(“If I love you, be on your guard!), as the fated Carmen says. There is an undercurrent of hostility, projected onto the object of desire: a male to be captured and conquered. And she can compete with that male not only by adopting his aggression—disguised as feminine seduction, cultivating a kind of psychic androgyny—but also by seducing women, whether in the pursuit of an ideal partner or simply for the pleasure of exploring another side of sexuality in freer, less conventional ways.

Sexual E2 men often grew up with a similar parental dynamic.

For example:

My mother used to tell me that my father felt proud of her and placed her on a pedestal whenever she succeeded in the impossible tasks he loved throwing at her. But soon enough, since she was not a divine being and inevitably failed at something, he would knock her down from it. That’s how my father was: he didn’t just want the most beautiful and desired woman, but also the strongest and most determined; someone infallible in his eyes. And if she wasn’t, he would punish her by refusing to speak to her for weeks on end.

LUIS HERNÁNDEZ
summary: Сексуальный E2 сохраняет детскую модель отношений с авторитарным отцом и подчиненной матерью, что порождает амбивалентную мстительность к культурно-мужественной власти: внешняя доброта маскирует требование получить что-то взамен, а соблазн становится способом захвата и завоевания, включая психоандрогинность и однополые связи.

title: Детские фантазии и компенсация через соблазн у сексуального E2
text:
The sexual E2 may eventually realize they both envy and despise their parents for making them feel excluded. This painful experience can manifest in childhood fantasies of not being their biological child, of having been secretly adopted, or something similar.

Through seduction, the sexual E2 child learned how to secure an important place. This wasn’t just a place in another person’s life, but a place in the world itself. Their compulsive drive to seduce is a call to be seen, to feel like they control relationships, to affirm their own existence. Seduction is the only way they know to escape the humiliation of being overlooked and the abyss of feeling an overwhelming emptiness.
summary: Сексуальный E2 может испытывать зависть и ненависть к родителям за чувство исключения, ведущее к фантазиям о усыновлении; соблазн становится компульсивной стратегией обретения значимости, видимости и контроля над отношениями, чтобы избежать унижения и экзистенциальной пустоты.

title: Когнитивные искажения: ложное изобилие и скрытая потребность у сексуального E2
text:
Interpersonal strategy and associated irrational ideas

The cognitive world of a sexual E2 is distorted by a core idea of overabundance, or false abundance (a term that defines the fixation common to all E2 subtypes). This belief fuels their passionate sense of superiority over others. They overestimate their capacity to give more than others, of being “universal givers,” especially in the realm of love, understanding, care, and intimacy.

They also believe they are freer or more independent than the rest of humanity.

Ultimately, they believe they are more special.

This self-centered generosity is a way of hiding their own need, their own lack. It is always the other who is missing something, and they are the ones who must provide. It’s like taking on the role of a mother to the needy—seeing themselves in the other person and giving to them: “I have more than enough, and you are lacking.” This way, they cover up their own sense of deprivation—both from themselves and from others.
summary: Когнитивный мир сексуального E2 искажен идеей ложного изобилия: они считают себя универсальными дарителями, более свободными и особенными, что на самом деле скрывает их собственную нужду и депривацию, проецируя недостаток на других и принимая роль все дающей матери.

title: Динамика власти и контроля в отношениях у сексуального E2
text:
I feel powerful when I give, and in doing so, I also control the other person. By putting myself above them, I put them in my debt. I don’t need anything—that idea is so deeply ingrained in my psyche that asking for something used to feel degrading. (And asking for forgiveness? Even more.) I still struggle to receive without feeling like I owe something in return.

With men, receiving is even harder, because it mixes with the sexual aspect, which confuses me even more. If a man invites me somewhere and pays for me, the thought immediately comes: “Will I have to pay him back ‘in kind’?” In intimacy, for years I completely rejected any positions that felt submissive: “I don’t submit. Who does he think he is? I’m not one of those women who grovels.”

Disconnected from my own sexual desire, I connect through men. And then, I enter a power struggle where I use them to get my own pleasure. Afterward, my body shuts down, expels, and rejects. And if I don’t connect, I play along, holding out until they’re done, expecting gratitude. But you will never find me there. I don’t give myself—I just pretend to.

I have a network of friendships based on one-on-one connections. If someone asks for something, I go into ‘response mode’ and that takes priority, even if it means putting my own life on hold. That’s the price of friendship, of a romantic relationship… “I can’t let you down”—I have to take responsibility.

My relationships are built on the you-and-me dynamic. I juggle multiple people one at a time, but when I have too many fronts open, I neglect my own basic needs and end up exhausted. Sometimes, I feel trapped in other people’s problems.

By approaching you with what I know you need, I reinforce my image as the ‘universal giver’ who can fulfill your desires. I run from the awareness of my own lack—of envy—which I see as humiliating and dangerous.
summary: Описание того, как сексуальный E2 использует дарение как средство контроля и утверждения власти в отношениях, избегая получения помощи из-за страха долга и уязвимости, при этом маскируя собственные потребности ролью вседающего спасителя.

title: Детские сны как отражение паттерна спасения и выгорания у сексуального E2
text:
ANONYMOUS

This cognitive pattern emerges early in life, as illustrated by a childhood dream of a sexual E2:

As a child, I dreamed that on our way to the town where we spent our summers, we got into a car accident and everyone was knocked unconscious. Even though I was little, I managed to reach the pedals and, guided by instinct, drove everyone safely to the nearest hospital. I was their savior, and they would all be forever grateful to me.

SONIA GOMÁ

A few years later, she had another dream:

I’m exhausted from carrying people. I’m riding my friend on her own motorcycle, but I realize my support has turned into her dependence; she’s stopped using her own abilities. The best thing I can do is let her fall and not pick her up.

Then, other women appear—completely relaxed—waiting for me to handle their problems, even though I’m already dealing with my own. They ask me to buy them tickets for something. “Everyone should take care of their own stuff, and I’m going to take care of mine,” I tell myself, frustrated, as I climb a steep hill in the rain.

At the end of the dream, my father appears and climbs onto my bicycle, expecting me to carry him. Resigned, I pedal with him on my back.

This pattern, learned in childhood, blinds me to my real needs. It perpetuates my difficulty in asking for things, in receiving—because it would mean admitting that I, too, need something. And more often than not, what I offer—especially love—is exactly what I need.

SONIA GOMÁ
summary: Анализ двух детских снов сексуального E2, иллюстрирующих раннее формирование паттерна спасения других при пренебрежении собственными потребностями, ведущего к эмоциональному истощению и невозможности принимать помощь.

title: Ложная самодостаточность и соревнование вместо близости: случай с фальшивым дипломом
text:
One more example by the same woman:

We had an English exam at school. During the oral section, my sister froze up, while I kept talking endlessly about the topic—we were being tested on something I’m an expert in. Thinking she would fail, I felt guilty for not saving her. So, to soften her disappointment and boost her self-esteem, I made her a fake diploma. In the end… I was the one who failed, while she passed. Now what? I cried a little, feeling disappointed and powerless, but then I brushed it off and joked: “Whatever, I consider myself passed anyway. And besides, I don’t need a diploma!”

Conclusion: Instead of admitting that I wanted my sister as my partner-in-crime for exams so I wouldn’t feel alone, I turned it into a competition. During the oral exam, my pride flared up (“I know more than her…”), then I pitied her, made her seem smaller than me, and on top of that, I tried to comfort her (thinking that lying to her with a fake diploma would actually help).

The act of giving doesn’t just reinforce my self-image as a “giver. ”It also creates an emotional debt in the other person. Whether they realize it or not, they start to see me as the generous benefactor, and they are left feeling like a lacking, indebted recipient.

SONIA GOMÁ
summary: Пример того, как сексуальный E2 превращает потенциальную близость в соревнование через избыточное darение (фальшивый диплом), чтобы сохранить образ всесильного спасителя, избегая признания собственной уязвимости и потребности в связи.

title: Иdealized образ «лучшего бывшего» и иллюзия заслуженной привязанности
text:
Another example:

I took pride in being an expert at ending relationships on good terms and in being “the best ex.” For years, I kept my former partners in my life, becoming their best friend, supporting them, offering them my shoulder to cry on, even attending some of their weddings… I maintained an exclusive and special bond with each of them, regardless of whether they were with someone else.

I believed that this unique place I held in their lives was something I had earned (after all, I had invested my time in them, and that meant I had certain acquired rights “because of what we had”). When a relationship ended, I somehow felt the person owed me for everything I gave them, for how much I loved them, for how I made them dream, for how I made them feel alive…

ANONYMOUS

This idealized self-image requires the construction and maintenance of an entire cognitive system, filled with mistaken assumptions that fuel numerous irrational expectations.
summary: Описание того, как сексуальный E2 поддерживает иллюзорную привязанность с бывшими партнерами, превращая прошлую заботу в неосознанное требование воздаяния и подпитывая когнитивную систему ложных предположений о собственном праве на любовь.

title: Идеализированный образ как продукт воображения и интеллекта
text: Pride is not specifically attached to imagination but to all mental processes: intellect, reason, and will power as well. […] The idealized image is a product of his imagination. But this is not something which is created overnight. Incessant work of intellect and imagination, most of it unconscious, goes into maintaining the private fictitious world through rationalizations, justifications, externalizations, reconciling irreconcilables—in short, through finding ways to make things appear different from what they are.
summary: Объясняет, что идеализированный образ личности E2 формируется не только воображением, но и интеллектом, разумом и волей, требуя бессознательной работы для поддержания иллюзорного самоощущения через рационализации и оправдания.

title: Иллюзии и стратегии сексуального E2 в отношениях
summary: Описывает, как сексуальный E2 маскирует свою потребность в любви через иллюзии изобилия и стратегии соблазна, основанные на убеждении в своем исключительном праве на любовь, несмотря на внутреннюю неспособность к глубоким связям из-за страха перед подлинной близостью.

title: Дарение как маскировка внутренней пустоты и неуверенности
text:
As we’ve been saying, the generosity of a sexual E2 hides motivations that are not as virtuous as they may seem. Their giving nature serves an inflated ego—a sense of pseudo-superiority: “I have so much to offer.” When they look at themselves, they see overabundance. They constantly offer their “services” to mask their deep-seated feelings of emptiness, helplessness, worthlessness, and inconsistency.

The irrational beliefs associated with this include: “If I show my needs, no one will love me,” “If I reveal my vulnerabilities, they’ll realize I’m worthless and abandon me,” and “Grown-ups give; they don’t show their needs—only if I act like a grown-up will I be loved.”

A real-life example illustrates this:

I was 27 when Manel asked me, “And you… what do you need?” The question hit me like an explosion in my mind, as if I had never heard it before. And I responded, “Well… I don’t know...” That moment marked the beginning of my personal therapy journey.
summary: Объясняет, что щедрость сексуального E2 служит защитой от чувства собственной неполноценности, маскируя внутреннюю пустоту и страх перед проявлением потребностей через убеждение, что нужно быть «взрослым» и давать, а не просить.

title: Стратегия «хорошего ребёнка» как избежание конфликта
text:
Another strategy, one that is more common among self-preservation E2s but present in all subtypes of E2, is portraying themselves as the “good boy,” or the “good girl.” It’s a way to avoid open conflict, a method of sidestepping confrontation, an implicit non-aggression pact. No one wants to hurt a child, especially not one who is “good.”

This strategy originates in childhood, in the learned behavior of trying to be loved by hiding the “bad” child. If the good child is what is socially accepted, the bad child is the one who has not hyper-adapted to the desires of others by erasing their own. The good child doesn’t desire, or at least, doesn’t make their desires obvious. Or, they only desire what is deemed “acceptable.” Therefore, the bad child is repressed, pushed into the shadow of the unconscious—along with their instincts.

The irrational beliefs associated with this are: “If I’m confrontational or express my anger, I won’t be loved,” and “If I show who I really am, I won’t be loved.”
summary: Описывает стратегию представления себя как «хорошего ребёнка» для получения любви через подавление собственных欲望 и гнева, основанную на убеждении, что проявление настоящегоself приведёт к отвержению.

title: Другие черты сексуального E2: жёсткость, агрессия и трудности с критикой
text:
Other characteristic features and psychodynamic considerations

We’ve already covered seduction, false abundance, egocentric generosity, and the denial of need. Now, let’s look at other traits that shape the personality of the sexual E2.

Some of these traits stem from the difficulty they have in sustaining attacks on their idealized self-image. They struggle to acknowledge their mistakes, are overly picky to the point of rigidity, and become disdainful when their pride is wounded. If they feel someone slipping away from them, they can turn tyrannical.

Aggressive

A sexual E2 finds it hard to ask for what they want. They can’t ask directly for fear of seeming human rather than divine, so they resort to manipulation or take on a demanding stance. They push and invade, taking up more space than is rightfully theirs, adopting a narcissistic sense of entitlement. Their life strategy revolves around securing a larger share of attention, a pattern rooted in their early family dynamics.
summary: Рассматривает дополнительные черты сексуального E2: трудности с принятием критики, склонность к жёсткости и деспотизму при угрозе самообразу, а также косвенная агрессия через манипуляции и чувство entitledности в pursuit of attention.

title: Impulsive and Aggressive Expression of Desire
text:
They are impulsive and live by the motto: “Make love and war.” When pursuing a goal, they bulldoze ahead, oblivious to their surroundings, recognizing no banner other than their desires—desires they often mistake for true needs. Their aggression manifests as sheer force in action. They raise their voice. They “buy” affection, if necessary. They stage dramatic scenes. Much like an E8, for them, the ends justify the means. Their intensity can lead to emotional disconnection, sometimes mistaken for the lustful personality. Beneath all of this lies their struggle with frustration, boundaries, and hearing “no” as an immovable barrier—something they perceive as deeply humiliating.

They can become violent, brazen, and scornful. In intimate relationships, once they reach a certain threshold of frustration, they react with indifference or leave without much consideration or lingering pain. They quickly replace what they’ve lost by seducing someone new, using attraction to cover up feelings of loss, frustration, and pain.

This differs from the social E2, who expresses aggression in a more intellectual way, through arguments and explanations. And especially from the self-preservation E2, whose aggression is buried under a childlike veneer of tantrums and sulking rather than open violence. The latter may even turn aggression inward, according to the Gestalt mechanism of retroflection. That’s something you’d rarely see in a sexual E2, who has no problem directing all their impulses outward.
summary: This chunk describes the sexual E2’s impulsive, aggressive approach to desire and relationships, emphasizing their forceful pursuit of needs, intolerance of frustration, tendency to replace lost connections quickly, and contrast with other E2 subtypes in how aggression is expressed.

title: Hypersensitivity and Pride Defense
text:
Hypersensitive

Pride rests on an inflated self-image that sometimes needs to be fiercely defended. Any confrontation, criticism, or perceived attack on this image triggers an immediate, prideful reaction. The intensity of their response has little to do with the actual stimulus; it’s fueled by their hypersensitivity.

When something manages to pierce their ego defenses and strike at their core, revealing a falsehood or deception, they explode with hyperreactivity, unable to tolerate the painful truth. Rather than allowing themselves to feel that pain or acknowledge a reality that would unravel their ego construction, they instinctively go on the offensive. Pride is often described as an emotion that’s “easily wounded.” In reality, it’s the reaction to a deep-seated, early humiliation that left them unable to differentiate between having limits, being criticized, and being humiliated.

This “thin skin” may or may not be conscious, depending on their level of maturity. But what sets the sexual E2 apart from other subtypes is their impulsive, almost “spontaneous” reactivity—an automatic, uninhibited release of emotion.
summary: This chunk explains the sexual E2’s hypersensitivity to perceived threats to their self-image, describing how their pride reacts explosively to criticism due to early humiliation, resulting in defensive aggression rather than vulnerability, and highlighting their impulsive emotional reactivity as a defining trait.

title: Idolizing Desire and Neurotic Love Patterns
text:
Idolizing desire

The passion of a sexual E2 is feeling passion—being swept away and sweeping others away in the intensity of idealized, sexualized love. Their impulses give them meaning and strength, making it difficult to renounce or postpone any desire, especially when it comes to love. Their longing becomes an uninhibited force that demands immediate gratification, using whatever manipulative tactics are necessary. They are invasive, fickle, and impatient—always chasing what they don’t yet have but believe they deserve.

Their greatest desire is to be loved and adored—to be special in love. But a sexual E2 struggles with the painful paradox that what they need most is what they are least willing to give. They need to learn how to love, yet they resist true, committed, and deep emotional surrender.

They seek a kind of love that serves a neurotic need that can never truly be satisfied. They unconsciously repeat a pattern of deficient love, based on seduction and the role it played in their early family life. At their core, they are trying to fill a void—a painful sensation that whispers that not everything is as grand or as loving as they would like to believe. This realization brushes up against envy and threatens their entire ego structure.
summary: This chunk explores the sexual E2’s obsession with intense, idealized love as a means to fill an inner void, highlighting their inability to surrender emotionally, their reliance on seduction to meet neurotic needs, and how their pursuit of love masks a deep sense of lack and envy.

title: Impulsivity, Freedom, and Boundary Avoidance
text:
Impulsive and without limits

Someone this wild and impulsive craves freedom. There’s a lack of boundaries, a thrill in breaking the rules—not out of deep conviction, but out of a need to feel rather than to think. As one sexual E2 puts it: “For me, rules are just general guidelines.”

This personality type has a deep-seated fear of external limitations. Their addiction to emotional highs creates an illusion of freedom, which might be mistaken for true spontaneity, but is actually an inability to resist immediate gratification. This makes them appear inconsistent and irresponsible.

From childhood, sexual E2s have often been used to getting what they want. It’s an echo of the Oedipal dynamic where they secured an intimate, special place with the parent of the opposite sex, often at the ambiguous encouragement of that parent, while pushing aside the same-sex parent (with whom they typically have a conflicted relationship).

Among all E2s, the sexual subtype is the wildest and freest. Far more so than the self-preservation E2, for example, who takes on a more childlike stance, giving up much of their freedom in exchange for parental privilege. To be the “good boy” or “good girl,” they sacrifice their spontaneity and free impulse, whereas the sexual E2 refuses to be tamed.

Freedom, or rather, the feeling of being “free” is closely tied to a lack of boundaries, either because none were ever imposed or because they came from an overpowering authority figure, whom they seduced to overcome their fear of being crushed, of death itself.
summary: This chunk details the sexual E2’s pursuit of freedom through impulsivity and boundarylessness, linking it to early Oedipal dynamics and contrasting it with the more restrained self-preservation E2, while revealing that their sense of freedom is rooted in fear and emotional dependency rather than autonomy.

title: Covert Dependency Beneath the Facade of Independence
text:
Dependent

Though they appear independent, sexual E2s champion a kind of freedom they often confuse with recklessness. In reality, they are covertly dependent—so much so that they can’t even admit it to themselves, as doing so would shatter their idealized self-image. They need others to validate them and to provide emotional and physical contact, through which they ultimately get what they want.
summary: This chunk reveals the paradox of the sexual E2’s apparent independence, exposing their deep, unconscious dependency on others for validation and emotional-physical contact, which they deny to protect their inflated self-image.

title: Терапия и кризис отношений у сексуальных E2
text: Because they deny their own sense of lack, they usually seek therapy only when a relationship crisis shakes them—when they feel abandoned and the foundation of their pride crumbles.
summary: Сексуальные E2 избегают терапии до тех пор, пока кризис в отношениях не заставит их столкнуться с чувством покинутости и рушением их гордости, что связано с их отрицанием внутренней недостаточности.

title: Гистриония как театральность эмоций у сексуальных E2
text:
Histrionic

These days, the term histrionic is widely used to describe the emotional theatrics of E2s, particularly sexual E2s, who are experts at dramatizing emotions. They are sometimes labeled hysterical, not in the clinical sense, but in the sense of being intensely emotional and impulsive, where emotions overpower reason and lead to dramatic outbursts. However, histrionic is a more accurate term, as it highlights their performative nature.

This emotional display is often unrelated to their true motivations. It’s merely a performance designed to achieve something else, while their real need—the one driving their emotional energy—remains hidden. Much of this happens unconsciously because every genuine desire or feeling is linked to a sense of deficiency, something that doesn’t fit within their inflated self-image and is therefore pushed into the unconscious through E2’s primary defense mechanism: repression. While putting on emotional scenes is characteristic of Twos in general, the theatrical, expansive, and aggressive nature of the sexual E2 makes it the most scandalous and brazen subtype.

Histrionics, then, are particularly evident in sexual E2s. The more trapped they are within their own character structure, the better they become at acting out affection in all its forms. Unlike social or self-preservation E2s, their expressions of passion are more unrestrained and shameless. They can become so swept up in their own emotional outpourings that words fail them; their eyes, hands, and entire body are not enough to convey what they feel. They want to pierce through others with their voice, their gaze, and the fire of their passion.

The most unrestrained of sexual E2s excel at expressing anger and struggle, channeling their emotions into a catharsis reminiscent of an actor in a climactic scene. In seduction, they can reach extraordinary levels of creativity and expressiveness: a feline rhythm, a gaze that captivates and dominates, a magnetic blend of sweetness and strength, warmth and instinct, an effortless ease with physical contact, a natural comfort with nudity, and a love of erotic expression that brings them immense pleasure.
summary: Сексуальные E2 проявляют гистрионические черты через театральную, импульсивную эмоциональность, которая служит выступлением для満ятия скрытых потребностей, а их подавленная недостаточность вытесняется через репрессию, делая их проявления страсти наиболее uncontrolled и экспрессивными среди всех подтипов E2.

title: Бунт и нарушение правил как способ выделиться у сексуальных E2
text:
Rebels and rule-breakers

E2s often experience a nagging sense of being a fraud, which makes them feel fake and, consequently, guilty. One of their escape routes is breaking social rules, not out of genuine independence in thought or action, but as a neurotic need to stand out and gain the admiration of those who piqued their interest.

The sexual subtype takes this into the realm of romantic and sexual relationships, sometimes leading them to explore throuples and polyamory. Through their sexual freedom, they see themselves as pioneers of new social norms. Their vitality and confidence often make them feel superior to those who follow more traditional relationship structures.

It’s not uncommon for sexual E2s to champion the triumph of desire, sometimes in ways that seem provocative or even scandalous to common sensibilities. This, however, is just another way to feed their narcissistic self-image.

They crave the exhilaration of relationships in which they imagine themselves as the center of the other person’s desire. Without intense emotional connections, they feel empty, isolated, and dangerously sad. They cling to the illusion that it’s others who depend on their generous affection—when in reality, it is they who need constant reassurance of their worth.
summary: Сексуальные E2 нарушают социальные правила не из истинной свободы, а из nevротической потребности выделиться и получить одобрение, часто проявляя это в нетрадиционных отношениях и полигамии, чтобы поддержать свою грандиозную самоимидж и избежать чувства фальши.

title: Гедонизм как逃 от боли и источник удовольствия у сексуальных E2
text:
Hedonistic

Sexual E2s are pure hedonists. Their pursuit of pleasure serves as an escape from pain and anything that might frustrate them—something they simply cannot tolerate. How could anyone say no to them? How could anyone fail to adore them!

Because they refuse to face limits, they often ensnare others in a constant game of seduction, dangling the promise of pleasure. These games satisfy not only their hedonistic cravings but also their need for novelty and excitement. As Claudio Naranjo notes, the pursuit of pleasure can sometimes act as a substitute for true enjoyment. E2s, desperate to eliminate anything unpleasant, unsettling, or dissatisfying from their lives, seek refuge in love. When they feel unloved, their low tolerance for frustration triggers either anger or restless agitation, both of which help them escape the dreaded monotony of routine.

Their hedonism also makes them voracious consumers of relationships and material goods. They indulge their intense desire to give and receive pleasure, often without restraint.
summary: Сексуальные E2 стремятся к удовольствию как способу избежать боли и фрустрации, используя соблазн и любовь как заменители истинного наслаждения, при этом их гедонизм проявляется в ненасытном потреблении отношений и материальных благ, часто без самоконтроля.

title: Идеализированный самообраз сексуальных E2 как защита от ран
text:
Idealized self-image

The self-image of a sexual E2 is grandiose and inflated. In their own fantasy, they are radiant and magnificent. But this fantasy is not grounded in reality. It is a dream, a contagious one. It’s so convincing that even others buy into it. It’s different from the narcissism of E3s, whose image-consciousness is backed by tangible achievements, packed schedules, gym memberships, designer wardrobes, or extravagant cosmetic procedures.

For sexual E2s, the image of a vamp or femme fatale—someone who must be desired and admired—is a way to compensate for deep-seated childhood wounds. But the energy spent maintaining this illusion only distances them further from their true selves.

Their self-presentation is theatrical, layered with all the elements of a well-crafted deception: an intimate, sultry tone of voice; provocative gestures and attire; and an exaggerated generosity that seems almost suspicious in its excess.
summary: Сексуальные E2 создают грандиозный, teatralный самообраз вамп или фатальной женщины, чтобы компенсировать детские травмы, но это иллюзия, основанная на обмане и избыточной щедрости, которая отдаляет их от подлинного себя.

title: Несогласованность между обещаниями и действиями у сексуальных E2
text:
Inconsistent

Caught between reality and their idealized self-image, sexual E2s imagine themselves to be far more giving and helpful than they actually are.
summary: Сексуальные E2 переоценивают свою щедрость и полезность из-за конфликта между реальностью и их идеализированным самообразом, представляя себя более дающими, чем они есть на самом деле.

title: Неисполнимые обещания сексуального E2
text: They live so much in the present that they often forget what they promised the day before yesterday. They might say, “I’ll help you with that,” or “You know you can count on me,” or “I’ll support you no matter what.” But when the time comes to follow through, their words rarely translate into concrete action. The promises are often just momentary feelings—emotional impulses designed to uphold their self-image. And when the moment arrives to prove themselves, it turns out they were more invested in the idea of being generous than in actually providing support.
summary: Описывает, как сексуальные E2 часто делают обещания под влиянием сиюминутных эмоций, но не следуют им, поскольку их действия направлены больше на поддержание образа щедрого человека, чем на реальную помощь.

title: Самообраз сексуального E2 как универсального дарителя
text:
Universal givers

A sexual E2 sees themselves as superior to others, believing they have so much to give in every way. Constantly fleeing from pain and seeking pleasure through love, they cannot afford to reveal that what they lack most is precisely that—love. Instead, they present themselves as a great giver of love.

For example:

I see myself as a vast, overflowing breast, endlessly available to anyone in need. Everything in abundance, with plenty of options (better to have too much than too little; scarcity is misery).
