Or I see myself as a firefighter, rushing to put out emotional or practical fires. Always with superpowers to give and give.
summary: Сексуальные E2 позиционируют себя как безусловных и бесконечных дарителей любви и поддержки, используя метафоры вроде «переполненной груди» или «пожарного», чтобы скрыть собственную нужду в любви.

title: Превращение потребности в любовь в добродетель через воображение
text:
ENRIQUE PÉREZ

Driven by their sense of superiority, sexual E2s develop lofty principles about life, love, and relationships, seeing themselves as a moral marvel. This, in turn, leads them to overlook the real consequences of their actions and the true nature of reality.

But how do they transform their own need for love into an ability to give love? Psychoanalyst Karen Horney explains:

His need to be proud of himself is so imperative that he cannot tolerate the idea of being in the clutches of blind needs; so he uses his imagination to turn these needs into virtues, to transform them into assets of which he can be proud. But only those compulsive needs which serve his drive to actualize his idealized self undergo this transformation.

As this becomes a core part of their personality, their need for affection and to be the center of attention turns into an urge to give love and care. But through all this giving, one thought never leaves them: they expect to be recognized for what they do. Their self-aggrandizement makes them focus more on what they will receive in return than on what they are actually doing for others. It’s a continuous effort to be seen, but with such a high self-evaluation, the recognition they seek never truly arrives—ensuring a constant state of frustration.

I know I’ve always put in a lot of effort. Even now, I feel like I haven’t done enough, especially for my son. Sometimes I wish I could multiply myself. When I feel this way, no matter what I do for my son, for my closest friends, or for my patients, it always seems like too little. Then I try to shake off the thought with a firm “Enough already!”—but it’s more of a reactive defense than true self-acceptance. In the end, I always go back to doing more for others.

ANONYMOUS

This relentless effort is a defining trait of the sexual E2. It allows them to hold their head high, warding off the underlying fear that they are undeserving—an echo of their humiliated inner counterpart.
summary: Объясняет, как сексуальные E2 через воображение превращают свою потребность в любви и признании в добродетель дарения, ожидая признания в ответ, что ведет к хронической неудовлетворенности despite постоянных усилий.

title: Антиинтеллектуализм и доминирование эмоций у сексуального E2
text:
Anti-intellectual

Sexual E2s are the most emotional of the emotional types. Sexual E4s, though also dramatic and intensely expressive, have a stronger intellectual component, as they need reasoning and argumentation to assert their competence. For a sexual E2, emotion itself is the ultimate argument: things are a certain way “because I feel it.” Their assertiveness comes from their emotions rather than cognitive reasoning, and this uninhibited intensity gives them a false sense of security—the arrogance of believing they can get whatever they want.

Their perception of reality is based more on feeling than on objective facts. Emotions color everything in the present moment, and in the name of emotion, anything goes. They identify passionately with what they feel, disregarding the logical and structured world of thought, which seems heavy and lifeless to them.

I’ve always struggled to remember song lyrics, but I retain melodies with no problem. They transport me to a world of images and fantasy. Often, I remember more about the parallel world my mind creates from the music than the lyrics themselves. The chorus gives me the entry point, and from there, I take off into my own dreamlike world, carried by the notes.

TONI AGUILAR

Cognitive or intellectual ability is devalued in all E2s. This is somewhat less true for social E2s, who build an image of being responsible, serious, and hyper-adult. Self-preservation E2s, highly attuned to basic needs, focus on concrete actions to get what they want. Sexual E2s also feel more than they think, placing much greater value on emotions and sentiment than on intellect. This mindset is at the root of their primary defense mechanism: repression.
summary: Подчеркивает, что сексуальные E2 руководствуются эмоциями, а не intellectом, считая чувства окончательным аргументом, подавляя мышление через репрессию и предпочитая образный, фантазийный способ обработки информации.

title: Конкурентность в романтических отношениях как способ подтвердить уникальность
text:
Competitive

For a sexual E2, competition plays out primarily in romantic relationships. Their battle to feel unique and unforgettable becomes fierce the moment a third party appears who might overshadow them. In such cases, they can suddenly rekindle a passionate, infatuated energy, even when it’s unclear whether they actually care about the object of their affection. They don’t stop to ask themselves if they truly want that lover or friend. Their real goal is to defeat the competitor and feel like the best in the eyes of their target. The passion returns, and they believe in it completely—but once they’ve secured the prize, it may lose all value to them.
summary: Описывает, как сексуальные E2 вступают в ожесточенную конкуренцию за внимание романтического партнера, где победа важнее искренних чувств, а интерес исчезает после достижения цели.

title: Physical presence and unconventional behavior of sexual E2s
text: Sexual E2s move through the world with an open, informal, and relaxed physical presence. They appear spontaneous and at ease wherever they go, filling the space around them, even invading it. Being unconventional is one of their trademarks, whether in the way they dress or behave. They love to break norms, to be different from everyone else at all costs. They are the type to do in public what others would only do in private: taking off their shoes, putting their feet up on a sofa, showing a scar in an intimate place, falling asleep in the middle of a meeting—blatantly ignoring social conventions. Their attitude is: “I do what I want, where I want, with whomever I want.” This makes them a provocateur, though softened by their seductive strategies and their deep-seated fear of rejection.
summary: This chunk describes the open, informal, and unconventional physical presence of sexual E2s, highlighting their spontaneous behavior, norm-breaking tendencies, and provocative yet seductive demeanor rooted in a fear of rejection.

title: Wilhelm Reich’s analysis of erotic movements in sexual E2s
text:
Erotic movements

Wilhelm Reich, in Character Analysis, described the physicality of the proud personality:

The most conspicuous characteristic of both male and female examples of this type is an importunate sexual attitude. This is combined with a specific kind of physical agility exhibiting a distinct sexual nuance […] The movements of the archetype have a kind of lilting quality (not to be confused with elastic), are supple and sexually provocative. That the hysterical character is easily excited can be inferred from the appearance as a whole.

The bodily movements of a sexual E2 are graceful and sensual, reflecting a body with minimal deep muscular blockages. Their physique is energized, well-proportioned, and harmonious. They appear integrated and in tune with themselves, exuding a sense of vitality, liveliness, and agility.
summary: This chunk presents Wilhelm Reich’s description of the sexual E2’s physicality, emphasizing their importunate sexual attitude, supple and provocative movements, and overall sense of vitality and agility due to minimal muscular blockages.

title: The chainmail muscular defense in sexual E2s and its energetic function
text:
Energy reaches the most distal parts of the body, giving the skin a warm, rosy appearance. Their gaze, lively and bright, reflects their emotional state—something they share with the rest of the rigid character types in bioenergetic classification.

More specific to E2s is their muscular armor, which takes the form of a “chainmail” defense—a trait they share with E7—manifesting as a systematic and generalized rigidity. This “mesh,” located just beneath the skin at the fascia level, is an efficient mechanism for draining anxiety, as it redistributes static energy across the entire body surface. In ancient warfare, chainmail was a metal armor made of interlocking iron or steel rings designed to disperse the impact of a blow across multiple rings, effectively absorbing shocks and minimizing damage.

This bodily defense mechanism activates in response to impending anxiety, as described by a woman in this testimony:

I couldn’t stop moving; I felt energy rushing through my whole body. It was carrying me, moving me nowhere, like a caged animal. My mother told me I was hysterical, but I couldn’t do anything about it.

When I finally stopped, I felt a strong emotion in my chest, an overwhelming and unpleasant sensation, and I broke down crying uncontrollably.

ANONYMOUS

This account shows how the failure of muscular defense allows anxiety to surface, along with the repressed emotion that was sustaining it.

Thanks to this efficient drainage, E2s, especially sexual E2s, rarely experience anxiety in a direct way. Instead, it is converted into smooth, undulating, erotically charged movements that often confuse their interlocutor, sending a mixed message: on one hand, a sense of provocation; on the other, a disconnection from the intention behind the movement, which is pushed out of awareness through the psychic defense mechanism of repression.

Their erotic, seductive movements provoke sexual reactions, even when that is not their actual purpose.

As Reich puts it:

If a hysterical woman displays strong sensuality, it would be wrong to assume that she is expressing genuine sexual willingness […] The hysterical character never recognizes the meaning of his sexual behavior […] What stands out here as sexual striving is basically sexuality in the service of defense.

This sensual, flowing movement—enabled by their “chainmail” muscular defense—distinguishes them from other character types who lack their distinctive agility and mobility.
summary: This chunk explains the 'chainmail' muscular defense in sexual E2s (shared with E7), how it drains anxiety through energetic redistribution, converts repressed anxiety into erotic movements, and serves as a defense mechanism where sexuality functions to avoid emotional intimacy.

title: The seeming seductive gait and its defensive function in sexual E2s
text:
Seemingly seductive gait

Juanjo Albert, discussing the hysterical character (Enneatype Two), states: “The defensive function of pseudo-erotic contact and genital sexuality is carried out through their specialized ability to detect the risk of emotional commitment and intimacy—and to immediately withdraw when it arises.”

The most extreme expression of a sexual E2’s walk is the very image of the “vamp,” whose seduction is conveyed not just through exaggerated, sinuous movements but also through their tone of voice, emphatic phrasing, captivating gaze, overt voluptuousness, and hip sway—suggesting a promise of orgasm without its guarantee.

This signature swaying movement, along with the retracted position of the pelvis, might seem like a sign of sexual health and connection with their sexuality, but in reality, it is not. The “charged pelvis” of an E2 is energetically primed to express its power through orgasm, yet its discharge movements are restricted by stiffness and rigidity, limiting the anterior movement of the pelvis.

Emotional disconnection from sexuality

The apparent freedom and fluidity of their hips mask the core conflict of this character. Their movement is not fully connected to their chest due to one of their primary tensions—held in the diaphragm. This muscle plays a central role in breathing, influencing both the perception and expression of emotions. It regulates the intensity of feelings in the chest, either amplifying or dampening impulses from the abdomen (representing needs) and the pelvis (representing sexuality).
summary: This chunk describes the sexual E2’s seductive gait as a defensive mechanism to avoid emotional intimacy, explaining how pelvic movement appears free but is actually restricted, and how diaphragmatic tension disconnects sexuality from emotional expression.

title: Эмоциональная диссоциация и напряжение диафрагмы у сексуального E2
text: In this personality, the diaphragm is tight enough to disrupt the energetic connection between the pelvis and the chest. This tension in the diaphragm dissociates emotions from needs, severing the link between emotional life and sexuality. While we wouldn’t describe this as a full diaphragmatic block in someone with emotional expression, it does create a resistance that hinders energetic flow.
summary: Описывается, как напряжение диафрагмы у сексуального E2 нарушает связь между эмоциями, потребностями и сексуальностью, создавая сопротивление энергетическому потоку.

title: Сложность сдачи и терапевтический потенциал
text:
Difficulty with surrender

Reading the tensions and blockages in a sexual E2’s body, it becomes clear that they struggle with deep emotional surrender—this is their most significant internal split.

As Lowen states, “the hysterical character of today is not so much afraid of the genital aim as they are of the deep love feelings originating in the heart.”

This is why tantric practice, bioenergetics, integrative body therapy, psychodance, or any other body-based technique aimed at uniting genital impulses with loving impulses holds great healing potential for this character type.
summary: Обсуждается трудность сексуального E2 с глубокой эмоциональной сдачей и рекомендуются телесно-ориентированные практики для объединения генитальных и любящих импульсов.

title: Радостное выражение и финансовая автономия сексуального E2
text:
Joyful

Compared to the other subtypes of pride, the sexual E2 has an expansive, satisfied, joyful expression. This sets them apart from the social E2, whose expression is less static but slightly more serious and rigid, due to the sense of self-importance they carry.

This same joy and smile, in the self-preservation subtype, are accompanied by a childlike gaze and facial expression, often making them appear younger than they actually are.

Spendthrifts

Money gives this personality type a sense of autonomy that feels crucial. For sexual E2s, financial independence is a matter of pride rather than inner freedom—they rely on their own resources and feel humiliated if they have to show financial need.

I’ve been working since I was fifteen, during the summers. Financial independence is essential to me. I can live on very little; I can eat just bread and tomatoes, or I can splurge on lobster if I feel like it.

I’m quite a big spender. I don’t have much money to spare, but I don’t care about brand-name clothes or specific luxury items—still, I spend, and I don’t even know how. Money itself has never been important to me; it’s not something I consider when making decisions. Even in romantic relationships, I don’t care whether a man has money or not.

What matters to me is proving I’m independent, not just being independent. It’s a power dynamic in relationships; I find it difficult to accept a man paying for me. It makes me feel small, and I have to reciprocate as soon as possible. That’s just how I am: I have difficulty receiving.

ANONYMOUS

Since childhood, I’ve had a difficult relationship with money because of my father’s financial ruin and the creditors who hounded us.

I had to start working at a young age. I quit school at fifteen, even though I loved studying, because I didn’t want to be a burden on my family. It also had to do with “not feeling worthy.” I never told my parents the real reason; it would have humiliated them. Instead, I made up an excuse that I had lost interest in studying.

ANONYMOUS

There was a time when my father helped me a lot, not just with my children but in other ways too. Thanks to him, I got to experience a level of financial ease I couldn’t have achieved on my own. I loved being able to spend on beautiful gifts or enjoyable activities.

But my father disapproved of how I lived. One day, as a way to control me, he said, “Well then, I’ll cut off your food money.” My pride surged so strongly that, for years, I refused to take even a single dime from him. I started working seriously and never asked for anything again. It was a cold shower, but in the end, it helped me.

ANONYMOUS
summary: Описывается радостное и экспрессивное поведение сексуального E2, их стремление к финансовой независимости как к вопросу гордости, а также личные истории о ранней работе, финансовой независимости и сложностях с принятием помощи.

title: Финансовая неорганизованность и паттерны трат у сексуального E2
text:
For sexual E2s, financial resources take a backseat to emotional needs and intimate connections. They often appear indifferent to saving or accumulating wealth. This attitude may stem from a deep-seated arrogance and a need for immediate gratification. They tend to spend what they earn, often on others rather than themselves.

This lack of concern can lead to poor money management. They might not track their finances, check their bank statements, collect on loans they’ve given, or even know how much they earn.

I’m not organized with money at all. I have only a rough idea of what I earn. I don’t check my bank statements, and honestly? I’m in the red!

These days, I feel much less generous than I used to. Sometimes I stop and ask myself, “Why am I even buying this gift?” and most of the time, out of principle, I decide not to spend. But when I want to impress someone, I can be extravagant—I’ll make some grand gesture to make an impression on the person I’m interested in.

ANONYMOUS

I have a difficult relationship with money. I don’t keep track of my finances, and I don’t know how to save. If I can, I love spending on books, music, seminars, and donations to NGOs. To me, money is like water: if it flows, it gives life; if it stagnates, it becomes lifeless.

ANONYMOUS
summary: Описывается склонность сексуального E2 к финансовой беспечности, трате на других, отсутствию контроля над финансами и эмоциональной связи между деньгами и чувством жизненной энергии.

title: Деньги как инструмент любви и риск самопожертвования
text:
For sexual E2s, money is a tool to strengthen meaningful relationships—to receive affection and admiration in return. This can manifest in lavish generosity, from fulfilling their children’s every desire to giving extravagant gifts to partners and friends, making them feel special and deeply valued. However, this pursuit of admiration can push them to financial extremes, risking their own survival for a romanticized ideal of generosity that overshadows all else.

I didn’t hesitate to quit my job at the hospital and sell my home to embark on an exciting adventure—cohabiting as a throuple and working together. I felt exhilarated and passionate. But when it all fell apart, I was left without any savings and with a very young daughter. It was devastating.

But from that low point, I rebuilt my life with a new awareness and found my way back to my career as a doctor in another place.

ALBA CHARTROUX
summary: Обсуждается, как сексуальные E2 используют деньги для выражения любви и получения одобрения, часто рискуя финансовой стабильностью, Illustrated by a personal story of extreme generosity leading to ruin and subsequent recovery.

title: Financial vulnerability and fear of failure
text:
My husband and I went bankrupt working together. When our marriage ended, I had nothing—I hadn’t protected myself at all. It was incredibly hard to meet my children’s needs. Realizing that I had put them in the same deprived situation I had grown up in gave me the strength to rebuild financially.

But I’m always on the edge, and unexpected expenses send me into a panic—I’m terrified of failing again. I tend to spend beyond my means.

ANONYMOUS

Out of hunger for love, sexual E2s take more pleasure in giving and spending than in holding onto possessions. Their pride in “giving” is often a way to compensate for a sense of lack, for the painful feeling of unworthiness. This compulsion to give, to overdo, hides an underlying fear—beneath the façade of abundance lurks the image of a beggar in ruin. It is precisely this fear of downfall that can push them into excessive self-sacrifice: if they don’t feel worthy of love simply for who they are, they at least strive to earn it through what they can offer.

Afraid of failure

In relationships, where sexual E2s take on the role of the giver rather than the receiver, they struggle to imagine anyone taking care of them in times of need. Their pride allows them to demand but not to ask because rejection would be devastating. This, combined with their need for freedom and autonomy, feeds the haunting fear of failure. If they can’t give, they believe they have no place in the world. They fear being left completely alone.

I’ve always carried with me a counter-image of myself as a complete failure—destitute, alcoholic, suicidal, or something along those lines.

ALBA CHARTROUX

I, too, have lived with an imaginary counterpart—a prostitute, a beggar, a drug addict.

ANONYMOUS

As a child, I witnessed my parents’ despair at having seven children and not being able to put food on the table. The thought of ending up living under a bridge doesn’t scare me. The real nightmare is watching the people you love hit rock bottom, seeing them fail—it’s the helplessness that’s unbearable. That’s what shaped my conflicted relationship with money: I want it because it’s necessary, but at the same time, it disgusts me because not having it has made my life miserable.

ANONYMOUS
summary: This section explores the financial vulnerability and deep-seated fear of failure experienced by sexual E2s, linking their compulsive giving and spending to a hidden sense of unworthiness and a need to earn love through generosity. Personal testimonies reveal anxieties about poverty, failure, and the emotional toll of not being able to provide, rooted in childhood experiences of scarcity and helplessness.

title: Emotionality, fantasy, and compensatory imagination
text:
Emotionality and fantasy

Being precociously mature granted the child, a future sexual E2, certain privileges at the time—privileges they clung to, seeing them as proof of a secret superiority, confirmed by that extra degree of freedom they were given.

It’s not uncommon for Twos to indulge in fantasies of having a secret aristocratic background, often paired with a sense of prophetic mission: the sexual subtype envisions themselves as a prophet of love, the social subtype as a catalyst for societal change, and the self-preservation subtype as a guardian of the eternal child’s fulfillment. The E2, therefore, inhabits a vibrant world of grand, exuberant fantasies—an escape that compensates for their deep inner sense of lack.

When I struggle to stay present—in my body, in pain, in exhaustion, or frustration—I escape into fantasies. This parallel world helps me dissolve a kind of underlying anxiety.

My need to escape into imaginative states began when I had polio. I was in front of two doctors who alternated between immersing me in tubs of freezing cold and scalding hot water, trying to provoke a reaction from my unresponsive body. In those moments, all I wanted was to escape my body, to flee, because staying still like that made me feel like I was dying. So I started to imagine. I saw myself calling out to my mother, begging her to hold me in her arms.

PABLO CAÑO

It is in their compulsive fantasies that the sexual E2 builds their persona that they later embody in everyday life with countless nuances, constantly shifting and manipulating both themselves and others in their thirst for recognition and superiority. Beneath it all lies a hidden need for love, which in turn makes it impossible for them to express it authentically.

Let’s examine how the compulsion to fantasize takes root:

My father used to call me a “stupid girl with her head in the clouds.” He was right. I lived in two secret refuges: whatever novel I could get my hands on and my daydreams. While I carried out my duties as the eldest daughter in an increasingly automatic manner, I inhabited a parallel, secret world—the only one where I could feel like someone. It was filled with grand fantasies, sometimes hostile and contradictory, but ultimately compensatory for my deep sense of worthlessness. I imagined I wasn’t really my parents’ daughter but rather an orphan of noble origins. Or that I was a powerful and valuable child who would save her family. I reacted to my childhood experiences of powerlessness with fantasies of omnipotence, centered around two crucial themes: the triumph of courage and truth.

Alongside my frustration and anger, I also carried a constant concern for my mother. Despite always being pregnant, she worked tirelessly for the family, and I would watch the floors obsessively, terrified she might trip. Eventually, this anxiety morphed into fantasies of rescuing her—I, my mother’s secret musketeer—saving her from imaginary dangers and from my father’s jealous outbursts.

But more than anything, I nourished myself with fantasies of saving my siblings.

ALBA CHARTROUX

Heroic childhood fantasies are common among E2s, as this autobiographical excerpt confirms:

I have many childhood writings—freeform stories about knights rescuing princesses from terrifying dragons, and I was almost always the hero.

Later on, my relationships with women would mirror these fantasies.

LUIS HERNÁNDEZ
summary: This section examines how emotional E2s, particularly the sexual subtype, use fantasy as a compensatory mechanism for inner lack and worthlessness. It details childhood origins of imaginative escapes—such as daydreams of nobility, heroism, and rescue—and how these fantasies evolve into adult personas driven by a need for recognition and love, often masking inauthentic emotional expression.

title: Фантазии о величии и компенсация через сверхсилу
text:
While writing “The Story of My Life”, my protagonist was a queen, complete with a scepter. I titled it “Between Smiles and Rage” (experiencing both with equal intensity). I know I have this trait in a neurotic way, but I “disguise” it; one can’t always go around acting like a queen. One must be discreet, avoid unnecessary suspicions.

I also see myself as a fairy (with a magic wand, leaving behind a trail of splendor, glitter, and joy). Or a goddess. Or a superheroine… Always someone with superior powers, capable of handling immense energy—energy I use to save, to shield others from emotional struggles or, in a more pragmatic sense, from their everyday difficulties.

SONIA GOMÁ
summary: Описание фантазий о себе как о королеве, фее, богине или супергероине с особыми силами, используемых для спасения и защиты других, как проявление нейротической компенсации у E2.

title: Глубокая рана от недостатка материнской любви и её проекция
text:
This enneatype felt the withdrawal of love at an early age, perhaps even while they were still nursing at their mother’s breast, gazing into her eyes. An infinite yet unacknowledged longing for a time and place of strong maternal connection drives many of their life choices. Their unfulfilled need projects itself onto a generous self-image of someone capable of offering the very love they feel they never received enough of.

A woman of the sexual subtype recalls:

The era of free love perfectly aligned with the new self-image I built in my imagination, an image I then unconsciously molded myself into. Now that I felt like I belonged to no one, I could belong to anyone I desired. I reveled in provoking men, both sexually and intellectually. I loved theorizing about and embodying the intoxicating chaos of love without exclusivity. My favorite thinker was Georges Bataille, the philosopher of Eros and excess. I envisioned myself as a priestess of sex—an orgiastic, hallucinatory figure, capable of both igniting and taming men’s wildest erotic fantasies through seduction and mystique. This became my rebellious persona, tangled with an unconscious attempt to heal through the pleasure I gave.

Even in the relationship with my partner, I openly pursued affairs that I abandoned just as quickly. I didn’t leave a trail of “bodies” behind, but I never let things go beyond reckless indulgence.
summary: Анализ того, как ранняя депривация материнской любви приводит к бессознательному поиску компенсации через сексуальную и эмоциональную гиперэкспрессию у сексуальных E2, включая фантазии о роли жрицы любви и множественные кратковременные связи.

title: Попытки усмирить мужскую агрессию через материнскую заботу и иллюзия идеальной женщины
text:
In a completely different register from the daughter who fantasized about protecting her mother from her father, I continued, nonetheless, trying to tame “ogre-men.” Rooted in my ingrained perception of masculinity, I was determined to refine the darkest, most animalistic instincts I projected onto men—offering a subtly castrating Eros, wrapped in the maternal language of care. I had learned that men are seized by the throat. That was my lesson.

I created a hybrid dynamic that rendered men almost childlike—just as irresponsible as I was—but who admired my sexual and intellectual freedom. In my mind, I spun fantasies of being the sacred cosmic lover, offering a love vast enough to include everyone, like a Dionysian feast—bestowing joy and redemption through sex. But I failed to see that I was merely trying to mend my original wound: the deep, unmet need for my mother’s loving body, now sought in the twilight enchantment of sex.

At times, the fantasy shifted, and I saw myself as an object, consumed by male desire and power. But in that chaos, I still clung to the dream of an idealized romance with an equally idealized man. This masked an even more destructive illusion—the fantasy of being the perfect woman: someone who could accept everything from her partner, fulfill his every desire, and still remain independent, free, optimistic, and endlessly pleasing.

All these grandiose, omnipotent fantasies coexisted with an exhausting, underlying sense of inadequacy, inauthenticity, unworthiness, and fragmentation. It took me years to realize just how much I feared sinking into a consuming depression. To avoid it, I inflated myself—engaging in relationships built on a mix of shared pleasure, admiration, and caretaking—all while distorting my true needs.

ALBA CHARTROUX
summary: Описание сложной динамики у сексуальных E2: попытки контролировать агрессивные мужские импульсы через заботу, фантазии о космической любви и идеальной женщине, маскирующие глубокую боль от недостатка материнской привязанности и страх депрессии.

title: Идеализация абсолютной любви и её последствия в отношениях
text:
These kaleidoscopic erotic-emotional relationships coexist, in fact, with the idealization of a singular, absolute love—one as pure and consuming as that between a baby and their mother. The sexual E2 is capable of turning their entire life upside down in pursuit of that dream.

It’s not uncommon for them to have a long-term partner while simultaneously engaging in a series of fleeting, volatile erotic-emotional entanglements. Their self-indulgence makes this possible. However, their partner may eventually leave. When that happens, the anguish and despair become unbearable. Yet, in a desperate return to an almost primal force—akin to an instinctive aggression—they overcome the pain, ready for new, exhilarating adventures.
summary: Описание сочетания множества краткосрочных эмоционально-сексуальных связей с идеализацией единственной, абсолютной любви, сравнимой с материнско-детской привязанностью, и цикла отчаяния и восстановления после ухода партнера.

title: Проблемы сепарации от матери и формирование идентичности у E2
text:
Childhood

The gradual construction of personal identity involves recognizing oneself as distinct from others while also developing a sense of belonging that is different from fusion, where there is no distinction between self and other.

This process begins at birth, understood as a separation from fusion with the mother and the emergence of individuality. For psychological development, this separation between mother and child continues through successive developmental stages, with the earliest neonatal stages being particularly delicate and foundational to identity formation.

Based on numerous biographical accounts, it appears that those who develop a personality corresponding to Enneatype Two experience a particular difficulty in separating from their mother, which prevents them from fully developing both a sense of belonging and a clear sense of self. As a result, they continuously recreate, in their relationships, the illusion of an impossible fusion; a kind of narcissistic fascination where they do not perceive the other as a separate person but rather as a reflection of themselves. This is especially evident in sexual E2s, with their relentless pursuit of the ideal partner.
summary: Объяснение того, как трудности с отделением от матери у E2 приводят к невозможности формировать здоровую идентичность и приводят к паттерну фузии в отношениях, особенно выраженному у сексуальных E2 в поиске идеального партнера как отражения себя.

title: Динамика конкуренции и выбора сторон в семье у сексуальных E2
text: text":

title: Трухильо о происхождении гордости и потере любви
text:
I was born with the gift of love because my parents loved each other at the moment they conceived me. I received a lot of love in my childhood, and I was open to it… like the unconditional love of my grandmother A. and the strength and fierceness of my grandmother S. But then, I couldn’t believe that I could keep this gift without doing anything. I understood that I had to do a lot to earn it. I became proud so I wouldn’t lose love.

Life, with its blows, has gradually stripped me of that feeling of superiority. Falling was important, and my downfalls have always been tied to experiences of abandonment.

CONSUELO TRUJILLO
summary: Consuelo Trujillo описывает, как с детства научилась зарабатывать любовь через гордость и активность, а позже потеряла ощущение превосходства из-за повторяющихся бросков, связывая падения с опытом оставленности.

title: Персона и тень: конструкция ложного自我
text:
Persona and shadow: destructive to themselves and others

From early childhood, we begin to construct, piece by piece, the face we present to the world—the relational mask, the persona. It’s an attempt to affirm and give reality to an idealized image of ourselves, seeking acceptance or significance. But as we progressively identify with this persona, we undergo a kind of distortion, forcing ourselves into a single, rigid aspect of who we are—an artificial, inauthentic identity.

However, the traits that define this persona cannot fully exclude their opposite—the part hidden beneath the mask that we don’t know or don’t want to know about ourselves. These are the aspects of self-awareness we reject, pushing them away and projecting them onto others: the shadow. The darker, destructive side of our being, which only grows stronger the less we acknowledge it.

Recognizing that the persona is merely an incomplete aspect of ourselves, and that it doesn’t deserve to be inflated with narcissistic content, requires confronting our shadow. This means facing the other side of who we are: our limitations, deficiencies, and everything we will never be, which every frustration painfully reminds us of. That’s why integrating the persona and the shadow is a process of inner transformation that requires accepting our shortcomings, our capacity for destruction, and the discouragement of someone who, above all, is disillusioned with themselves.
summary: Объясняется концепция персоны как социальной маски и тени как отвергнутой части Я, их конфликт и необходимость интеграции через принятие своих ограничений и разрушительных сторон для внутренней трансформации.

title: E2 и борьба с тенью: нарциссизм и самообман
text:
E2s are among the enneatypes most strongly identified with a narcissistic expression of self and among those who struggle the most to recognize their shadow. What’s more, what appears in them as spontaneity, charm, and originality is actually the opposite of the rigid mask and the destructiveness of the shadow.

Narcissistic personality structures are marked by a sense of omnipotence. This is also present in enneatype Two in general, but in this subtype, it’s overshadowed by their exhibitionism. According to Kohut, “the grandiose self’s boundless exhibitionism... is its insistence on being admired,” while omnipotence is “its insistence on the exercise of total control.”

In the sexual subtype, exhibitionism is particularly destructive (not only for the E2 themselves but also for those emotionally close to them) because it poisons the very thing they care about most: emotional connection. Their hunger to be liked in order to feel loved, their desire to be intensely desired, tends to be insatiable. And in their desperate declarations of love, sexual E2s risk destroying the very thing they claim to cherish: love itself and their romantic relationships.

Let’s look at the testimony of a man of this subtype:

It’s easy to be passionate in fantasies, and just as easy to lose that passion. It’s effortless to be accepted by others when you make a show of being happy and, on the surface, generous.

Deception—something that has been a true disaster in my life—was what allowed me to survive. Letting people believe they had a rare jewel in their hands when they were with me. I have spent an enormous amount of energy, even financially, to sustain this illusion. I’ve moved countless times, changed partners and jobs, suffered irreversible losses, and damaged my health—all in a constant flight from my shadow.

I was unaware of most of my crises, nor did I realize they always coincided with feeling abandoned. These crises never lasted long; I had an extremely low tolerance for frustration. My reaction was always another deception—another woman, another sexual conquest to seduce and, if possible, dominate.

When I finally became aware of my limitations, I found myself both passionate and brutal. The line between “I can do anything” and “I can’t do anything” is incredibly thin. Suddenly, all the wounds—both physical and emotional—burst open at once.

I don’t see myself as a compulsive seducer in the usual sense, but I recognize that I have been my own victim.

ANONYMOUS
summary: Описывается, как сексуальные E2 идентифицируются с нарциссической самостью, используют эксгибиционизм и обман для поддержания иллюзии любви и власти, бегая от тени, пока не сталкиваются с разрушительными последствиями своих действий и осознанием собственной уязвимости.

title: Проекция envy и инфантилизация в отношениях у сексуальных E2
text:
Too proud to acknowledge that they receive love—or to feel that they receive enough to meet their needs—the sexual E2 secretly disqualifies the other person. This disqualification, coming from a position of superiority, stems from their deep-seated taboo around feeling envy. Instead, they easily feel envied. In a way, they project the burden of envy onto others, encouraging them to direct it toward them—an advantage that allows them to take pride in the admiration they receive.

In romantic relationships, they will subtly or overtly infantilize or absolve their partner of responsibility. Perhaps because they are unable to free themselves from that childhood craving for a blissful, all-encompassing intimacy with their mother—a craving they unconsciously attempt to recreate, inverted, within their romantic relationships. Or perhaps to cover up the vague yet persistent sense that they themselves are unreliable or even dangerous: “Si je t’aime, prends garde à toi!” (“If I love you, be on your guard!”). Or simply to assert a certain power in the relationship.
summary: Сексуальные E2, стыдясь собственной зависти, проецируют её на партнёров, одновременно infantilizing их или снимая с них ответственность, чтобы сохранить контроль и чувство превосходства, маскируя страх собственной ненадёжности и разрушительности в близости.

title: Patterns of Superiority and Vulnerability in Sexual E2
text:
If they ever feel that sense of superiority slipping, they will attack the very bond they so passionately worked to create. In the end, this person, who once seemed so warm, giving, and intense, can turn cold with hysterical indifference the moment they feel at risk of losing or being confronted with the natural limitations of emotionally challenging situations.

The more strategic they are in creating intimate relationships, the less strategic they are in areas of life that require different skills.

In short, within the polarity of persona (public image) and shadow (hidden self), this character, who appears boastful, actually hides deep shyness. They seem confident, yet secretly tremble with fear over whether their carefully crafted image will hold up—anxious that their vulnerability and insecurity might ultimately expose them.

However, it’s important to recognize that their insecurity is just as false as their confidence. They don’t simply accept their limitations; instead, they devalue themselves in a form of self-damnation: “I’m worthless… I know nothing… everyone else is better than me.” When trapped in this feeling of helplessness, they no longer know what to think, what to feel, or what they want. While stuck in this state, they may become highly dependent on others or retreat into a melancholic loneliness, feeling hopeless, abandoned.

Continuing with the persona/shadow contrast, they appear original and creative, but this is often an unnatural result of their constant effort to stand out. They seem independent, yet they are deeply dependent on the impression they make on others. They seem passionate, but inside, they are frozen or disconnected from their true emotions. They seem spontaneous, but in reality, they are highly calculated. They seem generous and caring, yet beneath that, there is an aggressive possessiveness and an unsuspected resentment—an overwhelming need for love and validation that compensates for their difficulty in truly feeling. Deep down, they feel cold, empty, and incapable of giving love, as described in the following autobiographical excerpt:

I don’t know what angel has protected me under their wings because the life I’ve lived could have easily destroyed me. It feels like I’ve experienced a strange mix of passion and detachment—emotional frenzy alternating with a kind of cold shell around my heart. As this shell formed, I could no longer reach others, nor even myself.

When I saw my siblings being mistreated or when I felt humiliated, I boiled with rage, but then that anger locked itself inside an iron shell. Beyond a certain point, I felt nothing. It was the same when I experienced both pain and the fury of abandonment. I stripped myself of emotions, pretending to have a superiority I couldn’t even recognize as false, telling myself, “I don’t need anyone.”

When I was in this state of hysterical indifference—a state I couldn’t understand at the time—I didn’t feel authentic or believable, and that only made my inner emptiness worse. Then, that feeling would dissolve, and I would once again feel both pain and joy. But the fear of expressing my need for love and support remained. I was terrified that if I started, I wouldn’t be able to stop—that I’d be swallowed by the whirlpool of my own helplessness.

Now, after the last SAT, I feel a greater awareness of my most authentic needs—and I’m finally developing the ability to ask for help.

ALBA CHARTROUX
summary: This chunk describes the psychological dynamics of sexual E2, focusing on the contrast between their confident persona and insecure shadow, including patterns of superiority, self-devaluation, emotional repression, and dependency masked as independence. It includes an autobiographical account illustrating emotional swings between passion and numbness, and a growing awareness of authentic needs.

title: Love as Meaning and Illusion in Sexual E2
text:
Love

For a sexual E2, love is what gives life meaning. They rarely find fulfillment without a grand, all-encompassing love. Their motivation is an ongoing search for romantic love, experienced with passionate intensity and chased as a way to affirm their own significance—an exceptional dream of glory that they believe they are destined to achieve.

They justify their string of relationships as a search for their soulmate (a phrase they frequently use) without realizing that this is an illusory, deeply narcissistic goal.

Their grandiose self-image is matched by an equally grand vision of their romantic partner.

As described in this example:

I longed to meet a special woman—beautiful, unique, original. I would fall in love with women, then idealize them to the point of imagining them as perfect, adorning them with qualities I invented so I could place them on a pedestal. But since they were human, not goddesses, they never stayed up there for long. Sooner or later, the enchantment faded, and I would start longing for a new, grand, and ultimate love.

But while they were still on that pedestal, I was their biggest promoter, “selling” them as the best in their field, as people of such value that the world would soon recognize it.

Yet my devotion was never total, as if deep down I sensed that none of it was truly certain or forever. I always left myself an escape route—continuing to seduce compulsively, keeping a backup plan in case things fell apart, even planting the seeds of their eventual failure. I didn’t like to show emotional commitment outside of my romantic relationships, justifying it as nonconformity when in reality, I simply didn’t want to limit the number of potential candidates for my seduction games. Even my advocacy for open relationships, despite the pain it caused me, was really about avoiding commitment. One woman alone couldn’t fill my emptiness. But neither could all the women in the world, though I didn’t understand that at the time.

LUIS HERNÁNDEZ
summary: This chunk explores how sexual E2 experiences love as a central life purpose driven by a need for significance and grandeur. It details their tendency to idealize partners, maintain escape routes, and avoid true commitment through compulsive seduction and open relationships, ultimately revealing an unfillable inner emptiness despite their efforts.

title: Relational Roots and Emotional Defense in Sexual E2
text: Since a sexual E2’s psychological defenses are rooted in emotions and feelings, they are highly relational, always moving toward others. This is amplified by their underlying attempt to heal their original wound: abandonment. As children, they had no space to express their need for attachment, care, or the pain of not receiving it.
summary: This chunk explains that the sexual E2's relational behavior stems from emotional defenses formed in childhood due to unmet attachment needs and abandonment trauma, driving their constant pursuit of connection as a way to heal early wounds.

title: Погоня за любовью как защита от отторжения
text: For this enneatype, rejection is the greatest risk of depression.They preemptively defend against it with a relentless pursuit of love, which they envision as the ultimate, timeless fulfillment of their desires. This pursuit makes them lively and active, but in reality, they are running on a treadmill, chasing a self-referential love. They don’t truly love others for who they are, but for the needs they believe they can fulfill in them, reinforcing their self-image of grandeur. Their goal is to make themselves indispensable, placing themselves at the center of their partner’s world, fantasizing about embodying the very essence of love—an object of worship, placed on a pedestal.
summary: Описывает, как сексуальный тип 2 защищается от страха отторжения через навязчивое стремление к идеализированной любви, используя отношения для укрепления своей grandiозной самоидентификации, а не из genuine интереса к партнеру.

title: Защита от падения с пьедестала: гордость и автономия
text:
But eventually, they fall from that pedestal. And when they do, they protect themselves from emotional collapse with a set of strategies. What are these strategies? Looking at their place in the Enneagram can offer some insight. Feeling excluded from love and admiration is humiliating to their self-image, which triggers their anger. But expressing that anger would force them to acknowledge their emotional dependency—an admission that would only deepen their sense of loss and make their rage more destructive: “This can’t be happening to me. Not to me!”

From this tension emerges their pride and their outward display of autonomy. Unable to tolerate a narcissistic wound, rather than confronting their desolation, they react by reclaiming power over their emotions. They turn rejection into rejection—“Let them go, they don’t deserve me”—shifting from worship to contempt. Their pride shields them from emotional devastation, allowing them to rise from the ashes, often appearing as strong, resilient, and even positive.

If they suffer, they hide it, even from those closest to them, because their proud self-image must not be tainted by pain or need. They only speak of their struggles once they’ve overcome or suppressed them, leaving others stunned (“I had no idea you were going through that”) and often impressed by their apparent strength. Ultimately, they survive pain by isolating themselves or shutting it away: what looks like a zest for life is, in reality, a desperate fear of psychological death.
summary: Объясняет, как сексуальный тип 2 реагирует на отвержение: через гордость, автономию и подавление боли, превращая зависимость в демонстрацию силы, чтобы избежать психологической смерти и сохранить образ непобедимости.

title: Жажда абсолютного удовольствия и иллюзия единства
text:
Vitality, in the sexual subtype, is expressed through both giving and experiencing pleasure in its most primal form: enjoying good food, satisfying the other person’s hunger, or overflowing with love like a full breast (love they’re always thirsty for, yet, at the same time, eager to give). They long to become one with that pleasure—both nurtured and nurturing, hunger and food, water and thirst—so they never feel deprived and never deprive those they desire. It’s no coincidence that the polarity of E2 is the possessive intensity of E8, which takes in excess and feels no obligation to give in return.

It is precisely this craving for absolute pleasure, one that overrides all reason, that makes sexual E2s intense, passionate, and romantic, ready to swear “forever” and upend their lives in an attempt to prolong their illusion of total satisfaction. In doing so, they can become overwhelmingly clingy, suffocating in their desire to be everything for the other person.

Yet this powerful drive exists within a personality structure haunted by its deepest fear: what if this source of nourishment is not truly fulfilling? No matter how reasonable or realistic that may be, sexual E2s refuse to accept it and lash out against the risk of insufficient love, projecting a false sense of superiority over their source: “I’m not the one who needs you.” They withdraw with an air of pride from the object of desire that could cause them pain or from which they have already experienced disappointment, flipping the dynamic, turning the once-adored person into the rejected one. Unable to hold onto anything, they become untouchable (the femme fatale archetype). “I don’t need you” takes the place of their overwhelming need. This is where their apparent independence, nonconformity, and exuberance come from.
summary: Исследует, как сексуальный тип 2 ищет абсолютное слияние через удовольствие и любовь как форму искупления, но отвергает реальную недостаточность связи, переходя от поклонения к презрению, чтобы сохранить иллюзию самодостаточности и избежать боли незавершенности.

title: Карен Хорни о паразитической любви и внутренней пустоте
text:
Karen Horney describes the obsessive dependency that exists within the pride system:

Erotic love lures this type as the supreme fulfillment. Love must and does appear as the ticket to paradise, where all woe ends; no more loneliness; no more feeling lost, guilty, and unworthy; no more responsibility for self; no more struggle with a harsh world for which he feels hopelessly unequipped.

Horney introduces a psychiatric concept: parasitic or oral-erotic love. The proud personality type satisfies not only their need to feel loved and special but also sees love as redemption. They crave both loving and being loved. Becoming “one” with another person would, in their eyes, allow them to achieve a wholeness they cannot find in themselves.

Because they believe they can only realize their idealized self through love, they place so much of their identity in external relationships that they are left vulnerable to insecurity, terrified of rejection and of not being accepted. This is why they are so jealous.

Both men and women in this subtype sometimes display sophistication and carefreeness, while at other times they seem inhibited and naive. They may withdraw from erotic encounters just as things become serious. And they easily throw themselves into “the most important relationship of their life” only to push it aside when they find a more exciting prospect. They are always in pursuit of the great love—which always happens to be the last one they conquered—locked in an endless cycle of “giving in order to receive.”
summary: Представляет концепцию Карен Хорни о паразитической любви у гордого типа (E2), где любовь воспринимается как путь к целостности и искуплению, но ведет к зависимости, ревности и циклу идеализации и отвержения из-за внутренней пустоты и страха собственной незавершенности.

title: Зависимость от превосходства и цикл разочарований
text:
Proud personalities can fall into morbidly dependent relations, drawn to attributes in people which they not only bitterly miss in themselves but ones for the lack of which they despise themselves:

It may be a question of independence, of self- sufficiency, of an invincible assurance of superiority, a boldness in flaunting arrogance or aggressiveness. Only these strong, superior people—as he sees them—can fulfill all his needs and take him over.
summary: Описывает, как гордый тип E2 привлекается к партнерам, обладающим качествами, которых ему самому не хватает (независимость, superiority), создавая паттерн зависимости от идеализированного 'превосходного' другого, чтобы компенсировать собственное ощущение inadequacy.

title: Цикл разочарования и избегания близости у сексуальных Э2
text: These relationships often carry an underlying frustration, as if what they truly seek is the inevitable disappointment of never receiving the complete devotion they crave. At the same time, they fear true intimacy, because if they were to achieve it, they would have to reveal their true self, including the parts of themselves they despise. So, rather than take that risk, they seek a new relationship and start the cycle all over again.
summary: Описывает, как сексуальные Э2 избегают настоящей близости из-за страха раскрытия своей истинной сущности и вместо этого стремятся к новым отношениям, повторяя цикл разочарования.

title: Реакция на отказ и агрессия маскированная под теплотой
text: The issue is that sexual E2s cannot tolerate frustration and struggle to accept “no” as an answer. Whether out of fear of emotional death or simply because they themselves don’t know how to say no honestly, they feel deeply betrayed when faced with rejection and refusal. As a result, they develop a kind of aggression disguised as warmth, winning over the other person’s favor by offering their own. But no one can ever truly satisfy them or fill their inner emptiness. When this inevitably happens, they may come to despise the person they once pursued and turn toward a new conquest, telling themselves that this time, they will finally experience true love.
summary: Сексуальные Э2 реагируют на отказ с чувством предательства, маскируя агрессию под теплотой, используя других для получения любви, но никогда не находя удовлетворения, что приводит к череде разочарований и новых поисков.

title: Фантазия о любви как религиозном экстазе и избегание обыденности
text: They cultivate the fantasy that love, both given and received, is a near-religious experience, capable of bringing them to a state of mystical ecstasy. They have an aversion to the ordinary and to small, everyday gestures of affection. They feel truly alive only in moments of grand romantic intensity or in explosive acts of rebellion because deep down, they fear feeling nothing at all. They also fear discovering the inner coldness that protects them from pain.
summary: Сексуальные Э2 ищут любовь как трансцендентный опыт, избегают простых проявлений привязанности и чувствуют себя живыми только в экстремальных эмоциональных состояниях, боясь внутренней пустоты и онемелости.

title: Групповая работа над типами любви у сексуальных Э2
text:
As a result of our meeting at the IV International Enneagram Symposium in November 2015 in Grosseto, Italy, twenty-two of us came together, all sharing the same traits and subtype. We were all sexual E2s from different countries, trying to deepen our understanding of Claudio Naranjo’s proposal—looking for a common denominator based on our personal experience of the three types of love. The goal was to distill it into a formula that could establish a hierarchical relationship between admiring love, compassionate love, and erotic love.

The group agreed on the following order of importance: first, erotic love; second, compassionate love; and lastly, admiring love.
summary: Описание встречи группы сексуальных Э2 на симпозиуме Эннеаграммы в 2015 году, где они определили иерархию видов любви: эротическая — первая, сострадательная — вторая, восхищающаяся — третья по значимости.

title: Транзакционная природа любви у сексуальных Э2
text:
The love of a sexual E2 tends to involve using the other person, both through eroticism and compassion. They use others to obtain something they desire for themselves.

Even within erotic love itself, there’s a transactional nature, a falsification of true love. It becomes a “giving in order to receive” dynamic—a kind of prostitution of love, an exchange. There’s an underlying demand to be loved, needed, and seen.

A person with this character type confuses feeling loved with being physically desired. One of their worst nightmares is not being physically desired.

They perceive eroticism as a weapon, a tool of power. They mistake the idealized projection of eroticism for an actual connection with their deeper erotic essence. For them, eroticism often represents an ideal more than the reality of an encounter with another person.

The urge to meet the other person’s needs in order to be loved means they don’t truly see them. They’re not attuned to that person’s desire, nor to their own deep desire.
summary: Сексуальные Э2 относятся к любви как к обмену: используют эротику и сострадание для удовлетворения собственных потребностей, путают чувство желания с любовью, видят в эротике инструмент власти и идеализируют её, не видя реального партнера.

title: Манипулятивное использование сострадательной любви
text:
Sexual E2s also manipulate compassionate love. Let’s take a closer look:

The unconditional love I believed I received turned, within me, into a kind of net used to trap those who interested me. That generous love was always, in truth, a “love in exchange for…” It was never about helping the other person; I was satisfying my own desire to give. Sometimes in an invasive way; other times, in ways that degraded me; and almost always manipulatively and unconsciously.

At times, I thought I was escaping my own inner pain by seeking pleasure, but it was more about manipulating the other person. I don’t know when I developed an internal radar for detecting what others need. Even that radar is tainted by the false certainty that I know what they need. But somehow, for years, my instinct was dedicated to this—gaining their attention and affection.
summary: Сексуальные Э2 используют сострадательную любовь как средство контроля и получения внимания, маскируя свои потребности под заботой, не осознавая манипулятивного характера своих действий.

title: Путь к восхищающей любви через признание собственной боли
text:
ÁNGEL SAAVEDRA

Transformation happens when the love that is most distant from a sexual E2’s awareness—admiring love—is worked on.

But to reach admiring love, they must first experience compassion: they need to connect with their own lack, their own absence of love. Only when they acknowledge their emptiness and incompleteness can they feel their need—and from there, truly see the other person and recognize that same need in them. If they allow themselves to feel their own suffering, they can perceive the suffering of others—and in this way, open themselves to compassion.

At that point, they can experience true person-to-person connection, seeing others as equals. From there, they can open themselves to devotional love. To connect with admiring love, they need to feel the pain of having lacked love and the inability to trust in a stable authority figure they could admire.

As a child, I was abandoned by both my mother and father. The first time I tried ayahuasca, I had a vision that told me, “I am your true mother.” That was when I developed deep admiring love for the Divine Mother, a mother I could trust. She wouldn’t betray me, abandon me, or manipulate me. What I lack for devotional love is the ability to trust in surrendering. I need to trust in order to truly let go because I am afraid. Afraid that something might happen to me, because I feel a bit naïve.

LUCIANA VIEIRA
summary: Для развития восхищающей любви сексуальным Э2 необходимо сначала признать свою внутреннюю пустоту и боль, пережить сострадание к себе и другим, что позволяет увидеть людей как равных и открыться доверию к высшему или достойному объекту восхищения.

title: Самооценка и кризисы как путь к состраданию и восхищению
text:
Developing a true sense of self-worth is essential—having compassion for oneself. Recognizing where one stands, their place, and their value, whatever it may be, is the foundation for valuing others.

For sexual E2s, illness and life’s uncertainties have often served as doorways into both admiring love and compassion.

As one woman shared:
summary: Развитие истинной самооценки и сострадания к себе является основой для сексуальных Э2 чтобы ценить других; болезнь и жизненные кризисы могут открыть доступ к сострадательной и восхищающей любви.

title: Admiring love through illness and vulnerability
text:
Admiring love came to me through illness—through feeling such great need, fear, pain, and lack. From there, I could truly feel others and connect with my need for God. Feeling so small, so vulnerable, not knowing if I would live or die—that’s when my bond with the divine opened up. After impermanence, it’s the only thing that remains.

CONSUELO TRUJILLO

Parenthood can also serve as a gateway to compassionate love:

I felt that when I had nothing left to give, I somehow still had more to give. Seeing the need of this tiny, defenseless, sensitive being connected me with my own fragility and my own world of needs. My child showed me the emotional path to compassion—the ability to put myself in his place.

ÁNGEL SAAVEDRA
summary: This chunk describes how sexual E2s can develop admiring love through experiences of illness, vulnerability, and parenthood, where confronting personal lack and fragility opens the path to compassion and connection with the divine or others.

title: Overcoming envy and distorted self-worth in sexual E2s
text:
Another doorway into admiring love is first admiring the divine, and from there, learning to admire the human. Sexual E2s struggle to experience admiring love here on Earth, among the people in their lives. To feel admiration for another person, they must first recognize their own lack, which inevitably leads them to acknowledge their envy, a feeling they have always suppressed. Envy is the great taboo they have spent their lives avoiding through their strategies of superiority.

Recognizing their own envy, then, is another gateway to transformation: realizing you have something that I don’t. This allows them to admire the other person, value them, and learn from them. Their arrogant denial of envy has cost them countless opportunities for learning and nourishment.

Due to their low self-esteem, sexual E2s hold a distorted belief that “If I value and admire you, then I am worthless; I don’t exist.” This is why it’s so crucial for them to find an authentic sense of self-worth, rooted in their own inner strength.

At the symposium, there were discussions about experiences with plant medicine as a way to break through the inability to truly see others—to be able to see them as they are and to see oneself as one truly is.

The transformational process of the sexual E2 shifts the quality of all three types of love, moving them toward more authentic and less manipulative expressions. As a result, admiring love becomes less distant.

In summary, this character evolves by starting from eroticism and, through the experience of lack, integrating compassion—thus encountering the other person in their real need, rather than the fantasy they create about them or themselves. Only by accepting their own lack can they accept what is and develop authentic admiration and devotion—though, for them, devotion comes more easily toward the divine than toward the human.
summary: This chunk explains how sexual E2s can transform by confronting suppressed envy and low self-worth, learning to admire others through recognizing their own lack, and how plant medicine and self-worth development support a shift from manipulative to authentic expressions of love.

title: Mata Hari as an embodiment of the sexual E2 archetype
text:
Historical figures: Mata Hari and Isadora Duncan

Mata Hari

by Toni Aguilar

The story of Mata Hari—or rather, the legend embodied by Margaretha Geertruida “Griet” Zelle, a Dutch woman born in Leeuwarden on August 7, 1876—perfectly captures the essence of the femme fatale, an archetype deeply tied to the sexual E2. This queen of seduction became the mesmerizing face of the Belle Époque, a symbol of liberated sexuality and pleasure. In many ways, she personified the wild, feline, and capricious woman, capable of captivating large audiences (especially men) with her sacred Eastern dances and an undeniable ability to attract and enchant.

But when the more sober and puritanical era of the Great War arrived, the very qualities that had once brought her adoration and fame across Paris—and made her a celebrated dancer and high-society courtesan throughout Europe—sealed her tragic fate. Caught in a web of slander and intrigue, she was accused of being a double agent spying for Germany. Found guilty despite a lack of conclusive evidence, she was executed by a French firing squad in Vincennes, near Paris, on October 15, 1917.

As Pat Shipman writes in the preface to her biography:

The most important thing to know about Margaretha Zelle is that she loved men. The most crucial thing to know about her is that she did not love truth. When it was convenient, she told the truth. When it was not, or when she found the truth tedious, she invented what might be kindly called “alternative truths”—and unkindly, “lies.” For her, what was factually true never seemed as essential as what should have been true. By the time she had transformed herself into Mata Hari, she was highly skilled at fashioning the world to her liking.

Her childhood and life were profoundly shaped by her relationship with her father, a key factor in the development of her proud, seductive nature and her instinctive pull toward charm and allure.

Seduction, for her, was a promise of devotion and pleasure—something she radiated effortlessly. It was the art of manipulating love, a game where she demanded everything in return yet never fully surrendered her heart. She turned men into puppets, making them dance to her tune. A dangerous vamp who extracted from them everything she desired—desire itself, favors, fortunes. “Seduction” is the defining trait of the sexual subtype of Enneatype 2, and the word that best encapsulates the life of this courtesan and dancer.

Her father, Adam Zelle, was a hat manufacturer whom neighbors nicknamed “The Baron” for his grandiose dreams and his talent for “building castles in the air.” From an early age, he taught Margaretha to believe she was special, blessed with a unique charm and an almost magical allure. She became accustomed to being the center of attention, to receiving praise and admiration. The proud and seductive persona (sexual E2) of Mata Hari was already taking shape in her earliest years.
summary: This chunk presents Mata Hari as a historical example of the sexual E2 archetype, highlighting her seductive nature, manipulative relationships, truth distortion, and the paternal influences that shaped her proud, attention-seeking persona and lifelong pattern of using charm to gain control and validation.

title: Отношения с отцом и формирование личности
text: She was her father’s little princess, and the Baron loved to show her off. The kind of affection he gave her made her feel endlessly precious, as if she were the most extraordinary creature in the world. She was the apple of his eye, and not even the birth of her siblings ever displaced her from that role. She may have even believed that he loved her more than he loved her mother. In that deeply Oedipal relationship, the intimacy Margaretha shared with her father was not the kind typically expected between a child and a parent. She essentially replaced her mother in his affections, a dynamic that would shape her future relationships with men, power, and society at large.
summary: Описывает глубокие эдиповые отношения Маргариты с отцом, который баловал её и вызывал у неё ощущение исключительности, что сформировало её гордую, соблазнительную природу и повлияло на её будущие отношения с мужчинами.

title: Воспитание, роскошь и гордость
text:
Despite their modest means, her father enrolled her in the most expensive school in town. On her first day, he sent her in a gilded carriage pulled by two white goats, as if they were royal steeds.

Even after he went bankrupt, he left her with a love for luxury and an insatiable desire to shine—traits that, years later, classmates would remember as the most striking things about Margaretha.

Her proud, self-inflated, and haughty personality was shaped by the sense of personal importance and superiority that her father instilled in her throughout her life.

He bought her wonderful dresses in vivid, flamboyant colors—once a dress of scarlet velvet that she wore to school. She twirled to show her father how the skirt flared out, and he beamed and told her she was beautiful. She did the same for her friends at Miss Buys’s exclusive school, and they looked at her with wide eyes. They pretended to be shocked, to think it was a scandalous dress for a girl her age, but she knew they were only jealous. They were better suited to the subdued colors they habitually wore. They could have afforded a dress like hers easily, but they never could have worn such a garment with her flair. Their pallid skin and colorless hair and lack of personality condemned them. Only someone like her, with thick, darkly waving hair, compelling eyes, and café au lait skin— only someone whose very essence cried “Look at me!”—could get away with it.
summary: Рассказывает о том, как отец, несмотря на бедность, обеспечивал Маргарите роскошное воспитание, прививая ей любовь к splendour и чувство собственного превосходства, что проявлялось в её одежде, поведении и отношении к сверстникам.

title: Эмоциональные травмы и поиск внимания
text:
The bond she formed with her father shaped a compulsive drive for applause, recognition, and passion that would define her life. The public worshipped her, especially men, who found themselves mesmerized at her feet.

By the age of thirteen, she was a vain, self-centered girl used to having her father indulge her every whim, making life feel magical, effortless, and fun. But his business ventures kept failing, until he was finally forced to declare bankruptcy. Mr. Zelle left for The Hague in search of work, abandoning his family in a small, shabby apartment with little money to survive. This must have been Margaretha’s first real taste of abandonment. Ten months later, he returned, but tensions with his wife had reached a breaking point. After a dramatic separation, her mother passed away. Margaretha experienced a second abandonment when, instead of going to live with her father, she was sent to stay with relatives, who enrolled her in a school in Leiden—where, not long after, a sexual scandal took place.
summary: Описывает, как сильная эмоциональная привязанность к отцу привела к потребности в постоянном восхищении, а последующие бросания — отцом и матерью — стали травмой, которая определила её późнейшую зависимость от мужского внимания.

title: Пробуждение сексуальной силы и первая победа
text:
At sixteen, Margaretha was a bright student—intensely seductive and strikingly beautiful. She became sexually involved with the headmaster of the institution, Wybrandus Haanstra, a 51-year-old man of status and reputation. Despite being married, he fell hopelessly in love with her. It seemed to be one of the first true triumphs in the art of seduction for the young Margaretha—a moment when she realized her power to attract and stir desire. But in the end, she was the one blamed. Accused of immorality and causing a scandal, she was expelled in disgrace and sent home, while Haanstra suffered no real consequences—his respected position and reputation remained intact. Today, his actions would be recognized as sexual abuse of a minor, but in 1893, Margaretha was the one deemed immoral and guilty.

She quickly discovered that pleasing a man was a way to gain power and the ability to control him at will. The early lesson she learned from the erotic charge present in her relationship with her father gradually transformed into a seductive ability, serving a self-interested sexuality. She became an expert at awakening desire in others, weaving a web-like strategy in which her suitors—or rather, her victims—fell, becoming entangled in her disturbing games of love. They lost their will, allowing her to live off their favors and fortunes. She was a woman of expensive tastes, indulging in luxury hotels, fashionable clothing, fine dining… everything paid for in exchange for her prized love. In essence, she lived as a high-class courtesan.
summary: Описывает ранний сексуальный опыт Маргариты с главой школы, её осознание силы соблазна, последующее обвинение и изгнание, а также то, как она начала использовать свою сексуальность как инструмент власти и контроля над мужчинами, живя на их содержании.

title: Психология и защита Энеатипа 2
text:
Was she aware that she was trying to recreate the magic of her father’s love from childhood? Most likely not. The defense mechanism of the Enneatype 2 structure is repression—the suppression of anything that does not align with an exalted self-image, one that is magnificent and radiant, where the word “dependence” is completely absent. She would probably never have admitted to being dependent on men; rather, she used them, provoking their surrender and making them dependent on her.

The pain of being abandoned by her beloved father turned into a longing that fueled her relentless pursuit of male attention—a pursuit she overvalued, perhaps for a lifetime.

Beneath the surface of her romantic relationships lay a false sense of surrender. Every man loved her, every man desired her, and some had the pleasure of sharing her most intimate moments, yet she kept her heart tightly sealed.
summary: Анализирует психологические механизмы поведения Маргариты через призму Энеатипа 2: подавление зависимости, иллюзия самообеспеченности, использование мужчин для поддержания грандиозного самообраза и скрытая эмоциональная изолированность malgré внешней страстности.

title: Склонность к военным и поиск новой любви
text: She had a particular weakness for uniforms, especially those of officers. When she came across a matrimonial advertisement in the newspaper Nieuws van de Dag from a Dutch East Indies officer on leave, Captain Rudolf MacLeod, twenty years her senior, she responded.
summary: Коротко отмечает склонность Маргариты к мужчинам в форме, особенно офицерам, и её реакцию на matrimonial advertisement от Captain Rudolf MacLeod, что предвещает новый этап в её жизни.

title: Импульсивность и самооправдание в отношениях
text: From their very first date, Margaretha signed her letters as: “Your future wife, who already loves you.” This was the prototype of the impulsivity characteristic of the sexual subtype of E2—when they desire something, they mask their true motivation with the best of intentions. Naturally, she justified it with heartfelt and passionate reasoning, even hiding from herself the interests that tied her to an exotic, secure, and adventurous future. In the name of love and passion, and guided by her own contradictions, she embarked on a new life in Java that soon ended in failure.
summary: Описывает поведение Маргариты Зель в начале брака с МакЛеодом как проявление импульсивности сексуального субтипа E2, где истинные мотивы маскируются под благими намерениями и любовными чувствами, приводя к несчастливому браку в Java.

title: Разочарование в браке и признания о темпераменте
text:
After the honeymoon, the deterioration of their relationship became evident. Griet described it in several letters: “Well, [the marriage] did alter, from the moment that there was no more money…. I had not married to go without luxury and…I was flirtatious and he did not like that. He was jealous.”

And in another:

He was so much older than I am…. He could have been almost my father. And then, a woman with my temperament…. I want to confess truly and openly, that seeing a handsome young man made my heart start to beat quicker. And that is very natural, that is something that one can’t help…. I was very temperamental. I had also artistic aspirations…. I [had] inclinations that made it impossible for a woman like me to be a good housewife…. I was not like that [content at home], I confess frankly; I wanted to live like a colorful butterfly in the sun, rather than in the calmness of the inside of my room.
summary: Содержит выдержки из писем Грет, где она откровенно рассказывает о разочаровании в браке из-за отсутствия роскоши и ревности мужа, а также о своем темпераменте, художественных наклонностях и невозможности быть домохозяйкой, стремясь к яркой, свободной жизни.

title: Трагедия и перерождение: от утраты к новой идентичности
text:
