summary: Автор описывает глубокий эмоциональный конфликт с матерью, вызванный её неодобрением её сексуальности и жизненных выборов, что привело к чувству стыда, самоизоляции и хроническому внутреннему боли, несмотря на попытки скрыть правду и угодить ожиданиям семьи.

title: Бегство от боли и театральное самовыражение
text:
I didn’t talk to anyone about this, not even to myself, which led me to reckless and self-destructive behaviors. To my friends, I always spoke highly of my parents and siblings, painting the image of an ideal family. I didn’t admit, not to myself nor to anyone else, that I had problems with them that caused me pain. I ran from that pain because acknowledging it would have forced me to confront a void I couldn’t bear. I had to pull away, far away, before I could even begin to question my childhood and my relationship with my family.

I started making a living from my profession; I worked in a theater company, I was an actress, I was living my dream. This was my life. During that time, I learned a lot about the ins and outs of theater: production, distribution, stage management, assembling and dismantling sets, loading and unloading vans… everything that goes into staging a performance. I was on tour with one play while already rehearsing the next. Experiencing theater from every angle gave me structure, knowledge, and strength to turn it into a true calling and fight for it, despite the obstacles, the lack of support, resources, or money. I learned to push projects forward by working extremely hard, and earning a living from it gave me a lot of strength. This could have gone on indefinitely, but there always comes a moment in my life when, without fully understanding why, I feel an impulse that drives me to break away from what I have in pursuit of something greater, something unknown. I feel a Calling, and I follow it because I can’t not follow it. It happened when I left my hometown for Seville to go to university; when I left the dormitory; later, when I went against my father’s wishes to dedicate myself to theater. And now, I felt I had to leave Seville—the company I worked for, the boyfriend I had at the time who loved and cared for me, everything I had built there, my friends, my home... And I did. I wasn’t happy playing my roles. I felt like something was missing, I felt artificial, inauthentic.
summary: Автор описывает бегство от эмоциональной боли через отрицание и идеализацию семьи, а также глубокую вовлечённость в театральную профессию, которая стала источником силы и призвания, но в конце концов оставила ощущение фальши и внутреннего зовa к переменам.

title: Путь к самопознанию в Буэнос-Айресе
text:
I met Carlos Gandolfo at an acting seminar; his work captivated me, and I decided to apply for a scholarship and travel to Buenos Aires to study at his school. Later, I understood that this was the driving force, but that, deep down, my soul held many other reasons. Here, I can say that a journey began—one with no return—the journey of distancing myself in order to find myself. There’s something within me that makes me follow certain impulses when I feel them strongly; I don’t stop to analyze them—I simply trust that intuition and let it guide me without second-guessing.

I was twenty-seven when I arrived in Buenos Aires. There, I began to discover the kind of actress I wanted to be and the kind of theater I wanted to create. I traveled across South America, and my eyes were opened to the power of its vast nature and its people. I fell in love with a woman, and I allowed myself to name what I was feeling, to be loved in return, and not to hide it from others. The relationship was passionate and possessive—I suffered through love and suffered at the thought of losing it. But at the same time, I started psychoanalytic therapy and began working through my relationship with my parents, revisiting my childhood, and finally allowing myself to feel the pain and anger of the little girl who had never been allowed to feel them. There, I was able to start questioning the idea I had of my “happy life.”

I made many friends in Buenos Aires, immersing myself fully in everything the city had to offer—countless acting classes, bodywork training, voice work, so much theater. I dove deep into exploring my artistic expression. That’s where I met Juan Carlos Corazza; we became friends, and an artistic relationship began that would later have a significant influence on my personal and professional life in Spain.
summary: В Буэнос-Айресе автор начинает глубокий процесс самопознания через терапию, открытые отношения с женщиной и полное погружение в teatralное искусство, что позволяет ей confront и переосмыслить подавленные эмоции детства и пересмотреть свою жизнь как конструкцию, требующую аутентичности.

title: Passionate love and romantic idealism
text: Moving in with the woman I had fallen in love with rekindled my passion for intimacy. I experience love in a very physical way, yet also with a touch of romanticism. I was convinced that what I felt was the most special thing in the world—that this love story was unique. It was my life, but at the same time, it was a novel, and I was the heroine. I truly believed my way of loving was powerful, authentic, and all-consuming—I wanted to be a great lover, and at this point, love had become the center of my life.
summary: The narrator describes an intense, idealized romantic relationship in which love becomes all-consuming and central to identity, blending physical passion with a sense of being the heroine of a unique love story.

title: Return to Spain and cultural reawakening
text:
I ran out of money and decided to return to Spain to figure out my future. Leaving behind my love, my friends, my life there—it was incredibly difficult, but I felt it was time to go back. Suddenly, in those moments when I could have lost everything for passion, something always pulled me back down to earth—a sense of reason, the weight of reality jolting me awake.

Things were dire in Buenos Aires, but in Spain, by the late ‘80s, doors were opening for people. Culture and the arts were flourishing, creativity was everywhere, and hope filled the streets and nights. It was a golden era. I felt I needed to be in my country at that moment, to be part of this resurgence of freedom. I returned, afraid. I had changed so much that I felt distant from my friends, my family, and my old life in Spain. I thought that the person I had become wouldn’t be accepted. In Buenos Aires, some of my masks had begun to fall away. What I had once believed so fiercely, I no longer believed as much. The “Consuelo from Seville” was under scrutiny—some veils had been lifted. Now, it was clear that I loved a woman, that I wanted to experience acting differently, that I didn’t want to go back to how things were. I wanted to bring back what I had learned and discovered in Buenos Aires. In short, I now wanted to change others.
summary: After returning to Spain during a cultural renaissance, the narrator grapples with fear of rejection, recognizes personal transformation, and feels compelled to share her newfound insights with others, marking a shift from personal growth to a desire to influence those around her.

title: Savior complex and interpersonal patterns
text: This is also a recurring theme in my life—a leitmotif. I discover something that changes me, that makes me grow and fills me with passion, and I want everyone around me to experience it too. In doing so, I stop seeing or acknowledging the other person for who they are. This has happened with my partners, my siblings, my parents, my friends, my students... Believing I have the power to help, to solve other people’s problems and suffering, comes from a well-intentioned sense of superiority, from a savior complex. There’s a genuine desire to help, but also an inability to tolerate someone else’s struggle without offering solutions—a difficulty in simply being present without trying to intervene. Coming to terms with this has taken years, many blows, and a long inner journey.
summary: The narrator identifies a lifelong pattern of wanting others to share her transformative experiences, rooted in a savior complex that overrides genuine presence and stems from a need to feel superior while masking a deep desire for acceptance.

title: Emotional impulsivity and somatic manifestations
text:
So, I finally landed in Barajas. By then, I was already an Indian, and there were my soul friends: la Jose, Manolo, and Mati, fully embracing the ‘80s style. Afraid of their rejection and judgment, I gathered my strength and faced them, showing them everything I had become and expressing all my criticisms of their way of understanding life and theater. I’d call it spiritual superiority—just like when, as a child, I felt above my parents and siblings, above the people in my town, while deep down, I was overwhelmed by a desperate need to be accepted and loved. My friends had so much patience with me, and they showed me so much loyalty!

At that time, I didn’t know how to deal with my fear—I didn’t recognize it, and I reacted compulsively and counterphobically. But my body took the hit: I would get sick, run a fever, have muscle pain, tremors, chills, breakouts, diarrhea… That was how I felt my limits. So, I told my boyfriend I had fallen in love with a woman, I told all my friends, I arranged for her to come from Buenos Aires, I took her to my family’s home. Just like that—all at once, without a process, without thinking it through. Pure impulse, pure emotion. That was me.

The most important thing was what I felt. I couldn’t see the other person, couldn’t feel the pain I was causing this man who had been waiting for me. At that moment, I bulldozed everything that stood in the way of what I wanted to live. Me and my life. Me and what I wanted in that instant. But above all, me and my passionate love story.
summary: Upon reuniting with old friends, the narrator expresses spiritual superiority rooted in childhood patterns, acts on fear through impulsive emotional outbursts and somatic symptoms, and prioritizes her own feelings and desires over others’ well-being, revealing a counterphobic, all-or-nothing approach to love and self-expression.

title: Sacrifice, false abundance, and abandonment of self
text:
I was offered a job in production and organization at the Andalusian Theater Center in Seville, and I took it. I landed a good job, a position of power, money, and in no time, I was able to bring my partner to live with me in Spain. I distanced myself from acting—the very reason I had spent years studying in Buenos Aires. I neglected myself, forgot my deepest desire, focused on her and on status. My abandonment of my ideals was justified: I had to take care of her. She needed security; she communicated that to me at every moment—or at least, I believed that’s what she needed. I even convinced a friend of mine to marry her so she could get nationality papers and work in Spain. Once again, that compulsive need to give in order to be loved took over. To give myself materially, physically, emotionally. Because deep down, I was terrified she would leave me. And so, I abandoned my essential self, my center, my creativity—the inner child who had been with me my entire life until then. In the background, lurking in the shadows, was the woman who didn’t feel worthy of being loved as she was, with her fragility, her incompleteness, her fear. And the crazy thought: “If I have nothing to give, they won’t love me.” That was how false abundance played out in me.

This crazy idea shaped my life, bringing illness and suffering—to me and to those who truly loved me. And that shadow figure, the woman who didn’t feel worthy of being loved simply for existing, had been struggling to come into the light for my entire life. Even now, there are days when I realize I’m not facing her because my stomach hurts, or I’m exhausted, or I feel depressed, and the tears come at night as I drive home alone.
summary: The narrator sacrifices her artistic identity and self-worth to secure her partner’s love through material and emotional giving, driven by a core belief that she is unworthy of love as she is, leading to self-abandonment, illness, and a cycle of false abundance rooted in insecurity.

title: Разрыв и духовный поиск
text:
And then, just when I thought I had given her everything, she left me. She abandoned me for another woman. That year was the most devastating and sorrowful of my life. I was thirty years old and wanted to die. I was twenty when I went through my first great love crisis. With loss and betrayal, my entire life collapsed. I got sick, lost weight, couldn’t find the strength to get out of bed… I felt lost and desperately needed to find meaning.

I left Seville—the job, the house, the friends—and moved to Madrid. I needed to find myself, feverishly. I wasn’t happy; I was miserable. The angel had fallen from paradise. I plunged into the dark pit that, for me at that moment, was the experience of being human—vulnerable, weak, in pain. A great tower of pride came crashing down. How could she leave me, after everything? After how much I had loved her? I couldn’t believe it and took a long time to accept it. My pride kept raging, trying to rear its head again with the thought She’ll come back. But she never did. Years would have to pass before I became more aware of the traps of my love—how what I called love had actually distanced me from love.

This time of solitude, inner drought, and lovelessness felt like my adolescence—isolated and alone in my world. And once again, that yearning for God, for a spiritual search, surfaced. This time, I channeled it through yoga and began meditating. The rage and resentment were buried deep. I had an encounter with her and her new girlfriend—the crazy part was that I tried to get close to them. I’m so good, so exceptional, I can handle a situation like this… But my shadow remained hidden. It would emerge later, during another encounter, when I slapped her in public. I felt immense violence in my powerlessness to bring her back to me.
summary: Описание глубокого эмоционального кризиса после расставания, включая депрессию, потерю смысла, переезд в Мадрид, попытки духовного поиска через йогу и медитацию, а также вспышки гнева и насилия, связанные с неосознанной тенью.

title: Терапия и постепенное исцеление
text: I was deeply depressed; my own sadness terrified me, so I returned to psychoanalysis. I started realizing how blind love could be. I had lived under the illusion of this great love—mine, the best one, the one I had always sought and longed for. And in doing so, I had never truly seen the person in front of me. I hadn’t noticed her shortcomings or her needs. Therapy grounded me, cleared my mind, strengthened me. Sweeping away the cobwebs spun by my overwhelming emotions had always been good for me—clarity made me stronger, reconnecting me with joy, with a desire to live, with my artistic calling. At night, I still searched—compulsively—for encounters with women who would make me feel desired, make me seduce and conquer. But something had shifted. It didn’t satisfy me. It didn’t make me happy. The emptiness of love was still there, but little by little, my wound was healing—thanks to the balm of love for life, for art, for the pursuit of meaning.
summary: Процесс психоанализа, ослепленность иллюзией любви, осознание собственной слепоты к партнеру, постепенное исцеление через терапию и переориентация на внутренние источники смысла: искусство, жизнь и поиск.

title: Возвращение к искусству и новая любовь
text:
Juan Carlos Corazza came from Buenos Aires, and together, we created a theater project. After that, I continued training as an actress at his studio. My life seemed to find direction again. I could keep growing, keep learning, and that gave me confidence. I regained a bit of faith in myself, in my relationships with others. I went back to doing what I loved most in the world—acting, making theater. And it redeemed me. It renewed me. I entered a new stage of life. I felt stronger inside. The pain had softened me, and I was reconnecting with my inner child. I wanted to live again. Hope was coming back.

In the summer of 1991, I had no job, no money, no love—but I was starting to find my rhythm in life again. Then, I got a job offer in Seville. Once again, I could make a living as an actress. Theater wanted me back. What followed were two years of touring all over Spain, performing in two plays by Federico García Lorca. The roles—especially Adela in The House of Bernarda Alba—gave me the chance to grow immensely as an actress.
summary: Возвращение к актерскому искусству через сотрудничество с Хуаном Карлосом Коррассой, восстановление уверенности и творческого призвания, работа в театре, гастроли по Испании и рост как актрисы через роли в пьесах Лорки.

title: Начало отношений с Сузи и уроки любви
text:
In September, I started rehearsals and fell madly in love with Susi. And so began the most important relationship of my life. Every obstacle Susi placed in my way was a precious gift, striking my pride with a devastating but beneficial effect. She didn’t trust me easily, so she wouldn’t give herself to me until I had passed all the tests that a sexual Five puts their partner through before surrendering. I had to fight and, above all, be honest and open with her—love her while accepting both my limits and hers. Her heart slowly began to open, and I started to appreciate what wasn’t ideal or wonderful but simply human and imperfect, yet kind. The fog of false tenderness cleared away, allowing me to step into the thorns of everyday love—love rooted in actions, faithfulness, and perseverance.

The journey of this relationship will unfold over the course of this autobiography, but at this point, I can say that this was the beginning of both a love story and a story of pain. By Susi’s side, I experienced my maturity as a woman and had to face many of my shadows—the ones hardest to see because they were decorated with good intentions.
summary: Начало глубоких и трансформирующих отношений с Сузи, которая, как сексуальная Пятерка, ставит испытания перед intimностью; отношения становятся путем к зрелости, честности и встрече с тенью, маскирующейся под добрые намерения.

title: Преодоление иллюзий любви и столкновение со своей тенью
text: The biggest obstacle was always believing that I stood on the side of love. And how do you question someone who is on the side of love? How do you enter into crisis? That’s why my greatest falls were always tied to romantic failures. The only thing that truly made me question myself was the loss of love—the frustration of feeling that the person I loved didn’t feel loved by me, that they confronted me in the way I loved. With Susi, seduction was never enough. Nor was my ability to envelop her in intensity, passion, ecstasy, or grand displays of good intentions. My theatrical expressions of love didn’t win her over either. She always challenged my falseness, always looked at my excessive affection and physical closeness with suspicion, always saw through the performance of my love, even in our intimacy. This was deeply painful for me because I didn’t want to see my shadow, my manipulation, my power struggles, or my contempt toward her—even though I loved her as deeply as I always had, but in such a neurotic way. I wanted to keep feeding that image of ideal, romantic, generous, and sinless love… but she, distrustful of my exaggerated displays, scrutinized me and never played along with my seductive game. Susi’s stance toward me was often confrontational and painful, but I always felt her love. She gave me the opportunity to see my own shadow—my selfishness, my struggle with compassion, and my difficulty in truly admiring another. For a long time, I saw myself as the important one in our relationship, the one who deserved to be served. Acknowledging this part of myself was harsh and painful, but also liberating. It came hand in hand with shedding my seductive image and daring to be loved for who I truly was—opening my heart to compassion for my smallness and that of others. And in doing so, I could finally admire Susi—her greatness, her talent, her qualities—and allow myself to be small before her. I could enjoy the feeling of admiring the person I loved, recognizing that she was better than me in so many ways, and understanding that this didn’t make me unworthy but rather fortunate.
summary: Автор описывает, как её вера в собственную правоту в любви привела к конфликтам, и как отношения с Сусой раскрыли её манипулятивные тенденции, потребность в восхищении и невозможность принять любовь без игры, пока она не научилась видеть свою тень и ценить партнёрку как равную.

title: Путь к самопознанию через терапию и работу с Энеаграммой
text: Returning to the thread of the story, through Susi, I met Claudio Naranjo, and together we began our work with the Enneagram. Around the same time, I started my Gestalt therapy process. I dove deeper into myself, into discovering who I was, into recognizing myself, stripping away the mask, the seductive costume, the overabundance, and the illusion of omnipotence. I got to know my shadow, which so far had been strange and alien to me. I embarked on the hardest yet sweetest path: the fall from paradise—the fall from who I was, or rather, who I had wanted to be until then. I had to lose myself completely, exhaust all the roles I had known, until I finally met my essential self—my soul.
summary: После встречи с Клаудио Нараньо и начала работы с Энеаграммой, а также гештальт-терапии, автор начинает глубокий процесс снятия маски, признания своей тени и возвращения к подлинному я, описывая это как трудный, но необходимый путь от иллюзии omnipotence к самопознанию.

title: Профессиональное укоренение и переход от самовыражения к служению другим
text: In 1994, Juan Carlos Corazza invited me to collaborate at his acting school, teaching performance classes. It was an incredible opportunity for me at that time, as it meant professional recognition, financial stability, and the chance to be part of a project I believed in that would allow me to grow. But it was also difficult because it meant making a choice—losing that sense of freedom I had always sought in my life, that feeling that I could leave at any moment, go anywhere, and do whatever I pleased. I finally set foot on solid ground: I was thirty-four years old, and for too long, I had lived without knowing how I would make it to the end of the month. At that time, the weight of our household’s finances fell mostly on Susi. I needed more stability—to put down roots, to commit to life, to the day-to-day, to the small things, to the people around me, to my partner, to our home. So I started working every day on a fixed schedule, and in doing so, I stopped being an aspiring great actress and became just another worker. I committed myself to the school, to my students, to pedagogy—helping others act and develop their gifts. Suddenly, my work was no longer centered on myself but on others. My artistic training and my university studies in education finally converged. The daily discipline of work helped me become more aware of my limitations and deal with them. At that time, before turning forty, it gave me more solidity as a person—a truer sense of security and the dignified satisfaction of earning a living by doing something worthwhile.
summary: Автор описывает переход от свободного, самовыражающегося образа жизни к устойчивой профессиональной деятельности в актёрской школе, где её работа сдвинулась с акцента на себя на служение ученикам, что привело к личностному росту, осознанию ограничений и обретению внутренней устойчивости.

title: Долгосрочное влияние педагогической работы и интеграция социального инстинкта
text: I dedicated fourteen years to teaching and to the Estudio project led by Juan Carlos, alongside my colleagues Lorena, Manuel, Catalina, Rosa, Francisco… We sought to bring humanity to acting, combining new techniques with deep self-exploration, helping students understand themselves as human beings so they could embody the light and shadow of characters and stories. Today, there are many schools in Spain, and acting techniques have evolved significantly. But back then, there was a void—a lack of training, schools, and methods to renew and enrich the craft of acting. Estudio Corazza became a pillar, and the team of professionals who gathered around this project saw it as a mission entrusted to us, guided and inspired by Juan Carlos’s mastery and our love for our vocation. There, the foundations were laid for the work I later developed in theater and acting. Those were years of intense professional activity, and at the same time, my love life was stabilizing. I also began giving more space to my social instinct—always strong in me, yet often at the mercy of my heart’s intense whims.
summary: За четырнадцать лет работы в Estudio Corazza автор и её команда заложили гуманистическую основу актёрского обучения, объединяя технику с самопознанием, что впоследствии повлияло на её профессиональный путь, одновременно стабилизировав личную жизнь и позволив более сознательно выражать социальный инстинкт.

title: Разрушение гордости и начало исцеления через принятие ответственности
text:
Consumed by work, I neglected the relationship and failed to see the storm brewing on the horizon, which would destroy our life as a couple. Once again, the ghost of abandonment came back to haunt me—the fear of betrayal, the fear of not being the only one. Life struck the armor of my pride, wounding me where it hurt the most. It tore me apart inside to accept that Susi wanted to leave. But what hurt even more was facing my own demon: admitting that she was leaving, at least in part, because I had not known how to love her.

Being left hurts. Knowing there’s someone else hurts even more… and “all that hurts is ego,” Claudio always used to say. I suffered for myself, for feeling betrayed and abandoned. But Susi’s honesty, her transparency, pushed me to take a step forward—to go beyond the humiliation, the offense, the wounded pride, and open myself to the pain of awareness. I began to see my part in it, to recognize how I had hurt her, abandoned her, disregarded her… This feeling of failure in love, of emotional catastrophe, tempted me to give up and throw myself into the madness of heartbreak and destruction. But I wanted to understand what was happening to me when it came to love, to learn how to heal my heart. I wanted to figure out how to be in a relationship. And so, I made a commitment to Susi—to go through a process of reflection, of therapy, but above all, I committed to allowing myself to be questioned, to letting in criticism, to not defending myself, to allowing the water to seep through the cracks, to letting the dam break. How hard it was—and still is—for me to have my false love, my selfishness, my tendency to overlook the other person and to want to be the center of the relationship pointed out to me. My tendency to possess, to turn the other into a slave at my service until they have to run away, suffocated.
summary: Автор описывает эмоциональный кризис в отношениях после ухода партнерши, осознает свою роль в разрушении связи через эгоизм и потребность контролировать, и решает пройти путь терапии и самопознания, чтобы научиться любить по-настоящему.

title: Глубинная работа над сексуальностью и эмоциональной близостью как путь к исцелению
text:
We spent two years deeply examining our relationship: ingrained roles, lies, manipulations, boundaries, questioning what each of us really wanted from this relationship… Sex, for me, was possession, impulse, genitality, a search for satisfaction, a way to cover up the anguish and fear of not being loved—my eternal confusion between being desired and being loved. Sex was also theatricality, a mask hiding my vulnerability, my lack of appetite, my frigidity, my insecurity, and my fear of emptiness, of stillness, of deep and spontaneous intimacy. This has been a major theme in my life, and until then, I hadn’t paid attention to the depth of my struggle, to the underlying anguish that pulsed within me and poisoned my relationships. The wound opened, and I began to bleed… but I also began to heal. I was nearing forty; it was a time when I felt on the edge of an abyss—of pain, of reckoning, of unexpected discoveries. It was also a time of rediscovering Susi—of listening to her, seeing her, learning to love her in a way I didn’t yet know how. Simplicity began to emerge, along with gentleness, uncertainty, the absence of pretense, the willingness to walk together without knowing where we were going, giving ourselves permission to explore what our relationship was in that moment.

This has been something that has defined the course of our relationship. I suppose that, since it has lasted so long, it has evolved alongside our own personal growth, revealing how everything changes throughout life. Being two women, everything is more open, less predictable, and my longing for love had been a mirage—filled with idealization and myth, a movie in my mind that only hurt me, pulling me away from the other person and from my true capacity to love. Believing I was special in the way I loved, romanticizing the idea of love itself—these were patterns that stripped me of freedom and true spontaneity in experiencing love.
summary: Через двухлетнюю работу над отношениями автор осознает, что ее сексуальность была связана с контролем и избежанием боли, а не с близостью; начинает путь к подлинной простоте, честности и принятию неопределенности в любви, освобождаясь от романтических иллюзий.

title: Терапевтическая поддержка и циклические паттерны в отношениях: от кризиса к осознанной любви
text:
During that crisis, we received a lot of help from various psychotherapists. Especially from Suzy Stroke, who was always a friend and an inspiring teacher for our love. And also from Antonio Catalán and Mamen Duran, our therapists, who supported us with deep commitment through that journey.

That crisis was followed by others that accompanied us along the way—separations, doubts about whether we would truly be able to stay together, whether we could continue the path we had started… And beneath it all, the same pattern repeated itself: I wanted everything and didn’t value what I had. I overlooked things, I didn’t pay attention, I didn’t care for her, I didn’t stop to listen to her needs, to respect her timing. She felt alone. She felt that when she gave herself completely, I stopped seeing her, stopped tending to her, and she would retreat—into the cave of her distrust and her rigidity. And I, in turn, felt abandoned, punished. Breaking this cycle has been the greatest challenge of our relationship, and we’re still working on it. We’ve changed a lot, we’ve come to understand each other better. And it’s hard—because, at our core, we are very different. In some ways, we’re aliens to each other. But when the spark ignites, we burn. And as the great poet Rumi says: “It is burning of the heart I want; this burning which is everything, more precious than a worldly empire, because it calls God secretly, in the night.”

There was a time when I felt ashamed to even mention fidelity, and yet, I needed it. Now, I don’t even name it. It’s something spontaneous, genuine, intimate—a treasure, a great act of freedom, of accepting who we are as a couple and what we want. It’s our signature, the jewel of our intimacy, of our bodies as they transform—growing thinner, gaining weight, beginning to sag… The mystery of loving your body alongside another’s as you grow old together.
summary: С помощью терапевтов автор и партнерша проходят через повторяющиеся кризисы, связанные с паттерном пренебрежения и желания обладать, постепенно обучаясь ценить присутствие друг друга; верность перестает быть правилом и становится естественным выражением глубокой, зрелой любви, принимающей изменчивость тел и жизни.

title: Восстановление родительских отношений и самооткрытие
text: I return to the thread of my story, and I must speak of my journey toward love with my parents—something that propelled me into life and opened the door to loving myself. When I began working on my relationship with them, I was already aware of the issues with my mother, but I was still far from questioning my relationship with my father. Being able to acknowledge all the negativity they had passed down to me, to break through the internal censorship that tells us it’s a sin to criticize our parents, was liberating. It opened the door to a greater awareness of who I was and why I was that way. I remember how, in my first therapy work on parental relationships, Enrique de Diego pushed me by embodying my father—mirroring all his mechanisms of seduction and manipulation over the girl I had been. And how I resisted seeing it, how I refused to recognize his shadow. The pain was too great. If I stripped away my idealized image of him, what would be left of him within me? And what would be left of me within myself? Seeing his shadow also meant seeing my own—the manipulation hidden beneath kindness and affection.
summary: The author describes the beginning of healing their relationship with parents, particularly confronting the idealized image of the father and recognizing inherited patterns of manipulation, which leads to greater self-awareness.

title: Глубинная работа в программе SAT и осознание боли родителей
text: I continued this healing process in the SAT Program, and it was key to understanding myself, and in turn, to understanding them—their history, their pain, their wounds. Being able to feel my mother’s sorrow and resentment, the loneliness of that helpless little girl filled with desires she couldn’t express because she had no one to share them with. Recognizing my father’s suffering, his anesthetized rage, his profound loneliness—so unprotected and voiceless in front of his own parents. This filled me with love and compassion for them, for my grandparents, for everyone who had come before me. At that moment, I felt the divine grace of love toward my parents—and an immense gratitude for the gift of life they had given me. But it was a long process, one that took years to truly take shape and meaning within me. Slowly, I began to see them more clearly, to relate to them with greater sincerity. More precisely, I stopped lying to them—something I had been doing until then. The guilt faded, and with it, the games and manipulations—both mine and theirs. My siblings also took up more space within me. I started seeing them as equals, and most importantly, I began to need them, to show myself to them, to share my struggles—not just my successes and strengths.
summary: Through the SAT Program, the author develops empathy for their parents’ unresolved pain, releases guilt and manipulation in family dynamics, and begins to relate to siblings as equals, fostering authentic connection.

title: Поворот в отношениях: от superiority к взаимной близости
text: And then, one day, it happened. Suddenly, I felt it: the need for my parents and siblings, their love, the desire to be close to them, to share myself with them. It was a feeling I couldn’t remember, one that pride had stolen from me when I was still a child. Until then, I had related to them from a place of superiority, of overabundance. They were the ones who needed me, and I was there to help them solve their problems. I had carried the weight of everyone’s burdens alone, never leaning on anyone, keeping myself distant from their love, from their protection—held up by my own omnipotence. But little by little, things started to shift. Our way of relating to each other changed—and it was mutual. I changed, and so did they.
summary: The author shifts from a paternalistic, superior stance toward family to embracing vulnerability and mutual need, marking a fundamental change in relational dynamics.

title: Благословение родителей и внутреннее объединение
text: The definitive turning point came when Susi asked Claudio to marry us; we had to keep shedding layers in every aspect of our lives, sharing our love, opening it to the world. I traveled south to ask for my parents’ blessing; I felt like I was about to experience one of the most crucial moments of my life. I bared my heart to them and spoke about how important this step was for me. My mother opened up, she cried, and she shared all her feelings and inner conflicts regarding my sexual orientation. And I kept opening up, peeling back more layers; we listened to each other without judgment, without criticism, accepting—through compassionate pain—our differences and points of disconnect. It was the first time I could stand before them in my full truth, without needing to do anything to earn their love. That night, my mother came to wish me good night, hugged me, and gave me her blessing. I felt that something once divided had finally come together within me: a deep warmth filled my heart, and I slept as peacefully as I had when I was a child. Feeling my parents’ love and acceptance for everything that I was propelled me into life with a new strength, full of a genuine love for myself.
summary: Receiving parental blessing after honest, vulnerable dialogue about identity and orientation leads to a profound sense of inner unity, self-love, and emotional peace.

title: Интеграция в SAT и рост через служение
text: In the summer of 2001, Claudio married us at La Casa Grande in Quintana de Valdivielso, and we had a big celebration with many friends. It was a moment of glory, of celebration and joy, preceded by deep work—the work that comes before a vow. This period of crisis in our relationship, between the ages of thirty-seven and forty-two, which culminated in our engagement, was also marked by the deepening of my SAT process and my integration into its teaching team. It’s true that when we grow inwardly, we also expand outwardly, and life brings us what we need to keep evolving. In that sense, life was incredibly generous with me. Claudio invited me to collaborate in the SAT program, using what I knew best—working with expression, with theater… What a gift to continue my own journey while also contributing, in my own small way, to my teacher’s great work! And beyond that, to be close to him. This was a turning point in my life—feeling his love beyond both my flaws and my brilliance.
summary: The author’s integration into the SAT teaching team marks a milestone of personal and professional growth, where inner work enables authentic contribution and deepened connection with their partner and teacher.

title: Сдача в боли как путь к возрождению
text: After a regression exercise in the SAT, I was left lying on the floor like a rag; life had drained from me, and I couldn’t move. I felt like a fallen angel, as if I were dying. At that moment, I saw Claudio—towering and majestic—like a great patriarch descending from above, reaching out to me as I was perishing in the underworld of pain and darkness. He helped me sit up and said, “I love you as you are, for who you are.” At that instant, my heart opened. I was able to truly feel my pain, to acknowledge my suffering, and in doing so, I returned to the land of the living. If my teacher loved me like that—stripped of all seduction, of beauty, power, or intellect—if he could love me when I was nothing but a bare, fragile being, emptied even of the basic will to live, then what more proof did I need? What else was I waiting for to feel worthy of God’s love, to bow before Him, and to finally recognize myself as His daughter?
summary: После регрессивного упражнения в SAT автор описывает переживание крайней уязвимости и боли, где любовь и принятие со стороны учителя Claudio помогли ей вернуться к жизни, осознать свою ценность и ощутить связь с Божественной любовью как дочерью Бога.

title: Путь через боль к подлинной любви и принятию себя
text:
And so, I began a journey into pain—and therefore, into love. Until then, I hadn’t realized how closely the two were intertwined. But this new path was no longer about romantic relationships, success or failure, or worldly conflicts. It was about encountering my true self, embracing who I was meant to be, and stepping fully into my destiny.

For a time, the experience felt like hell—so I could know it, so I could deepen my understanding of human suffering, so I could feel my own mortality, and so I could break down the illusions of my pride and bring them into the light.
summary: Автор осознаёт, что боль и любовь тесно связаны, и начинает путь познания себя через страдание, описывая этот опыт как ад, необходимый для разрушения иллюзий гордыни и приближения к своей истинной сущности.

title: Расширение сознания через потерю контроля и сдачу
text: One day, during an exercise guided by Claudio, I lost control completely. I had no sense of space or time, no grasp of what was dream and what was reality—only chaos. I felt death approaching, the terror of dying, of never coming back, of facing it alone. I believe that in that loss of control, the deepest mechanisms of my ego were dissolving, and I couldn’t bear it. I resisted, but the force of it was overwhelming; it broke me down, stripped me of every defense, and left me with no choice but to surrender completely—to be born anew. I had experienced moments of completion before, cycles of wholeness, but this time, after going through Hell, I did not ascend to Heaven—I came back to Earth, to the realm of mortals. I felt profoundly human, deeply connected. I needed others. And for the first time, I was grateful to simply be here, among them. I remember stepping outside the room and taking in the wild, wounded nature around me—it mirrored how I felt. I had aged, yet I had never felt so young. I sat with my companions, Vicenç and Muriel, watching the mountains as the sun faded. Gray snow swept across the peaks in motion, the air was crisp, our hands intertwined, and pure tears of humanity streamed down my face. In recognizing my need for others, I felt the immense relief of being mortal, of belonging—side by side with my brothers and sisters in this world.
summary: Во время упражнения с Claudio автор переживает полную потерю контроля, śmierть эго и вынужденную сдачу, после чего возвращается не в небеса, а на землю, ощущая глубокую связь с людьми, благодарность за простую человечность и осознание своей смертности как источника принадлежности и радости.

title: Преображение через принятие боли и человеческой связи
text:
Since then, small revelations have come to me in everyday life: greater sobriety, a deeper inward focus, fewer words, less need for physical contact—yet, at the same time, a stronger need for others.

The hell of pride unleashed its full violent, destructive force, resisting, refusing to let me surrender, even when surrender was the only path to the peace I so desperately needed. For a time, I was deeply afraid of this hell, dreading its return, as if God had decided I had enjoyed life too much and was now condemning me to suffer, casting me aside. Later, through another therapeutic exercise, I began to understand that hell doesn’t exist—that we create it ourselves. That after death, heaven awaits us all, unconditionally. And that purgatory and hell are not in the afterlife; they unfold here, in this life, because they, too, are part of it.
summary: После пережитого кризиса автор отмечает внутренние изменения: большую трезвость, внутреннюю направленность, уменьшение потребности в словах и физическом контакте, но усиление потребности в близких. Затем описывается борьба с адом гордыни, осознание того, что ад и чистилище — творения ума, существующие в этой жизни, а не в загробном мире.

title: Исцеление через принятие боли и открытость любви
text: My path to redemption has always gone through pain—embracing it, living with it, befriending it, tasting its bittersweet essence. After a painful experience, one in which I allowed myself to feel my own suffering and that of my brothers, the men around me, my heart opened. I became porous, receptive, surrendering to the moment, relishing human connection, skin against skin, the fire of love. In those moments, I reclaimed my deep spontaneity, the joy of simply being, my love for others, and for myself. I surrendered to who I was, to what I felt, to my most genuine expression—embracing everyone and all of myself.
summary: Автор описывает свой путь к искуплению через принятие боли как друга и учителя, объясняя, как открытость своей боли и боли других привела к открытию сердца, восприимчивости, искренности в человеческих отношениях и восстановлению спонтанности, радости бытия и любви к себе и другим.

title: Спонтанность и истинное выражение сердца как духовная практика
text:
I was forty-five years old when I wrote:

For me, the spiritual experience is about shedding the solemn weight of pride, letting go of the script, and rediscovering my true spontaneity—not the kind that is put on display, but the kind that simply is. In my relationships, this translates into a sincerity free of manipulation, light and unburdened; flowing, transparent as water, speaking my truth without attachments or heaviness, allowing what arises from my heart to express itself freely, with laughter and humor always present.

I remember my teacher once asked me, “If you were to become a Buddha or a saint, what would you be like?” At the time, I was fixated on “being very humble,” so I replied that I didn’t want to be a saint—an answer that, ironically, was quite arrogant. Now I ask myself the same question and begin to understand what Claudio teaches us:that our passions can be transformed into wisdom. So my Buddha is love—burning in love, pierced by the arrow, surrendering into the arms of the Beloved. It is generosity and devotion, given freely, without display, without expectation. It is compassion and kindness. It carries a joy for life that is contagious. It has a calling to serve, to help those in need—not from a place of superiority, but from closeness, walking beside them, doing what it can without trying to save the world. It is a warrior, but one moved by a greater force, a purpose, a dream. It can make others laugh and cry—authentic expression is its gift, and sharing it with others, its destiny.
summary: В 45 лет автор формулирует своё понимание духовного опыта как избавления от гордыни и сценариев, возвращения к подлинной спонтанности, которая проявляется в искренних, лёгких отношениях. Она переосмысливает идеал святости не как смирение из тщеславия, а как любовь — живую, щедрую, сострадательную, служащую из близости, а не superiority, способную выражать подлинные эмоции и делиться ими как дар и предназначение.

title: Сдаться потоку чудесного
text:
As Claudio says: “The battle against the ego is just a phase, not the entire path.” At this moment in my life, my greatest wish is to stop doing, so that the miraculous can unfold.

And the miraculous did unfold.

March 2005: A routine check-up revealed a tumor in my left breast. Everything happened so fast. I underwent surgery, and due to the nature of the tumor, they removed eighteen lymph nodes from my armpit. The biopsy confirmed that the first node in the chain was affected. A skilled surgeon performed what he called an “artistic” procedure, leaving my breast with barely any scars. And so began my journey with illness—something I had never foreseen. My fall from the horse.
summary: Автор делится откровением Клаудио о преодолении эго как этапе пути и описывает, как в марте 2005 года у нее обнаружили опухоль груди, после чего началась быстрая медико-хирургическая интервенция и начало пути с болезнью, которую она метафорически называет 'падением с лошади'.

title: Сдаться болезни: химиотерапия и уязвимость
text: From that moment on, everything became about surrender and letting go. At first, I couldn’t grasp that my life was about to be turned completely upside down, that nothing would ever be the same again. I remember stubbornly insisting on attending my first SAT retreat in Brazil, convincing myself that I could postpone chemotherapy—that the retreat would somehow strengthen me, bring me clarity. But it was no longer my time to be in control, to make decisions. It was time to surrender to that painful force, to the devastating hurricane that is cancer and everything it brings with it. In May, I started chemotherapy—the grueling process of destroying my cells, my immune system. With every session, I had to face my anger, my confusion, my fear. With every session, I cried out, Why?, and with every session, I fell a little further down. I was hospitalized multiple times because my white blood cell count had dropped dangerously low, bringing all the risks that come with it. My world was reduced to a single thing: my body—fragile, aching—showing me the way, the way down…
summary: Автор описывает начало химиотерапии как акт сдачи контроля над своей жизнью болезни, detailing физические и эмоциональные страдания, включая нейтропению, госпитализации и ощущение, что мир свелся к хрупкому телу, показывающему путь через боль и слабость.

title: Любовь как опора в беспомощности
text:
Susi was by my side through every stage of the treatment, and through everything that followed. In moments like those, you truly feel the strength of great love, the unwavering support of someone who loves you in your entirety. It was so difficult for me to accept that even in this state—so weak, so helpless, stripped of all strength and resources—there was someone in the world who could love and care for me. But Susi, with the truth of her love, her unconditional devotion, slowly dismantled my inability to believe in a love that asks for nothing in return. A love that simply cares, because I need it. She would say to me in those days, “You needed chemo to surrender to the illness.” And she was right. Without it, I wouldn’t have gone through the journey I did…

After my fourth cycle of chemo, I wrote:

For the first time, I feel like I’m not jumping onto the runaway horse of my mind—not pushing beyond my limits, not trying to be stronger than I am. This cycle has been the hardest. I’ve plunged into the dark pit of absolute weakness, of sheer powerlessness. Not a drop of strength left—800 white blood cells, neutropenia. My candle was flickering out, and there was no way to pull myself back up. I was so exhausted, so drained of life, that I didn’t even want kisses or caresses—just to retreat into myself, to listen to my body sobbing, begging for relief, too weak even to complain. Fever, stabbing pains, loss of appetite, despondency… collapsing, physical suffering. At times, I’d feel a slight improvement, get my hopes up, and then fall right back into the abyss. My body pleaded with me: “Let me fall. I can’t go on. Let me fall all the way. Respect my will—I can’t take any more.” So I let go with it. I became a baby again—defenseless, sick, in need of everything: nourishment, a guiding hand, the unconditional love and care of a mother. And I was afraid—of the darkness, the catastrophic thoughts, the physical decline… But Susi was my pillar. My strength. My sister, my friend, my mother, my love, my nurse, my guide. She pulled me back to life. She held me up, and I leaned on her. I collapsed into her arms, wept in her lap, seeking comfort, finding refuge in her body and her gaze. I walked this via crucis with her, and in the depths of my being, I could feel the power and truth of her love.
summary: Автор описывает трансформирующую силу безусловной любви Сус during химиотерапии, которая помогла ей принять собственную уязвимость и беспомощность, пережить крах контроля над телом и умом, и вновь обойти связь с жизнью через принятие и доверие.

title: Облысение как акт освобождения
text: It was that process of being stripped of my strength, of vulnerability, of losing control over my body and my life that led me to fully surrender to life itself. It was that very process that finally taught me to feel love—love that I could no longer earn through seduction, charm, effort, generosity, or abundance. Chemotherapy left me like a tiny bird, drained of all energy, incapable of anything. It’s the closest I’ve come to dying, though I still don’t know what that truly is. Because in chemo, our youngest, strongest, most vital cells are killed off, in case they carry the poison of cancer, which multiplies so quickly. And with that comes damage to the liver, kidneys, spleen, skin, eyes, hair… At the time, I had a thick mane of long hair; it felt like a part of my identity. Or at least, that’s what I believed. When the oncologist told me I would lose it all, that was the first time I cried over everything that was happening. And so it was. Before my hair started falling out in clumps when I brushed it, I shaved it all off, down to a buzz cut to be radical and defiant. I dyed it in bright colors, trying to console myself, to play, to rebel against the stigma of illness. They told me to get a wig matching my old hair, so I did. But as the last strands began to fall, Susi bought a razor, and every time the fuzz grew back, she shaved it down to nothing. I wanted to be bald and clean. Weightless. I never wore the wig. Eventually, I even stopped wearing the scarves that hid my bare head. And what a liberation it was to show myself… without eyebrows, without eyelashes, without hair, stripped bare by my illness. What a release, to stop hiding what was happening to me! And why had I even wanted to hide it? To avoid scaring people. To avoid showing weakness. Out of fear that I wouldn’t be hired for work. For so many reasons that, in the end, made no sense at all.
summary: Автор описывает потерю волос во время химиотерапии не как потерю идентичности, а как акт освобождения от страха осуждения и необходимости прятать болезнь, culminating в сознательном выбривании головы и отказе от парика и платков как символе принятия своей уязвимости и настоящего себя.

title: Болезнь как стигма и внутренняя борьба
text: When we’re sick, we fear rejection. We live in a world that turns its back on illness, making us feel stigmatized. For a long time, I felt guilty for being sick, as if it were the consequence of not having done things right; as if I were being punished. How much omnipotence I found in my own mind! As if I had the power to prevent illness, as if I were God, as if life followed some clear law of cause and effect. I kept thinking, If only I had done this or that… if only I had avoided that other thing… if only I had taken better care of myself... My mind raced, desperately trying to grasp the formula for life, for wellness, to understand where I had gone wrong. There was so much suffering, so much exhaustion, so much resistance to my fate—to the simple fact that everything was beyond my control, in the hands of something greater, a vast intelligence that both creates order and disorder. So much rage, so much guilt, so much shame.
summary: The narrator describes the stigma of illness, feelings of guilt and self-blame, and the illusion of control over fate, ultimately confronting the helplessness before a higher power governing life and death.

title: Сдача и принятие помощи как путь к исцелению
text: Little by little, those thoughts started to dissolve; there was no way I could control the mystery of what was happening to me. One day, Claudio asked me, “Are you taking this as a punishment or as an opportunity?” His words, along with meditation, broke the dam. There was nothing to do but live through it as best I could—not even be grateful for it, just live it. Surrender to the powerful force that was breaking me down. And so, I began to savor the small things, the major events of my day-to-day life: waking up with an appetite for even a little food, tasting the juice while I still could, reading in the hammock and feeling the sunlight streaming through my bedroom window, a friend’s visit, doing a little yoga with Pepe, stepping onto the balcony to catch some fresh air and watch people go by, listening to music, the touch of Susi’s hand, the way she looked at me... Everything was slow, fragile, quiet. And for the first time in my life, I was truly experiencing something I had always avoided: feeling needy, receiving without giving anything in return.
summary: Through Claudio’s question and meditation, the narrator begins to surrender to illness, finding meaning in small moments and learning to accept care and vulnerability without guilt.

title: Отношения в болезни: брат, родители и жена как источники поддержки
text:
There were two moments in this process that I want to share. During my fifth round of chemo, Susi got a role in a film in Valencia. We needed the money, and I didn’t want her to miss out on the golden opportunity. I felt like she was giving me her whole life, all her time, so I had to ask my younger brother Roberto to come take care of me. It was so hard to ask, to let myself be cared for by the baby of the family—the one I had always looked after and advised! Putting myself in his hands, letting him see me so weak, having him stay with me through the brutal effects of chemo, helping me pull through, watching me fall apart, and being the one to comfort me... It brought us closer in a way that felt more honest than ever before. And, as life always does as it pleases, with its own mysterious wisdom, my last chemo session was spent with my parents. It became one of the most healing experiences of my life: to go back to being the baby I once was, needing everything, to be their sick daughter who relied on them—not the self-sufficient, superior child I had become at five years old, but a daughter in need of comfort.

I was in bed during one of the crashes that would hit me for ten days after chemo. I cried out of sheer despair, out of feeling stripped of all life force. But looking back now, I realize I was also crying so they could comfort me—so I could feel their comfort. My mother sat at my bedside, gently stroking my forehead, while my father softly caressed my PICC line. That moment healed one of the wounds that had built the tower of my pride—the denial of the deep, endless need a child has for their parents. That bottomless well we all feel, which I had filled with pride, superiority, and self-sufficiency. It moves me to remember how much hope my father’s cheerful voice around the house gave me, how my mother’s anxious, over-the-top attentiveness soothed me. I had them all to myself again, just like in my first year of life—me, their daughter, and them, my parents.
summary: The narrator recounts two pivotal moments of receiving care: asking her brother to help during chemo and being nurtured by her parents during the final session, which healed her pride and reawakened childhood dependency and love.

title: Иллюзия как порядок и красота в хрупкости бытия
text:
Fifteen years have passed, and I see now that, among many other things, illness brought order to my life. It put everything in its rightful place. The doctors were doctors—they were there to heal me. And I was there to let myself be healed. My parents were my parents. My siblings were my siblings. Susi—my wife, my partner—was the family I had built. I felt the presence of friends who showed up, and the absence of those who couldn’t. My teachers became more than ever my teachers, and I needed them to help me bring light to the darkness that had swallowed me.

Meditation and the fragility of my body connected me to the divine. Doing gave way to simply being, to a more subtle perception, to being moved by beauty. There is a flower in my garden that embodies this fragility—tall and slender, holding itself up, swaying with the wind’s movement. That is its dance. It offers no resistance; it allows itself to be carried. That is its balance. That is how it survives. Any harsh movement could snap its stem and end its existence, yet there it stands, offering its beauty to the world, fulfilling the purpose it was given. I was overwhelmed by its beauty. I knew its life would be short, that it could be crushed at any moment by an animal, a passing footstep, a drop of rain. But it had given me its beauty—it offered itself fully in that instant, only to die afterward. A life that lasted mere hours, a life made into an offering so that I could witness it, so that it could add to the world’s beauty. And I thought: That’s what I want to do with the life I have left—offer myself in the beauty of my essence, holding nothing back, without pretending, without trying to remain, without clinging to it. And that day, I exhaled. I found meaning in what I was living.
summary: Reflecting years later, the narrator sees illness as a restoring force that clarified relationships and roles, leading to a spiritual awakening through fragility, symbolized by a fleeting flower, inspiring her to live authentically and offer her beauty without attachment.

title: Аяуаска и встреча со смертью
text: A year after beginning treatment, as I was starting to recover, I had an experience with ayahuasca in Brazil. I came face to face with my own death. It said to me: “Look at me. I’m here. Take me seriously.” Taking it seriously didn’t mean fighting it. It meant giving it its place, looking it straight in the eye, knowing it was there—and that it had been so very close. Taking my life very seriously.
summary: Автор описывает свой опыт с аяуаской в Бразилии, где столкнулся лицом к лицу со своей смертью и осознал необходимость принять её серьёзно, не борясь, а признавая её присутствие как часть жизни.

title: Сон о лодке и ощущение мира после бури
text: I had a dream. I arrived at the sea. There was a boat, with a young man and an older man I had encountered earlier. The older man slept on deck while the young one sat in lotus position at the helm. I jumped onto the boat and clung to the mast. We sailed toward the open sea. I felt the wind rising—it was dangerous. I called out to them from above. The sail tore, we wrecked, we were rescued. There were many people, and we reached a vast shore. Despite being drenched and having been in danger, I felt an immense sense of peace.
summary: Во сне автор попадает в шторм на лодке с двумя мужчинами, переживает крушение и спасение, но несмотря на опасность и дискомфорт, ощущает глубокий внутренний покой.

title: Цитата Питера Брук о решениях из глубины
text: “Decisions emerge when something deeper than our desires pushes through the clouds of longing—something more essential than our own ideas. And when that happens, you don’t think about the cost, and you don’t try to predict the outcome.” (Peter Brook)
summary: Цитата Питера Брук о том, что истинные решения возникают не из желаний или расчётов, а из чего-то более глубокого и essential, когда человек перестаёт думать о последствиях и просто следует внутреннему зову.

title: Освобождение после болезни и звонок свободы
text: When I started to recover, the hardest yet most glorious moment arrived: realizing that I was no longer the same person and couldn’t keep living as I had before. The call of freedom, of my instincts, of my heart, was so strong that I couldn’t ignore it—it was real, coursing through every cell in my body. A clear and powerful voice told me: “Consuelo, do whatever you want. Now you can, because you are in harmony with yourself, with the life that has been given back to you, and with your destiny. This is your sacred freedom—it’s not selfishness, whim, or neurosis. It’s life; it’s the call of your blood.” And I felt, with deep conviction, that I would follow it. My battle scars became my reasons, my strength. Rarely in my life had I felt such certainty. I still didn’t know what I wanted, but I was sure of what I didn’t. I knew I had to leave, though I didn’t know where to go or have a plan. And so began the process of leaving the Estudio, the project I had been part of for seventeen years, and separating professionally from Juan Carlos—my mentor and dear friend.
summary: После выздоровления автор переживает глубокое осознание своей трансформации и слышит внутренний голос, призывающий к священной свободе — жизни в гармонии с собой и судьбой, что приводит к решению уйти из долгосрочного проекта и расстаться с mentor.

title: Боль и ясность расставания с семьёй и коллективом
text: Leaving family is never easy. It was painful, but I don’t think I had ever felt so alive, so present, so clear about what I wanted, so completely myself. I suffered, and they didn’t make it easy for me; it was hard for all of us—hard for me to leave and hard for them to let me go. Again and again, my seductive energy was put to the test—my need to leave without angering anyone, to do everything the “right” way. But I had a warning bell inside me: I could not betray myself. My life was at stake. I had just come out of a brutal illness, and I wasn’t about to change my path just to please others or to meet the expectations I imagined the group had of me.
summary: Автор описывает болезненный, но ясный и живительный процесс расставания с семьёй и коллективом, где внешнее давление и внутренние соблазны угождать сталкиваются с непреклонной потребностью остаться верным себе после тяжёлой болезни.

title: Свобода в неопределённости и пустоте как источник смысла
text: After the loneliness, the emptiness of having no plans, the vertigo of an uncertain future, the fear of not knowing how I would make a living—came the magnificent experience of being free again. I remembered the moment I left the Centro Andaluz de Teatro at thirty years old, riding a bus to Madrid with a million pesetas in my bank account and no idea where I was headed—but free as a bird, taking charge of my own path. I needed that blank space, that lack of plans. I needed time to sit with that emptiness, that not knowing. I needed to let my soul steep in it, to make space for my desire, to allow the meaning of this new life to reveal itself. And it did—without plans, without projects, without forcing anything. Just by living. A time of uncertainty, of lying fallow. And now I understand what I discovered in that period, what that permission gave me: the key to my path. From that moment on, I have done only what I truly want. Honoring my deepest desire is the greatest commitment I can have—to myself and to the world. I can no longer escape it. When I stray from that path, when I get distracted, my body reacts instantly—it falls ill, or I begin to drift like a lost soul. That’s how I know I’m not being true to myself.
summary: После одиночества и страха перед неопределённым будущим автор переживает magnificenтное чувство свободы, вспоминая прошлый опыт жизненного прыжка в неизвестность, и осознаёт, что только в пустоте и отсутствии планов может раскрыться истинное желание и смысл жизни, которые становятся внутренним компасом.

title: Изменение понятия свободы: от нейротической к священной
text: I had always sought freedom—but a neurotic kind, the kind that meant getting my way, being willful and self-indulgent. I have a childhood memory of desperately wanting to go on a school trip. My father told me we didn’t have the money, but I convinced him anyway. I had all the best arguments for why I had to go, and in the end, I got my way. Today, it pains me to think of my father’s sacrifice—and my own inability, back then, to accept being denied, to renounce something for the sake of someone else. But now, I was beginning to understand a deeper kind of freedom. Staying true to my real desires, to my inner calling, meant accepting that my choices might bring rejection from others. It meant letting go of the need to be liked by everyone, understanding that my choices wouldn’t always please the world. It meant choosing what truly made me happy and nourished my soul—my sacred freedom. And when I align myself with that, my life is good—not just for me, but for everyone around me. Its fruits benefit even those who disapprove of my choices.
summary: Автор контрастирует своё прежнее представление о свободе как得道得志 и самовольстве с новым пониманием священной свободы — верности внутреннему зову, даже если это приводит к неприятию, и осознаёт, что такая свобода приносит пользу не только ей, но и окружающим.

title: Освобождение через отказ от одобрения группы
text: This need was born from the many years I spent working at the Estudio, sacrificing myself to maintain the status of being my mentor’s right-hand woman, living for his approval. I had fought so hard to get everyone to follow my vision for the project, convinced it was the best path. The endless effort to “be right” had poisoned my relationship with Juan Carlos and my colleagues. It was a dark time—fighting to make a collective project my own dream, trying to convince them to adopt it as theirs. And suddenly, I realized—I didn’t have to convince anyone. I just had to let go and follow my dream alone. When you’ve built yourself around a group for years, when you have that tribal sense of belonging, breaking away is painful. You feel it in your gut, like you’re betraying your family. Who are you outside of this group? It’s like quitting an addiction—you have to go through withdrawal, let go, walk alone. But once you do, the feeling is incredible. I realized how much weight I had been carrying—and how light I was beginning to feel…
summary: The author reflects on years of seeking approval through overwork and control in a group setting, realizing that true freedom comes from letting go of the need to convince others and following her own path alone, despite the emotional pain of separation.

title: Пересмотр свободы как внутренней искренности
text:
After a therapy session, I wrote:

Before, I thought freedom was getting others to do what I wanted. But in that mindset, I was a slave—building my life around seduction and manipulation to achieve it. Now, I do what I want, without needing others to follow me. And that is true freedom.

I am shedding my old skin; it’s exhilarating, but I also feel exposed, raw. Today, I believe with all my heart that choosing my own path is my right, my freedom—it’s how I honor my dignity.

I want to keep discovering myself, finding myself. That is what it means to live—to feel my life. My true freedom is listening to my soul’s desire and following it. I tell myself: “Do whatever you want.” And hearing those words makes me so happy—I can feel my cells dancing in joy, celebrating this initiation. Yes—“Do whatever you want” holds both immense freedom and a deep commitment to life.
summary: The author contrasts her earlier, manipulative understanding of freedom with her current realization that true freedom lies in self-directed action, self-honoring, and following one’s soul’s desire without needing validation from others.

title: Творческое расцветание через аутентичность и смирение
text: So, at forty-eight, I entered the most creative phase of my life—the one in which I grew and expanded the most as an artist. It was about letting go, and suddenly, everything began to open up. I explored texts that fascinated me, working with groups of actors in my own way. I deepened my craft and realized how much I could help others simply by being myself—how far I could go with someone else when I was true to my deepest intuition. I discovered the magic that emerges when I fully inhabit myself, which, paradoxically, means surrendering my sense of self and becoming a channel for something greater. Until then, I had been a rough sketch; now, I was painting the full, vivid picture of my existence. And then, the path to my dream unfolded—returning to acting, growing as an actress, evolving. The big roles came my way, not because the projects were always significant—some were, others less so—but because the characters were. They arrived exactly when I needed them, each one pushing me forward, allowing me to reveal myself, to express my truth to the world, to transcend my own limits. They forced me to confront the constraints of my personality and the deep-seated insecurity about my worth as an artist—an insecurity I had long masked with arrogance. How many times had I said, “I won’t work that way or with that person because I’m special, because I’m a superior artist”? But beneath those thoughts lay a profound lack of trust in my own abilities. I had spent so long chasing artistic excellence that I had never dared to throw myself into the fire and face the ghost that haunted me—the terrifying belief that I wasn’t good enough, that I would never be capable of playing great roles. But then the opportunity came—to take a risk—and I took it. And then another. And another. And with each one, I realized how much humility is required to do great things—how much surrender, how much strength it takes to fall and get back up, to fail and keep trying. How much love it takes to prioritize something greater than my ego’s comfort—to drag it through the mud, bruise it, let it resist, let it rise again only to be knocked down once more. Art does not tolerate ego. Art demands surrender. It demands that you bite into the fire, the filth, the struggle. It’s like a force of nature—you either yield to it completely, giving yourself over without resistance, or it rejects you, spits you out, turns you into an empty shell of an artist. But that’s not my path. My path in art is to set my fire at its service—this fire of longing, of intensity, of an unrelenting hunger to experience life to its fullest. And finally, I was able to do it. What a relief!
summary: The author describes her artistic awakening at age 48, marked by letting go of ego, embracing humility and surrender to the artistic process, and discovering that true creativity arises from authenticity and service to something greater than oneself.

title: Подтверждение аутентичности через внешнее признание
text: One summer, I was talking to Annie Chevreux and Claudio about my work on the role of the mother in Blood Wedding, and Claudio said to me, “You’ve put your fire on the stage.” And that was it—betting honestly on what I could give to art, so that art, in turn, could refine and shape it…
summary: The author recounts a pivotal moment when a colleague recognized her authentic artistic expression, confirming that her honest investment in her work allows art to transform and elevate her contribution.

title: Тринадцать дней прощания и отъезд в Мадрид
text: Thirteen days in a coma. Thirteen days to prepare ourselves, to say goodbye, to cry and console each other, to communicate with him through the tubes and wires, to tell him so many things, to let him go. Two of us at a time, taking turns, while my mother sat there—devastated, shattered… Thirteen days to feel the greatness of this small, extraordinary man—this wonderful father. And then, one morning, my brother Fale and I, just the two of us, gave the doctors permission to remove his life support. The doctor said he didn’t know how long it would take. I said my goodbye, then boarded a train to Madrid for rehearsals. How could I leave? But I did. I fled… On the train, I called Claudio. I told him my father was dying. I needed to tell him because, by then, Claudio had become like a second father to me. I arrived in Madrid and received my brother’s call: He’s gone… And then, back to Cádiz—with Susi, with my brother Roberto and my sister-in-law—traveling all night, what a brutal night, to return home and find my mother completely broken, drowning in grief, terrified by the loss of her husband—her love, the foundation of her life.
summary: The narrator describes the thirteen-day vigil during their father’s coma, the decision to withdraw life support, the emotional journey to Madrid for work, and the painful return home to find their mother shattered by grief.

title: Осознание сироты и начало скорби
text:
I had become an orphan, though I hadn’t realized it until that moment. Only then did I truly grasp the depth of my father’s presence—his immense love, his life force—and the vast emptiness he left behind.

Months later, in Mexico, I sat with Claudio and told him how lost I felt without my father’s gaze. How, before, everything had made sense because he had been there to see me. I hadn’t had enough time to say goodbye, to appreciate him fully. And now—who was I doing things for? Who was watching me? I felt numb, as if life had lost its meaning. I had no desire to live it. Claudio told me to try speaking to him, to reach out to him. He shared a moving dream in which he had encountered his own father and had felt his love in every fiber of his being.

And I have felt it, too. I feel it still. I know how much my father loved me, and I can sense his love in every part of my body, in every cell. Now that he is gone, I understand that, deep down, he always loved me exactly as I was—and that he still embraces me from the stars.
summary: The narrator reflects on the realization of being an orphan, the emotional numbness and loss of meaning after their father’s death, and the enduring sense of his love as a spiritual presence.

title: Два года скорби и исцеление через ритуал
text:
The grief lasted two years—a long, internal journey of acceptance and healing. Supporting my mother through it was, and still is, the hardest part. Being by her side means sitting with raw grief, with the unbearable despair of loss. And it’s difficult for me. I want her to be okay. I want her to stop hurting. Her pain tears me apart; it makes me feel powerless. In one exercise, I allowed myself to feel her grief—and it was vast, devastating. But after that, I was able to hold more compassion for her. I stopped carrying so much of the weight, stopped feeling so responsible. I could finally sit beside her without trying to change her, allowing her sorrow to exist as it was.

Two years after my father’s death, I met the Yoruba priest José Vilas from Cuba, and I asked him about my father. He said, “He’s right here with us. And he wants me to tell you to go and buy lots of the flowers he loved and throw them into the place where you laid his remains. That’s what he needs to move happily toward the light.” As soon as I returned to Spain, I went south. My brother Fale, my mother, and I set out in a small boat, our arms full of flowers. We scattered them into the sea, right where we had spread his ashes—celebrating his life, honoring this wonderful man. That ritual brought me peace. Fulfilling his final wish, sending him off with flowers, knowing that he was running joyfully toward the light—and that his legacy would always remain with us.
summary: The narrator describes the two-year grieving process, the emotional toll of supporting their mother, and the healing found through a Yoruba-inspired ritual of scattering flowers at sea to honor their father’s passing.

title: Принятие хрупкости и поиск силы в уязвимости
text:
These past few years have been intense—entering my fifties, losing my father, a deep crisis in my relationship, a separation and reunion, immense professional growth… and time and again, coming face to face with my own fragility. Feeling the limits of my body, growing older… Fragility! My soul lives in it, in accepting it, embracing it, smiling at it, cradling it—that is who I am. And now, more than ever. It’s not like before; suddenly, I’m fully aware of my age, of what it means to grow older. My pride fights against time and my body, because inside me, there’s an undefeated voice: I can, I won’t be like the others, I will push further. Learning to live without control, with fear, with the needs of my body—learning to smile at my own fragility—is part of the journey. “In the acceptance of weakness lies true strength.” I believe this is a healing mantra for the proud.
