One example: for a long time, I identified with Tom Thumb—the clever, thumb-sized boy who saves his seven brothers from being abandoned by parents too poor to feed them, and later, from the Ogre who devours children. After overcoming countless obstacles with his wit, Tom Thumb returns home triumphantly with his brothers and a treasure he heroically wins that ensures their parents can now provide for them. I saw myself in his superiority over his parents and, in my fantasies, I too achieved their ultimate recognition—a victory, just like in the tale.
summary: Объясняет, как социальные E2 мыслят образами, верят в осуществимость своих fantasies и пытаются подстроить реальность под них, не осознавая своего давления на других; иллюстрируется личными примерами идентификации с Томом Thumb и использованием метафор солнца и пламени.

title: Компульсивная амбициозность и逃避 реальности через фантазию о успехе
text:
ALBA ARENA

The ambitious type enjoys mentally anticipating future successes, using this foresight to better structure their goals. This positive visualization drives them into compulsive action, masking a deep sense of emptiness. Much like E7, they often mistake fantasizing for actually doing. They become consumed by grand projects, celebrating the victory before the battle has even begun. Social E2s use fantasy to amplify their emotional intensity, turning into a whirlwind of energy in service of their latest ambition. The downside? They neglect relationships and even their own basic needs, expecting others to do the same. When they don’t see that same level of dedication in others, they become frustrated and lash out.

They imagine dramatic, unexpected events that will miraculously solve their problems and earn them widespread recognition. Their thoughts don’t always follow fixed rules or logical connections, reinforcing their self-perception as highly intuitive, even bordering on genius. Their intellectual life is intense but not always rational, as they selectively seek out information that confirms their suspicions, leaving little room for doubt or ambiguity.

What is often perceived as superficiality stems, in part, from a lack of connection with their true emotions. Avoiding pain or remaining “unaware” of what’s really happening is a result of the emotional numbness characteristic of E2s—particularly social E2s—leading to moments of striking detachment from reality.

When I was around twenty-seven, I was at my parents’ house, where my grandmother was living at the time. My mother and I noticed something was wrong. She was struggling to breathe. She passed away while I was holding her hand. When the emergency team arrived, it only took them a few minutes to confirm what we already knew: she was gone. As the doctor approached me to deliver the news, my first instinct was to smile, point at the name on his coat, and say, “Wow! You have the same name as my brother.” The man went pale, staring at me like I had completely lost my mind. Could I have been any more superficial?
summary: Описывает, как социальные E2 используют позитивную визуализацию будущих успехов для структурирования целей, путают фантазию с действием, пренебрегают отношениями и потребностями, демонстрируют поверхностность из-за эмоциональной онемённости, illustrated by a personal story of reacting inappropriately to their mother's death.

title: Цикл неутолимого стремления у социальных Э2
text: The social E2 can be seen as a compulsive consumer of projects, a glutton for ambition. But they don’t stick around to truly receive love, nor even to savor their own successes, which are fleeting at best. Once a goal is achieved, it loses its emotional value almost immediately, making way for new desires that materialize into yet more objectives—serving only to fuel and feed an insatiable personal ambition. No accomplishment ever carries enough weight to feel like a true endpoint, a moment of lasting fulfillment. They don’t even take time to enjoy their victories; they discard them and move on. This never-ending cycle—from the fantasy of having to the reality of engaging with the object—causes them to lose interest the moment something becomes real.
summary: Описывает, как социальные Э2 постоянно стремятся к новым целям, не получая удовлетворения от достижений, поскольку их успех теряет эмоциональную ценность сразу после осуществления, поддерживая бесконечный цикл амбиций без истинного покоя.

title: Путаница между желанием и потребностью у социальных Э2
text:
Like all emotionally-driven personalities, they confuse desire (more accurately, hyper-desire) with genuine needs. Disconnected from their basic needs (to be cared for, to be loved, to recognize themselves as human), the social E2 redirects their sense of fulfillment toward public validation. This leaves them perpetually dissatisfied, trapped in the magical belief that being important will somehow make them feel truly alive.

At times, my need for compensation or contrast to the painful emptiness manifests in the search for instant gratification—seeking excitement that’s consumed in the moment, leaving me with the same inner void, the same dissatisfaction as before. That’s when I turn to something external, and in a burst of consumerism, I buy clothes I don’t need. This vain investment in appearance only deepens the gap between my social image and my inner feeling of emotional deprivation.
summary: Объясняет, как социальные Э2 принимают гипержелание за настоящие потребности, ищут подтвершения во внешнем мире и через потребительство пытаются заполнить внутреннюю пустоту, что лишь увеличивает разрыв между их образом и внутренним состоянием.

title: Воображение как инструмент влияния и самозащиты у социальных Э2
text:
In order to cultivate the emotional dynamic needed to captivate a group and earn its approval, the social E2 weaves elaborate scenarios in their mind, using tricks and spectacle to “tap into” the hidden emotions of those they seek to influence. Through this, they draw the strength to present themselves as confident, grounded, and deserving of attention, positioning themselves as the one who can give voice to the ideals and concerns of their audience.

Their imagination knows no bounds.

I had two ways of comforting myself. One was waiting for everyone to fall asleep, then sneaking into the kitchen with our little puppy and crying into its fur, making sure no one saw me.

The other (aside from endlessly reading) was fantasizing. I’d pull the covers over my head and create an apocalyptic world in my mind, where only a few survivors remained. We covered ourselves with cloth to protect against radioactive rain or a contagious disease that, of course, I was always immune to. And then, at some pivotal moment, when someone happened to catch a glimpse of my eyes between the folds of fabric, they’d realize that I had the power to heal them. I had all kinds of powers, but they all revolved around healing: I cured, I listened, and I illuminated people’s hearts, helping them see the world in a more hopeful light. And with these stories, I’d drift off to sleep night after night.
summary: Описывает, как социальные Э2 используют воображение для создания впечатляющих сценариев, чтобы влиять на других и поддерживать собственный образ, а также как фантазии служат утешением и способом избежания боли через сакрализацию собственного исцеляющего начала.

title: Видение будущего и страх уязвимости у социальных Э2
text:
Social E2s use imagination as part of the strategies they employ to convince individuals and groups to invest in projects that reflect their current desires. They often dream up community initiatives based on both personal and collective needs and ideals.

The people they address come to recognize in them the one who will finally give voice to their thoughts and desires. Captivated by the enthusiasm characteristic of this personality, others recognize their importance and reinforce their belief that they are carrying out work of profound social significance.

Their visionary thoughts, tied to success, allow this subtype to live in the future, keeping them distracted from the inner experiences that unsettle them. The past holds little value for them, and the present is only important as preparation for what’s ahead. The projects they pursue always seem like the ultimate goal, yet the objective remains elusive, always postponed—never fully attained.

Imagination is mainly driven by the desire to envision a future where they are finally recognized in their rightful place—whether within the family, the group, or society—where no one will ever forget them, cast them aside, or deny them the love they believe they deserve. They picture actions that represent the realization of the justice they feel is vital for the world, all made possible through their personal commitment.

The expression of “negative” emotions, like anger and sadness, is tied to the fear that both others and themselves would uncover a side of them that’s less impressive, a side that’s in need. This contradicts their idealized image of being strong and “superior,” leading to fears of being rejected or destroyed by others. These emotions would also force them to confront the reality of being just like anyone else—needing support—while their self-image insists that they should always be the one offering it from above.

Facing failure is the dreaded moment of confronting frustration, a sense of inadequacy, and above all, humiliation. In response, they either retreat to buy time and restore their image, or manipulatively spiral into victimhood, dramatically expressing their “deep pain”—the deepest a human could feel. This manipulation serves as a form of revenge against whoever caused the failure, rather than an opportunity to confront who they truly are and integrate parts of themselves that might threaten their narcissistic self-image.
summary: Раскрывает, как социальные Э2 используют воображение для построения идеального будущего, избегая настоящего и прошлого, подавляя негативные эмоции из страха перед уязвимостью и реагируя на неудачу манипулятивной позицией жертвы, чтобы защитить своё завышенное self-образ.

title: Мировоззрение социального E2: агрессоры и жертвы
text: In their view of the world, it’s divided between aggressors and victims, and the social E2 swears never to be the victim again. Yet, they inevitably play this role throughout their life. But they can't acknowledge this, repressing the pain and losses that inevitably come. They deny any form of abuse and push it to the shadows, dissociating from the suffering while also avoiding the possibility of protecting themselves assertively. What matters most is not feeling dependent, fearful, or insignificant. As a result, they become dismissive, condescending, and authoritarian, convinced they have no limits—allowing them to feel powerful and above others.
summary: Описывает социальный E2 как видящий мир через призму ролей агрессора и жертвы, стремящегося избежать позиции жертвы, но неизбежно попадающего в нее, что приводит к подавлению боли и авторитарному поведению как компенсации страха зависимости и незначимости.

title: Детство социального E2: ранняя зрелость и отсутствие границ
text:
Childhood

The title of this chapter may seem paradoxical, considering that social E2s often didn’t have typical childhood experiences and may never have truly felt like children. From an early age, they were unusually advanced in developmental milestones such as psychomotor skills, speech, and bladder control. Their intuitive abilities, particularly their skill at perceiving others’ emotions and understanding adult experiences, also became apparent early on. This is partly due to the fact that they develop empathy at a young age, often by offering it to a parent who relies on them, and to whom they direct their greatest attentions and care.

Lack of boundaries

Social E2s quickly learn that neither parent is truly available to them, so they assume the role of their own authority. In their world, boundaries (whether internal or external) don’t exist. Everything seems possible. There is no emotional or behavioral containment from either parental figure. The sense of omnipotence they begin to build in their early years reinforces their belief in their capacity for self-rule.

As long as I can remember, I’ve always felt older, like I belonged among the adults. My quick wit, sense of humor, disregard for boundaries, and boldness have always earned me a place with them. My father, but especially my mother and maternal grandmother, consistently conveyed that I was someone special.

My mother treated me like her sister (in fact, she often calls me by her own name), her husband, her confidante. But I never truly felt, I suppose due to my lack of respect for her, that she acted as a mother; I was both mother and father to myself. She didn’t know how to (or perhaps didn’t want to) set boundaries for me. In some way, she tried to make me feel free and powerful, perhaps because that’s what she also wanted for herself.
summary: Описывает особенности детства социального E2: ранняя психологическая и эмоциональная зрелость, отсутствие родительских границ, ролевой обмен с родителями (особенно матерью), что формирует убеждение в собственной самодостаточности и omnipotence.

title: Роль социального E2 в семье: опора родителей и изолированность
text:
The social E2 subtype was not a particularly difficult child for their mother. They quickly learned to be responsible, maturing prematurely, and often became one of their parent’s right hands—or, as Paolo Baiocchi puts it, the left hand, stepping in to fill the father’s role when possible. They were independent, especially in the eyes of the mother, who relied on them, and neither parent needed to take care of them.

The strong bond between the mother and child often leaves the father out of the picture. During the Oedipal phase, the father is either excluded from the relationship or leaves the family altogether, becoming a peripheral figure, either forgotten or idealized as long as he remains distant and doesn’t interfere with the child’s desires. If the child rebels against the father in any way, it is usually to defend the mother or siblings, especially when they are treated unfairly, oppressively, or abusively.

With my father, I always felt more mature than he was, bigger than him. He was always incredibly proud of me, of how smart I was and the social awareness I showed. As a child, I was the apple of his eye. When he left home, I convinced myself he wasn’t abandoning me, but my mother. His absence was just collateral damage. I remember telling him that night, “I understand, Dad. Don’t worry.”

Everything changed when he came back, and by then, I was already a teenager. The idol I had built in my mind came crashing down.
summary: Рассматривает социального E2 как ребенка, ставшего опорой для родителей (особенно матери), при этом отец часто исключается из близких отношений, что приводит к идеализации или отвержению отца и глубокому эмоциональному кризису при его возвращении.

title: Автономия и ответственность социального E2: опека над другими
text:
From an early age, social E2s exhibit autonomy in their actions and thoughts, cultivating a sharp self-awareness and a critical perspective on others. They are often treated as though they’re older and more mature than they actually are, expected to serve as a support for the adults around them. As a result, they never learn that they, too, might need others who could offer them the same support in return.

At some point, they start to take initiative and assume responsibilities that are generally well-received by at least one parent. As adults, they often position themselves as a point of reference or a guide for others, sometimes even overstepping boundaries with their desire to help when no one has asked for it.

Over time, I also took on the task of calming my father, or at least trying to, to prevent his anger from being directed at my siblings. Later, I learned to confront him, or at least try, even though I felt as though I was dying from fear and love. I loved my father deeply, as well as my mother, but it always felt like I had to reach out to them, never the other way around.
summary: Описывает, как социальный E2 с ранних лет проявляет автономию и берет на себя заботу о взрослых, не научившись принимать поддержку, что приводит к роли посредника и опекуна в семье, часто в ущерб собственным эмоциональным потребностям.

title: Подростковый возраст социального E2: роль «хорошего ребенка» и одиночество
text:
ALBA ARENA

In my teenage years, I tried not to disappoint, taking on the role of the “good kid,” the one with their head screwed on straight; the reliable one that others could count on. It made me feel important.

MAURIZIO MARTELLI

They position themselves closer to the expectations of adults and the parental system than to those of their siblings, never experiencing the same carefree childhood or feeling like their playmate. This leaves them with a deep sense of loneliness, as though they’re caught in no man’s land.

They come to realize that their place in the family isn’t granted by birthright, but earned through their actions. Their comfort lies in clinging to a dual fantasy: the sense of grandeur that comes with feeling so close to the adults, and the belief that the future will bring wonderful surprises where they will finally be rewarded with justice and love for all they’ve done for others.
summary: Описывает подростковый период социального E2: стремление быть «хорошим ребенком» для одобрения взрослых, отчуждение от сверстников, чувство одиночества и убеждение, что их место в семье должно быть заслужено, а не дано по праву рождения.

title: Опыт старшей сестры и ранняя ответственность
text: I was always trapped by the responsibility of my actions. As the oldest sister, I had the task of setting a good example, as my mother would constantly remind me, which weighed heavily on my heart. This position sparked a certain envy in my siblings, so I withdrew. I didn’t compete or seek attention. Instead, I limited myself to helping my mother around the house, taking care of the little ones, and not seeking affection.
summary: Первый чанк описывает опыт рассказчика как старшей сестры, которая чувствовала тяжесть ответственности, избегала соперничества и сосредоточилась на заботе о доме и младших siblings, не ища привязанности.

title: Раннее осознание родительских ожиданий и забота о брате
text:
ALBA ARENA

Since I was five, I was aware of my parents’ expectations, trying to meet them in every way and fully conforming to their desires.

By seven, I was looking after my brother while my mother worked. I’d prepare his meals and make sure nothing happened to him, so she wouldn’t worry or scold me.
summary: Чанк рассказывает о раннем осознании родительских ожиданий с пятилетнего возраста и практической заботе о брате с семи лет, включая приготовление еды и обеспечение его безопасности.

title: Социальный subtype E2 как «хороший мальчик/девочка» в детстве
text:
MAURIZIO MARTELLI

Their sense of themselves as someone capable of offering magical, healing love clearly originates from their childhood experiences, influenced by two key factors: ambivalent attachment wounds and the illusion of being bigger than their parents.

The social E2 subtype is often the “good boy” or “good girl” in early childhood. They’re the pride of the household, eating and sleeping well, speaking early, being witty, obeying readily, and always eager to please everyone around them.
summary: Чанк описывает социальный подтип E2 как ребенка, который внутренне формирует ощущение способности давать исцеляющую любовь из-за амбивалентной привязанности и иллюзии превосходства над родителями, будучи «хорошим ребенком» в глазах семьи.

title: Детство как единственный ребенок и ощущение избранности
text: My parents conceived me on a train one full moon night. I’m the product of love, the first daughter and granddaughter in my family. I was a baby that was wanted and loved by everyone. For two years, I was the only child, and each person treated me like a queen in their own way, so I, in turn, entertained my subjects.
summary: Чанк повествует о том, как рассказчик была долгожданным первым ребенком и внуком, получала поклонение как «королева» и внутренне принимала роль центра внимания и развлечения для семьи.

title: Динамика предпочтения отца и rivalry с матерью
text:
ANA BAZA

At this stage, a dynamic begins to take shape that will follow them into adulthood, especially in their romantic relationships. If it’s a girl, she may feel like Daddy’s favorite, even more than Mommy, whom she soon starts to see as an equal, and even a rival, for her father’s affection.

My father says he adored me when I was little, that I was his little princess. He hardly ever expresses affection, but when he reminisces about those years, his tone softens: “You were so beautiful... so good…” I feel like he’s always looked at me with admiration.

Most of my life, I’ve felt that I was more important to my father than my mother was, and she definitely noticed that. For example, she would get jealous of how he treated me: “Why does he talk to you so much about things he doesn’t share with me?” Or, when we traveled, my mother would give up the front seat next to my father without me asking, even when I was very young. If there was a problem between them, she would ask me what she should do, or try to manipulate me to get me to convince my father to do something.
summary: Чанк описывает формирующуюся динамику, в которой девочка ощущает себя любимицей отца, видит мать как rivals за отцовское внимание, и как это влияет на семейные отношения и самооценку.

title: Родительские ожидания и отсутствие эмоциональной поддержки
text:
ANA BAZA

In some way, one or both parents place high expectations on them, believing they will become someone important in their life, who will surpass them in status. It doesn’t have to be a financial success, but more often it’s cultural, social, or intellectual. However, these children don’t always receive the emotional support they need along the way. Some social E2s talk about parents who were too distracted, depressed, or frustrated with their child’s emotional needs. Others mention parents who were too busy or just couldn’t tune in to their child’s deeper emotional world. These parents didn’t have the tools to help the child process and understand intense emotional phases. As a result, the child learns early to distract themselves from their suffering, focusing on a facade of being okay, pretending to feel fulfilled, and showing easy enthusiasm.

My mother had such immense confidence in me, and I remember when my friends from school rejected me. I felt like I was dying from the pain. In her attempt to help me, or maybe just to cope with her own discomfort in seeing mine, she told me I had to be indifferent to those “stabs” because I was special and they just couldn’t understand me. She didn’t really hear my pain; instead, she dismissed it, telling me I needed to rise above it: “They’re the ones losing out.” But the truth was, I was the one losing out, and I wasn’t learning to accept my flaws or realize that maybe I wasn’t as perfect as I thought I was.
summary: Чанк объясняет, как родители возлагают на ребенка-E2 высокие ожидания по статусу, но часто не дают эмоциональной поддержки, что приводит к подавлению боли, созданию fachada благополучия и невозможности принять свои недостатки.

title: Эмоциональное оставление матерью и паттерн выживания
text:
ANA BAZA

Abandonment issues and depression

A core wound of the social E2, shared with the E4, is the deep feeling of emotional abandonment by their mother. Although there may be no clear reason for dependence on the father, the mother often adheres to patriarchal values that position the feminine as subordinate to the masculine. In many cases, the mother shoulders the majority of family responsibilities in the father’s absence, without allowing herself the space to care for herself or truly nurture her children.

I always saw my mother as the one I could count on, both for practical support and emotional reassurance—the person who made the important decisions for me and for the family. She worked hard and was financially independent, earning more than my father. She was the pillar of her own family, always there for everyone. Yet, I often felt the sting of unrequited love due to her absence. Despite this, I accepted it, carrying both a deep sense of lack and a strange sense of pride. I learned to cope with this void by adopting the strong woman model she embodied.
summary: Чанк описывает core wound социального E2 — эмоциональное оставление матерью из-за патриархальных установок и её перегрузки, что приводит к внутреннему ощущению недостатка, которое компенсируется идентификацией с моделью сильной женщины.

title: Недостаток эмоциональной связи в раннем детстве и его последствия
text:
LUANA SEVIRIO

Sometimes, the mother becomes ill, works long hours, or is simply absent due to family obligations. In any case, the emotional connection during the child’s early years is insufficient.

By the time I was seven, I had experienced a series of emotional abandonments, each one leaving a deep wound that shaped how I would later form attachments with others.
summary: Чанк подчеркивает, что недостаток эмоциональной связи с матерью в раннем детстве из-за болезни, работы или обстоятельств приводит к серии ран abandonment, которые формируют паттерн привязанности во взрослой жизни.

title: Childhood emotional abandonments
text:
When I was barely six months old, my mother had appendicitis and abruptly stopped breastfeeding me. Before I turned two, we moved away from the house where I had been born, losing much of the connection I had with my grandmother and aunt, who had spoiled me. When I was three, my mother’s younger brother died suddenly in a car accident, and the entire family spiraled into grief, leaving little room for me. At four and a half, my brother was born, and I saw him as nothing more than a nuisance. He peed, pooped, and “stole” my mother’s attention. Then, when I was seven, my father left the house to “save the world.”

I don’t remember anyone being there to care for me or help me navigate through those wounds.
summary: This chunk describes a series of childhood emotional abandonments experienced by the narrator, including early weaning, moving away from extended family, uncle's death, sibling birth, and father's departure, which shaped their attachment wounds.

title: Childhood depression and attachment struggles in social E2s
text:
ANA BAZA

The childhood wound of social E2s manifests as a form of childhood depression, resembling what is known as anaclitic depression, which disrupts their emotional growth. The typical process of separation after the first year of life is not smooth for them, turning what should be a natural shift into a painful loss. As a result, they struggle with separations in adulthood, and they often seek validation through relationships to fill this void.

The emotional pain experienced as a child during attachment formation makes it difficult for them to build and maintain deep connections in adulthood, including friendships. This often leads to an existential paradox: despite knowing many people and being part of various social circles, they remain fundamentally lonely. This difficulty turns social E2s into individualists who deeply crave connection but struggle with the idea of letting go.

I’ve always known a lot of people, but I’ve had very few real friends, and maintaining those friendships has been incredibly difficult for me. Either I distanced myself, or they just disappeared. I never connected it to abandonment. It was as if they simply vanished, just like my father did. Whenever I lost someone, I felt a strange ambivalence. On one hand, I became emotionally numb, unable to fully grasp what I did wrong or what might have upset them. It was almost like playing dumb gave me an excuse. The reasons they left? Overstepping boundaries, being intrusive, impulsive or risky behaviors, selfishness, arrogance.
summary: This chunk explains how the childhood wound of social E2s leads to anaclitic-like depression, impaired attachment, and chronic loneliness in adulthood despite social engagement, illustrated by the narrator's personal experience with fleeting friendships and emotional numbness after loss.

title: Need for reimagined maternal bond and fear of abandonment
text:
ANA BAZA

What they seek emotionally is a reimagined version of the close, fusion-like bond typical of mother-child in early childhood—an unspoken emotional dependence. This leads to a constant need for validation and, though often hidden, a deep desire to feel truly loved.

After a painful breakup with my partner, I became acutely aware of my overwhelming need for love. What resurfaced was that deep-seated fear tied to survival; I was confronted with my most basic need and the ancient fear of being unable to provide for my own survival, or for my child.

ILARIA FACCIOLI

I think there’s always been a silent scream inside me, one that I’m ashamed to even voice: “Will someone please take care of me!”
summary: This chunk describes the social E2's unconscious longing for a symbiotic mother-child bond, leading to dependency and fear of abandonment, illustrated by personal testimonies of seeking care and voicing a silent plea for nurturance.

title: Grandiosity as a defense in social E2 childhood
text:
ANA BAZA

Grandiosity

In the childhood of a social E2, emotional support from their parents is scarce. They quickly learn how to get attention, but at the same time, they abandon the fundamental need to share and understand their emotions, as well as to receive help with their problems.

I remember feeling deeply afraid at times of being left alone because my mother often fainted due to anemia. There were several occasions when she collapsed to the floor, and I didn’t know what to do. I always managed to figure it out, but it left me with the sense that I had to solve things on my own and rely only on myself.

ANA BAZA

Often, as a way to receive emotional support, this child becomes the confidant of one of the parents. It is often the mother who relies on them, not just for practical matters, but also for emotional support within the family—even in matters concerning her romantic relationships. Sometimes, they are treated differently from their siblings in family decisions. The child accepts this responsibility, thinking it makes them special, interpreting it as a form of love that, although not truly nurturing, provides them with a sense of warmth. Over time, this turns into pride—an illusion of importance that fills the emotional void. This paradoxical situation forces the child to develop a fantasy of grandiosity, building the illusion of having extraordinary abilities—the strength to bear the weight of responsibility, the belief that they are indispensable within the family. These illusions are reinforced by manipulative messages from their parents, who play into this fantasy.

My mother always had complete confidence in me—too much confidence, I would say. When my father left home, I was seven years old. From that moment, my life changed. My mother confided in me about her relationship with my father, even about their sex life. We did the household finances together. She asked for my ‘advice’ on how to handle my younger brother. I even taught him English… She leaned on me completely, and I felt so important, so proud to be that valuable to her.
summary: This chunk explains how emotional neglect in social E2 childhood leads to parentification and grandiosity, where the child earns emotional validation by becoming a parental confidant and taking on adult roles, fostering a false sense of indispensability and pride.

title: Parental imposition of grandeur and performance-based love
text:
ANA BAZA

At the same time, one of the parents imposes their own dream of personal grandeur onto their child, which may or may not have a specific direction. This expectation often manifests implicitly in everyday life or may be expressed in vague terms, such as: “You must become a... or a... great person in some way.” Regardless, the child feels compelled to fulfill this mandate, driven by the parent’s need to satisfy their own ideal. Behind this request lies the narcissistic desire to brag about the child or the fear of not being able to live up to their own ideal as a parent.

When I took my final exam in high school, I was the second person to finish. When I stood up and walked away, to the astonishment of all the professors, the rest of the class stood up too. “But you’re the leader!” one of the professors exclaimed. The moment caught me by surprise, but at the same time, it filled me with pride for the triumph.
summary: This chunk describes how parents project their own grandiose ideals onto the social E2 child, creating pressure to perform and excel, which the child internalizes as a condition for love, as illustrated by the narrator's pride in academic recognition.

title: Влияние родительских ожиданий и манипуляций на ребенка-E2
text: If I was afraid or shy about something, she would get upset and tell me I had to be brave. If something surprised or impressed me, she would get angry and remind me that someone like me should be above such things. I often felt how she showcased me in front of her friends. She, an E4, would constantly put herself down, despite being an incredibly capable, strong, dedicated, and determined woman—except when she was proud of me.
summary: Описывает динамику в отношениях ребенка с матерью-E4, которая требует смелости и превосходства, одновременно демонстрируя ребенка перед другими, несмотря на собственную склонность к самокритике.

title: Изоляция и поиск принадлежности у социального E2
text:
ANA BAZA

The king in search of territory

The conditional love they learned to depend on, combined with emotional distance from their siblings and a subtle competition with either of the parents, leads social E2s to feel deeply isolated. They don’t experience a true sense of belonging, and they struggle to find a real place in the family.

The need to take on a role that isn’t theirs, that of an adult, becomes the push for this subtype to continue searching for a place in the world that matches their expectations, with the hidden desire to fill the void of not being seen or loved for who they truly are. They were a child who could intuitively sense the needs of their parents and act accordingly. Sometimes, it even felt like they had magical abilities, able to understand the needs of others before recognizing their own.

Among the painful experiences they keep hidden from others is a deep sense of shame over one of their parents’ behavior, which, in some way, threatens their social image.

I remember feeling embarrassed by my mother’s behavior in social situations from a very young age. I thought she was an amazing woman, but also a little odd, eccentric. Now, I understand why I didn’t like her dramatic displays (she was a social E2 too). It was unbearable to watch her behave so theatrically, just to prove to herself and others that she deserved admiration. I felt such sadness and embarrassment in front of my friends. So, I would try to change the topic by doing something else: I’d come up with a fun game or tell a funny joke, hoping they’d forget the situation that was making me uncomfortable. I was terrified that they’d see how I was really feeling in that moment.

LUANA SEVIRIO
summary: Описывает глубинную изоляцию социального E2 из-за условной любви и родительских ожиданий, чувство стыда за поведение родителей и попытки скрыть собственное неудобство в социальных ситуациях через юмор или отвлечение.

title: Травма стыда и компенсаторное поведение у социального E2
text:
Shame related to something involving them and self-devaluation are deeply traumatic for the social E2 child, and these experiences stay with them throughout their life. It is these hidden, unrecognized moments—often overlooked by adults—that lead them to seek narcissistic compensation. As children, they often act older than their years, and as adults, their relationships tend to be strategic, with a strong focus on intellectual pursuits.

Most of the time, they were children physically larger than their peers and siblings, with a bigger appetite. In comparison to their siblings, they are often seen as “the best,” the one who meets their parents’ expectations most consistently, which is publicly acknowledged, making them feel a pressure to perform at a very high level.

My brother was always the one with problems, no matter his age. My mother always defended him, even when he was indefensible. Meanwhile, I was the one expected to be exactly what my parents wanted me to be. They saw me as strong, I felt strong, and I proved it—even at the expense of my own well-being. I drank excessively, not to party or get drunk, but to show how much I could endure.

MAURIZIO MARTELLI
summary: Описывает долгосрочное влияние стыда и самоунижения на социального E2, приводящее к нарциссической компенсации, гиперответственности, взрослому поведению в детстве и самопожертвованию, включая вредные привычки как доказательство силы.

title: Персона и тень: идеализация себя и подавление недостатков у социального E2
text:
Persona and shadow: destructive to themselves and others

The social E2 wants to be a hero, and they believe they have everything in their favor to achieve it. They’ve constructed a persona made entirely of light, banishing anything they consider unworthy, inadequate, or dark into the shadow. No flaw that might diminish their value is left exposed. If one emerges, they’ll either project it onto others, deny it, or justify it with relentless fervor.

Maintaining such an elevated persona forces them to hide, behind a façade of decisive control, aspects like envy, rivalry, resentment, fear of making mistakes, and a deep sense of not belonging. This leaves them feeling very isolated.

As a hero, not only do they believe in their own power but also that they can abuse it to achieve an end they’ll dress up as a noble, common goal. For the social E2, everything becomes a power struggle, one they’re determined to win, regardless of the harm caused or the relationships lost (which they cannot understand when it happens). They are very skilled at concealing or denying their failures, as they cannot bear to admit, even to themselves, that they are unable to accomplish everything they set out to do.

The emotional highs and lows for this subtype resemble an intense wave, followed by an equally powerful crash—an exhilarating self-exaltation followed by a deep depletion. Their actions are frantic, compulsive, and devoid of risk assessment. Their goal is always to push further.

Even their spontaneity is used manipulatively, aiming to impress and win others’ consent and attention. Deep down, this personality avoids truly revealing themselves: their desire for perfection prevents them from showing who they fear they really are. They show the rose while hiding the thorns.

It’s difficult for others to see them as emotionally involved in the competition. They want to dominate but without “getting their hands dirty.” They don’t like to experience the emotions that may arise from open competition, as that would force them to confront envy or fear.

When the social E2 feels threatened in their self-esteem, they distort reality and let their aggression show, using it to mask their sadness and restore a sense of well-being.
summary: Описывает конструкцию персоны социального E2 как идеализированного героя, подавление тени (зависть, страх, resentment), манипулятивное использование спонтанности, эмоциональные колебания между экзальтацией и истощением, и защитную агрессию при угрозе самооценке.

title: Личный опыт социального E2: подавленная уязвимость и конфликт в отношениях
text: Sooner or later, the moment comes when my repressed vulnerability demands to have its moment and inevitably surfaces, since my strength is not as limitless as my narcissism would like to believe. Over the course of my life, I have especially tried to keep this hidden in the private sphere of my partner and family, aggressively demanding my needs and blaming others with punitive reproaches where I once “lovingly surrendered.” This behavior has caused immense confusion for those around me, particularly for my daughter, who has endured my unpredictable outbursts following moments of tenderness since she was a child.
summary: Автор описывает, как подавленная уязвимость социального E2 прорывается наружу, вызывая эмоциональные вспышки и конфликты в близких отношениях, особенно с дочерью, из-за непоследовательного поведения между нежностью и агрессией.

title: Рационализация боли и самообман у социального E2
text:
ALBA ARENA

The social E2 often justifies what they feel deeply is painful, especially when they perceive it as unjust to them. They shift from their emotional experience to what they believe would be the fair response, compensating for their feelings of inferiority and inadequacy in the process.

I threw myself into situations with full commitment and self-sacrifice, convinced that there was no other way and that my actions were necessary for the good of the community. But when I was later forced to step away, not by my choice, I was met with a crushing sense of self-devaluation and thoughts of how others would disqualify me. Instead of feeling enthusiasm and grandeur, I was depressed. Instead of generosity, I felt like a thief.
summary: Социальный E2 оправдывает боль через рационализацию, заменяя真实 чувства на «справедливый» ответ, что приводит к эмоциональному истощению и чувству вины при отказе от участия, несмотря на прежнюю самоотверженность.

title: Потребность в связи и самопредательство у социального E2
text:
LUANA SEVIRIO

This character lacks reserve, carefulness, and a sense of moderation. They don’t like to keep secrets, as their need for connection with others outweighs any consideration of timing or relevance. In revealing confidences that others have entrusted to them, seduced by the closeness they create, they expose their lack of intimacy, unaware of their betrayal. They don’t understand what trust truly means or believe in it. The result is that they harm themselves, deepening their sense of loneliness and lack of trust in others, while still claiming to offer “generous and friendly love.”

Their need to seduce individuals or groups is less about wanting to be liked and more about devouring the object of their seduction. This is an oral-receptive personality. Although it’s unlikely for this subtype to become obese, they are often large individuals with a rather self-destructive attitude toward food, using it not for pleasure but to fill the emptiness they feel once they make contact with it. They may even deny themselves food, as a way to reject their basic needs, or as a paradoxical act of revenge, depriving themselves of the connection to life that food symbolizes.

When they’re not the center of attention, a sense of loneliness sets in. That’s why they surround themselves with many people, even though they feel like they’re alone. The approval of others becomes their lifeline, a buffer against the intense loneliness and desolation.

They are hypersensitive to criticism and dislike being challenged. The need for admiration and the rejection of criticism are their attempts to maintain their self-esteem, which, despite appearances, is actually quite fragile.

They’re unaware of how they exploit others because they justify it with the higher purpose of fulfilling a common mission. They also fail to recognize their emotional exploitation when involving others in their projects or seducing them with their ability to help—doing so to feed their self-image as benevolent and to feel needed by others.

They position themselves as spokespersons for others’ unspoken desires, with an enthusiasm that generates warmth both within themselves and in those around them.
summary: Социальный E2 стремится к связи любой ценой, предаловерив доверие, используя еду и внимание как заменители эмоционального питания, и остается неосознающим своей эксплуатации других, оправдывая ее высшей целью, при этом испытывая глубокое одиночество несмотря на окружение людьми.

title: Детская травма и потеря себя в служении другим
text:
Since I was little, I never felt seen or loved. As the youngest of three siblings, I always sought affection by helping others and making myself indispensable, going above and beyond with my altruism. I gave up my childhood: I became my mother’s helper, the daughter she had always wanted.

ANTONIO MESSIA

The social E2 disconnects affection from their awareness, making it impossible for them to fully experience both the cognitive and emotional aspects of an event, leaving them isolated from each other.

When I devoted myself to a spiritual growth project, I poured all my time and energy into it. I didn’t realize then how much I was neglecting my children and family. It was only much later, during a long period of inactivity, that I finally saw it.
summary: Автор описывает детскую стратегие заработания любви через служение, приведшую к потере себя и эмоциональной диссоциации, когда осознание пренебрежения близкими приходит лишь спустя годы.

title: Зависимости как способ избежания боли у социального E2
text:
LUANA SEVIRIO

One of the social E2’s most common ways of self-destructing is through various addictions—whether it’s television, social media, food, sex, or drugs. However, their greatest indulgence is work addiction, which allows them to bury their emotional life, self-care, and enjoyment, disrupting the flow of their consciousness. By suppressing their needs, they continue to ignore them. And when they finally realize they’ve neglected both themselves and their loved ones, they punish themselves by feeling unworthy and contemptible. They’ve sold their soul to their profession. For them, life becomes a constant race against time, with no satisfaction lasting more than a fleeting moment—just enough to catch their breath before diving into the next project. This addiction helps them deny the pain that arises when they face the emptiness or depressive feelings lurking beneath the surface of their character.

The people around them, whether in their professional or personal lives, get swept up in their whirlwind, where there is no real exchange and no space for a voice that doesn’t feed their need for attention. The social E2 invades the lives of others like an unstoppable force. In a team, it’s less about collaboration and more about having a team at their disposal. The result for those around them is a pervasive sense of inadequacy, annihilation, and alarm. Their internal and external “rush” ensures that no one truly gets to know them or can stand in the way of their plans for expansion.
summary: Социальный E2 использует работу и другие зависимости, чтобы избежать confrontation с внутренней пустотой и болью, что приводит к истощению,'exploitation близких и иллюзии продуктивности, при этом усугубляя одиночество и самоотвращение.

title: Фасад свободы и ложная мораль социального E2
text: Like the other two subtypes, the social E2 may appear confident and free, but that’s just a façade. In reality, their freedom is illusory, as is their supposed courage. The actions with any social impact and displays of bravery are fueled by a lack of awareness about how they navigate the world. What drives their behavior is, above all, frustration with rules. It could be said that they create an ad hoc personalized moral code, with rules and values changing depending on the situation. This isn’t about self-indulgence, as in the E7, nor is it about rationalizing guilt as an E6 would do. Instead, these are logical justifications where the social E2 only confronts themselves, and others don’t exist as autonomous people. It’s a self-referential morality built to optimize the functionality of their neurotic agenda. The result of this process is the validation of their own logic, rather than an objective examination of reality. This leads them to avoid questioning themselves, ultimately falling into a delusion of omnipotence.
summary: Описывает иллюзорную свободу и ложную смелость социального E2, их фрустрацию из-за правил, создание ситуативного морального кодекса и самореференциальную логику, ведущую к заблуждению всемогущества.

title: Примитивные защиты и инструментализация других
text: The formation and upkeep of these strategies rely on primitive defense mechanisms, such as splitting the negative self-representations of themselves from positive ones, projecting their own negative traits onto others, and subsequently devaluing people and relationships that don’t serve their project of self-aggrandizement. The other person is an object, a tool to be used according to what they need to advance their agenda.
summary: Объясняет, как социальный E2 использует примитивные защитные механизмы (расщепление, проекция, обесценивание) и рассматривает других как инструменты для самоутверждения.

title: Страх уязвимости и внутренний ребёнок
text:
Their high expectations and the self-image they’ve constructed prevent them from freely revealing their limitations, vulnerability, or needs. This includes the act of seeking support, care, or protection, which would risk diminishing their social image and tarnishing their idealized self-image—an outcome they find too painful to bear. Beneath the grandeur lies a child who was never allowed to be a child, someone who grew up concealing their humiliating smallness.

I was afraid people would see my lack. So, I had to always be at my best, hiding the pain and exhaustion. I thought, “Others come before me.” This served to create a toxic form of emotional dependence.

ANTONIO MESSIA

The denial of vulnerability is a patriarchal trait of the ambitious social E2, someone who always wants to be at the top and never asks for help. In doing so, they suppress feelings of inadequacy that would undermine their self-exaltation. It’s the trap of false abundance, which, over time, turns against them on an intrapsychic level, leaving them with a painful sense of deprivation.

When the circumstances no longer require me to manage everything, I find myself sinking into a state of depression, both physically and mentally, which I fear and do everything I can to conceal.

ALBA ARENA
summary: Описывает, как высокие ожидания и идеализированный образ мешают социальному E2 проявлять уязвимость, что скрывает внутреннего ребёнка, лишённого детства; включает личные testimonies о страхе быть увиденным в недостатке и депрессии при потере контроля.

title: Стремление к совершенству и саморазрушительные установки
text:
Intolerant of mediocrity, their passion is tied to their sense of personal triumph. For someone as special as they are, there is no life without excellence, which often pushes them into self-destructive situations. Life’s game becomes about betting on a winning horse.

For many years, I had two dominant thoughts. The first was: “I’ll achieve it no matter what; I’ll be independent and won’t need anyone.” And the second: “I wish I could die so I could make them pay for it.” These two conflicting thoughts have accompanied me throughout my life: on one hand, success; on the other, the possibility of losing everything, throwing it all away.

The first time I went to Paris and saw the clochards under the bridges, I was twenty years old, and I felt a deep emotion. I was them; their eyes were mine. They had rejected everything, while I was the model student, sure that I would find my way in life. I felt as though my life could have unfolded in either direction, and that both paths were a part of me.

TERESA MOSCA
summary: Описывает нетерпимость к посредственности, связь страсти с личным триумфом, двойственные установки на успех и саморазрушение, а также личный опыт Терезы Moska, увидевшей в бездомных своё альтернативное 'я'.

title: Импульсивность и хроническое одиночество
text:
Another way their destructive tendencies manifest is through impulsivity.

There were many times when I thought I could have become a homeless person. To live a life where nothing has value, or to throw away everything I once considered valuable. I often experience regret for things I might say or do when I’m swept up in the waves of emotion.

LUANA SEVIRIO

The primary experience of loneliness is constantly renewed as they repeatedly encounter it throughout their life. They replace the bitterness and pain they’ve felt with a constant stream of new goals, which, at least in their idealized fantasy, offer them the illusion of fulfillment and strength. The persistence of infantile attitudes, such as the behavior of a child who sucks and bites, defines the destructive nature of the social E2.
summary: Описывает импульсивность как проявление деструктивных тенденций социального E2, включая мысли о брошенной жизни и раскаяние; далее — хроническое одиночество, замещение боли новыми целями и сохранение инфантильных установок.

title: Отношения как территория контроля и выгода
text:
As is evident, the world of relationships and love is deeply damaged and impoverished in the social E2, who uses them to attack and self-destruct. They are afraid of surrendering, losing control, and confronting their own inner chaos. If they do experience these emotions, they quickly push them aside. They present themselves as rigid, uncompromising, and perfectionistic, particularly with their family and loved ones.

Their strong elitism makes them very selective about who they consider part of their inner circle. In their arrogance, they believe it’s normal for others to want to be their friends, yet they struggle to understand what these people could actually offer them.

They are territorial, possessive, and highly utilitarian—qualities that are the exact opposite of love, which makes maintaining lasting friendships very difficult. The overwhelming workload they impose on themselves leaves them with little time to nurture or care for friendships. As a result, they might keep relationships at a distance, but it becomes nearly impossible to sustain on a day-to-day basis. To put it metaphorically, they treat platonic love the same way they treat plants: a social E2 typically doesn’t keep them because they either suffocate them or let them die of thirst.
summary: Описывает, как социальный E2 повреждает мир отношений, используя их для саморушения, избегая уязвимости и контроля; проявляет ригидность, элитизм и утилитаризм в дружбе, что делает её неустойчивой из-за перегрузки и территориальности.

title: Сложности в установлении стабильных связей у социального E2
text:
For them, establishing solid, stable bonds is difficult—and they see this as very dangerous on an internal level. They’ve long forgotten any need for love, partly because they are ashamed of showing vulnerability, tenderness, or neediness. Submitting to another’s affection is also hard.

In their “false” need for independence, they struggle greatly to form egalitarian relationships. By trying to position themselves as indispensable, the one in charge, or the most capable, they inevitably push others away, exhausted from living under the emperor’s tyranny. This only perpetuates their sense of not belonging and deepens their internal feeling of loneliness.

The hardest harm for them to acknowledge is how they place others in an inferior position by making their own greatness unattainable. At the same time, by transferring their emotional needs to the other person—who is weakened and dependent—they trap them in a double bind: “I help you so that you are satisfied, perfect, and happy, as I know how, on the condition that you will always need me and see me as greater than you.”
summary: Описывает внутренние барьеры социального E2 в построении близких отношений: страх уязвимости, потребность в контроле, создание двойной зависимости и избегание равенства в связях.

title: Отношение социального E2 к сексуальности и интимности
text:
The topic of love will be discussed in the following chapter, but it’s worth briefly mentioning the social E2’s relationship with sexuality. Their difficulty with surrender and trust makes this area feel incredibly dangerous, if not unnecessary, as they believe there are more important things to focus on. Two seemingly opposite situations may arise, but in fact, they are not contradictory. Either their fear of sexuality prevents them from engaging in intimate relationships, or their fear of intimacy leads to compulsive sexual behavior. In other words, they either deny it or use sex as a tool for manipulation. The real goal is to avoid entering into an emotional and intimate relationship, something that would leave them defenseless, losing control of the situation and of themselves on an emotional level.

The social E2 is, ultimately, a defenseless child disguised as a giant, emotionally and behaviorally wreaking havoc wherever they go, destroying any possibility of loving selflessly or being loved. Their ultimate revenge takes the form of attacking and ruthlessly harming themselves, denying themselves any form of love in order to avoid ever feeling used, betrayed, excluded, or abandoned again; the heart doesn’t suffer if it’s never even given the chance to feel.
summary: Объясняет, как страх утраты контроля приводит к избеганию или манипулятивному использованию сексуальности, а также описывает социального E2 как человека, разрушающего свои отношения из-за глубокой травмы.

title: Клинические иллюстрации и работа с эмоциями у социального E2
text:
Brief clinical illustrations

For a social E2, it’s essential to recognize the disorder in regulating self-esteem. The grandiose self is maintained through narcissistic investments, which prevent the development of a healthy, integrated superego aligned with the self’s ideals. As we’ve witnessed throughout this book, the pride expressed by the Two is an attempt to cover up feelings of insecurity related to their self-esteem. Proud individuals share the tendency to eliminate or overly compensate for feelings of inferiority and inadequacy, traits that are more prominent in the Four.

Asking for help is difficult for me—I view it as a sign of weakness. I often project my needs onto others, which makes me feel better because it allows me to avoid confronting them. Since I started participating in the SAT, I’ve begun to recognize these needs.

MAURIZIO MARTELLI

Anger, which this personality has no trouble recognizing and expressing, can act as a parasitic emotion, masking and distorting sadness. It’s useful to seize the opportunity when it arises to probe into it deeper.

As for the feeling of excited joy, it may serve as a defense mechanism, often linked to intellectualization and strategic thinking, used to avoid confronting a challenge one is reluctant to face.

This subtype would benefit from being more in touch with their deeper experiences, with the body that speaks and reveals the truth. Staying present in the here and now is the only antidote to the intellectualizations and self-affirmations used to soothe the inner turmoil.
summary: Представляет клинические примеры и терапевтические insights: проблемы с самооценкой, гнев как маску печали, радость как защиту, и необходимость телесной осознанности для преодоления интеллектуализации.

title: Особенности проявления любви у Twos и социального E2
text:
Love

Twos thrive on touch, laughter, playful teasing, and deep eye contact, creating an almost magical atmosphere. Being around an E2 feels like a promise—an unspoken assurance that something profound is about to unfold. And in a way, it does, because for this character, every connection is an attempt to recreate the primal bond with their mother, a subconscious effort to mend the deep wound of loneliness they carry in their heart. But this kind of intensity has a downside: it burns too brightly to last. It’s more of a thrill than a steady, enduring emotion.

The social E2 makes promises they don’t keep. The intensity they spark is bound to fizzle out. In general, Twos give more than they promise and promise more than they give. Though they invest heavily in relationships, they’re inconsistent and superficial. Instead of following an upward spiral where meaningful connections are gradually cultivated, deepened, and nurtured, their relationships are marked by dramatic highs followed by equally dramatic lows.

As dealers in parental love they never truly received, social E2s construct an idealized version of it. They maneuver relationships in a way that positions them as a mentor or guide, hoping to “buy” admiration and devotion. They long to be adored the way a child longs for unconditional love. To fulfill this desire, they pour their energy into grand visions and ambitious projects, presenting themselves as leaders who know the way forward. They generously share their ambitions with their “children,” expecting gratitude and loyalty in return—measured through obedience and unwavering support, all of which serves to reinforce their own sense of importance.
summary: Описывает, как Twos (особенно социальные E2) выражают любовь через интенсивность и идеализацию, но сталкиваются с нестабильностью 관계 из-за скрытой потребности в одобрении и контроле.

title: Ранние влияния родителей и цикл разочарований в любви у социального E2
text: One or both parents projected their own unmet needs onto them, offering a love that was manipulative, transactional, and conditional. As a result, every relationship they build carries these same three components. They chase after a version of unconditional love they believe once existed, but that remains forever out of reach. This fuels a cycle of constant disappointment, expressed through passive punishment and emotional withdrawal—a form of revenge that ultimately condemns them to a life devoid of real love.
summary: Описывается, как манипулятивная и условная любовь родителей формирует у социального E2 паттерн отношений, основанный на поиске недостижимой безусловной любви, что ведет к циклу разочарований и эмоциональному отстранению.

title: Анализ форм любви у социального E2 по Клаудио Наранхо
text:
The three types of love

According to Claudio Naranjo, the Two, as an emotionally driven personality, represents compassionate love—the nurturing love of a mother. However, the social E2 leans more toward admiring love, a common trait among many social subtypes, while struggling to fully embody both compassionate and erotic love.

That said, their version of admiring love differs from the kind Naranjo describes—“a love for God or abstract aspects like beauty, music, or art.” On the contrary, their focus is on impressing others and being worshipped, elevating their own image to that of a revered patriarch. In the social Two, admiring love takes on two distorted forms. Unable to surrender to anything greater than themselves, they direct admiration inward, turning it into self-worship. At the same time, they excessively idealize those they want to win over—not out of genuine appreciation, but as a way to soak in the admiration reflected back at them.
summary: Обсуждается, как социальный E2 проявляет сострадательную, восхищающую и эротическую любовь, но искажает восхищающую любовь через самовосхищение и идеализацию других как способ получения отраженной admiration.

title: Отсутствие upward-ориентированной любви и корни в детстве у социального E2
text: What social E2s lack is a love that looks beyond the self—one that aspires upward, toward something greater. This often stems from growing up without a model of authentic love between their parents. Having taken on an adult role too early, they never learned how to admire others; instead, they learned to seek admiration. They are essentially children playing at being adults and authority figures.
summary: Социальный E2 не способен на любовь, направленную на что-то большее себя, из-за отсутствия примера здоровой родительской любви и premature взросления, что приводит к поиску admiration вместо умения искренне восхищаться.

title: Желание быть обожаемым и страх перед эротической близостью у социального E2
text:
This longing for admiring love drives them to cultivate an image as charismatic, intense, and inherently good. More than anything, they desire to be adored by others—to be respected leaders who are followed out of love rather than fear.

Eros belongs to the realm of instinct, something social E2s find difficult to embrace. Sexuality forces them to confront an unsettling truth: their own animal nature. Disconnected from their core self, they carry an unspoken sense of sexual shame, struggling to accept the parts of themselves that reveal their dependence on others and remind them of their humanity.

Despite their natural allure, they resist fully surrendering to pleasure, especially to intimacy. This is because they associate deep love with ultimate betrayal. As children, they once experienced this ecstatic sense of unity, only to later be abandoned. That kind of love now feels dangerous, a forbidden place they dare not return to. The fear of being exposed at such a deep level is unbearable, so social E2s avoid intimacy altogether, shielding themselves from the painful echoes of past loss. In many ways, that early wound signified the death of an essential part of them—the ability to give freely and the belief that they are worthy of love.
summary: Социальный E2 стремится к обожанию как замене материнской любви, но избегает сексуальной и эмоциональной близости из-за травмы предательства в детстве, связывая глубокую любовь с опасностью и потерей себя.

title: Потенциал исцеления через восстановление связи с сексуальностью у социального E2
text: For the social E2, reconnecting with their sexuality could be a gateway to healing. Approaching it as an act of both play and self-love may help them begin to shed their emotional armor, let go of control, and embrace their most intimate needs without fear.
summary: Восстановление связи с сексуальностью представлено как путь к исцелению для социального E2, позволяющий снизить защитные механизмы и принять свою уязвимость через игру и самолюбовь.

title: Искаженная сострадательная любовь у социального E2: эмпатия как инструмент контроля
text:
In social E2s, compassionate love is deeply skewed—always exaggerated and transactional. While they possess remarkable empathy and generosity, their kindness is laced with subtle manipulation. Their gestures may stem from sincerity, but the ego quickly twists them into opportunities—tools for securing something in return. At that point, their compassion is neither pure nor selfless.

Though they have a keen ability to recognize the light in others, they wield it as a means of control—offering excessive flattery to foster loyalty and create a sense of indebtedness, gathering followers.

They struggle to show compassion because their relentless self-demand leaves little room for recognizing vulnerability—either in themselves or others. Admitting to fragility or mistakes would require an unsettling openness of heart, a risk they’re unwilling to take. To shield themselves, they maintain a quiet but persistent anger, keeping them trapped in a state of harsh judgment toward everything and everyone. This contempt is a defense mechanism, and by devaluing others, they distance themselves from both the divine and the profoundly human.

They do feel the suffering of others, but rather than embracing it with true presence, they distort it into a dramatic display—a performance shaped by their hyper-emotional nature. The only real way forward is through the dark night of the soul: surrendering to pain, acknowledging lack, and facing their own limitations and vulnerability without resistance.
summary: Социальный E2 проявляет эмпатию и щедрость, но искажает их через манипуляцию и потребность в контроле, используя похвалу и драматизацию чужих страданий для получения признания, избегая настоящей уязвимости.

title: Личная история о боли, сдаче и внезапном опыте безусловной любви
text: I was in the hospital, heavily sedated on morphine. The pain had become so unbearable that even the act of breathing was excruciating. They had removed half of my lung, and when they took out the tubes, I suffered a pneumothorax, so I had to undergo another surgery. They wheeled me down to the operating room and left me on a stretcher in a freezing cold room. I was alone for what felt like an eternity. Fear gripped me. The pain was so overwhelming that, for the first time in my life, the idea of surrendering to death didn’t just seem appealing—it felt like something I deeply wanted.
summary: Автор делится личным опытом сильной физической боли и эмоционального отчаяния в больнице, дошедшего до мысли о желаемой смерти из-за невыносимых страданий.

title: Опыт уязвимости и сострадания
text: Then, as if my hand belonged to someone else, I reached up and stroked my own face, murmuring to myself like a mother soothing a child. “Poor thing, poor Ana…” I whispered. And suddenly, something warm and impossibly gentle opened up inside me. A soft light surrounded me. Maybe it was the morphine, or the anesthesia—though it was only local—but in that moment, I felt my body grow weightless, my mind utterly still. There was no fear, no emotion, only quiet. A vast and boundless love filled me, yet emptied me at the same time. Nothing mattered anymore except the silent embrace of compassion that held me. I had never felt anything like it before.
summary: Автор описывает глубокий личный опыт внезапного сострадания к себе, возникший в состоянии уязвимости после операции, когда боль и лекарства создали условия для ощущения безусловной любви и внутренней пустоты одновременно.

title: Социальные E2 в отношениях: иллюзия равенства и скрытая конкуренция
text:
ANA BAZA

Social E2s are capable of building supportive relationships and expressing love through reciprocity, but their generosity is never without an agenda. Their underlying neurosis prevents them from truly accepting care or attention, or from cultivating relationships where maternal love takes precedence. Instead, they project their deepest need for affection onto others.

Romantic relationships

In romantic relationships, the social E2 may seem the least dependent of the Twos, but in reality, they are counter-dependent. Rather than seeking intimacy, they crave recognition for their special qualities and, in one way or another, end up making themselves indispensable to their partner.

The social E2 presents the illusion of an equal partnership, but in truth, what they want is followers. They struggle with true reciprocity, and romantic relationships are no exception. They see themselves as stronger, smarter, faster, more resourceful, and more capable. To prove this, they unconsciously turn the relationship into a competition—one that only ends when their partner submits, leaving them in a position of superiority. They achieve this through control, strategic foresight, hyper-organization, and the ability to seize every opportunity. Over time, their partner is left feeling inadequate, clumsy, slow—never quite good enough. This inevitably creates an emotional distance and a dynamic of inequality. The power structure is set.

At some point in the relationship, the social E2 begins molding their partner to fit their ideal, subtly smoothing out any perceived flaws. If their partner makes a mistake or expresses any disagreement, they may adopt a patronizing tone, like a mother correcting a child, or launch into a passionate, emotionally manipulative verbal battle until their partner gives in, either out of conviction or sheer exhaustion.
summary: Описывается, как социальные E2 строят отношения, маскируя свою зависимость под независимость, стремясь к признанию и превосходству, превращая партнерство в соревнование, где они доминируют через контроль и манипуляции, оставляя партнера чувствующим себя недостаточно хорошим.

title: Личное признание: власть через вину и обесценивание
text:
I wield an almost imperceptible power, and if it’s even slightly questioned, I react with anger, condescension, and offense, as if to say, “How dare you question me?” And then, I turn the tables, trying to make the other person feel guilty: “After everything I’ve done for you…” Since I project an image of self-sufficiency, as if I need nothing, I make them feel worthless. I reinforce this by subtly devaluing whatever they offer me.

With my partner, I went through a whole process of stripping away his masculinity, his power, only to look at him with quiet contempt and say, “You’re not good enough for me,” making him feel unworthy and ultimately, despising him.
summary: Автор признаётся в бессознательном использовании вины и обесценивания как инструментов контроля в отношениях, демонстрируя, как социальные E2 undermining партнера, чтобы укрепить собственное чувство превосходства и самодостаточности.

title: Император/Императрица в быту: организация вместо заботы
text:
ANA BAZA

It’s behind closed doors where the emperor—or empress—truly reveals themselves, assuming the role of a gifted, entitled ruler, preoccupied with far more important matters than the “hustle and bustle” of running a household. They offer a fatherly kind of love, but not the warmth or tenderness of a maternal love. What they truly enjoy is organizing, planning, designing, and, above all, orchestrating—telling others what needs to be done and how it should be done. It may seem like they’re the backbone of the household, but in reality, they delegate the actual domestic labor to those around them.

When guests come over, however, it’s a different story. Social E2s find creative ways to impress and dazzle their visitors, even if it means spending hours preparing or subjecting those closest to them to countless perfectionist demands—all for the sake of their public image.

They’re highly possessive and territorial, so if they feel threatened in any way, they will deploy every tool at their disposal: charm, persuasion, seduction—anything to win the other person back. This applies to friendships as well. If they allow themselves to truly feel the pain of loss, they will first react with disbelief—then with devastation.

The social E2 harbors a childlike resentment, where even the slightest dissent feels like a betrayal. This deep-seated distrust often manifests as silent retaliation—through coldness, cynicism, distance, or quiet disdain. The empress and emperor are in constant need of validation of their worth and superiority. To secure this, they expect their partner to make sacrifices as proof of love, sometimes subtly pushing them to abandon passions, hobbies, or even personal aspirations.
summary: Описывается, как социальные E2 проявляют себя в домашней жизни: предпочитают контроль и организацию заботе, используют общественное признание как источник самооценки, реагируют на угрозы своей территориальности и требуют жертв от партнера как доказательства лояльности.

title: Парадокс присутствия и отсутствия в романтике: лояльность родителям vs партнеру
text: In romantic relationships, the social E2 exists in a paradoxical state—both present and absent. Something within them prevents them from fully surrendering or making a deep, sincere committment. This stems from a fundamental internal conflict: a subconscious loyalty to their mother or father (depending on their gender) versus loyalty to their partner. On the other hand, while they long for romantic fusion, idealizing love, they are convinced that love is always conditional, just as it was in early childhood.
summary: Обнаруживается внутренний конфликт социальных E2 между бессознательной лояльностью к родительской фигуре и партнеру, что мешает глубокой эмоциональной отдаче, несмотря на желание слияния, поскольку они верят, что любовь условна, как в детстве.

title: Sexual dynamics and emotional avoidance in social E2
text:
Generally, they have many affairs but rarely commit to long-term relationships. Women of this subtype tend to be quite faithful, and when they break up with one partner, they typically leave some time before moving on to the next relationship. However, others move between multiple lovers, unable to establish a stable partnership. Some reasons for this include their high expectations, a need for independence and freedom, or prioritizing their career over personal matters. It’s common for the social E2 to be the one to end the relationship, whether due to frustration that comes with their high expectations, boredom, inability to maintain commitment, or fear of intimacy or abandonment.

Sometimes, they use sex as a form of power—seeking conquest and control—but also as a way to release built-up tension or unconsciously avoid true intimacy. There is a resistance to surrendering emotionally, and they rarely relinquish control in the bedroom.

I don’t spend too much time on foreplay, and once the sex is over, I quickly pull away, leaving no room for tenderness or aftercare.

I’ve never let myself be conquered by a man; it’s always been the other way around: I choose, I go, I take. I have a fondness for conquering confident men, leaving them craving more, just for the pleasure of making them want what they can’t have. I also struggle to fully complete that conquest—I’m more about the kisses and the chase than the actual act.

I get genuinely offended when someone I don’t consider my equal tries to seduce me.
summary: This section describes the social E2's approach to sexual relationships, emphasizing their use of sex as a tool for power and control, emotional avoidance, preference for conquest over intimacy, and offense taken when approached by those deemed inferior.

title: ANA BAZA: Social E2 in family dynamics
text:
ANA BAZA

The family, like any group, can become a place where their need for recognition plays out. They take on a role of authority, offering guidance, leadership when necessary, and protection. In a way, they become the emotional backbone of the family, but they can’t afford to show weakness or vulnerability. Displays of affection are avoided because they see them as an exposure of their own fragility, something that could threaten their emotional stability.

Social E2s often find themselves mediating conflicts within the family, which grants them a certain sense of power. This gives them control over their family dynamic, but it’s a control they keep to themselves. They distance themselves from the family system, placing themselves above their siblings and parents. They only allow themselves to receive admiration, not unconditional love.

There’s a strong desire to rise above the ordinary and be seen as special, to secure a place of significance and visibility. Often, they fulfill this by helping their partner gain social recognition that benefits their own personal agenda.

The confusion between love and territoriality

The social E2 often confuses the admiration they get from groups with unconditional love. They believe it’s love when, in reality, it’s just recognition. To them, it feels like applause from those who are part of their territory. But when ownership is involved, love can’t really exist. As they bask in the group’s applause, they mistake admiration for genuine love, care, affection, and inclusion.
