I don’t know if my father found out she had died, but the next day—on my birthday—I was sent to school as if nothing had happened. And that’s where he showed up. He came to the convent school I attended. The nuns didn’t know my grandmother had banned his visits, and I didn’t say anything. Now that my grandmother was gone, they assumed I’d want to see him.

We met in the visiting room and talked for as long as recess lasted. The only thing I remember him saying was, “Happy birthday.” Then he left. I didn’t hear from him again until I was twenty-four.
summary: The narrator recounts her father's public infidelity, her confrontation with B., her eventual return home, her grandmother's death, and her father's brief appearance on her fifteenth birthday, marking a turning point in her emotional suppression.

title: Погружение в печаль и отстранение
text:
A sad and silent teenager

When I was eleven, they transferred me to a new school, and I found the change quite traumatic. I had been in the same public co-ed school with my cousins since I was three, sharing the same class, surrounded by my childhood friends from the neighborhood. In elementary school, I was the wild one, the drama queen. But in middle school, I became autistic.
summary: At age eleven, the narrator's transfer to a new school marks a traumatic shift where she withdraws emotionally, contrasting her former outgoing self with her emerging silence and detachment.

title: Переход в католическую школу для девочек и кризис идентичности
text: They enrolled me in a private Catholic girls’ school run by the Mercedarian Sisters of the Child Jesus, where my sister was in her final year of high school. Moving to an all-girls, religious, structured environment was like stepping into a whole new world. Elementary school had been full of joy, diversity, chaos, and boy energy—it was easy to blend in, to roughhouse, to explore my own masculinity. At the new school, everything was secluded, serious, orderly, disciplined, rigid, and uniform. And suddenly, I realized I had trouble connecting with so many women, since we were just girls. There was no escape. I found them childish, slow, foolish, fragile, envious, prissy, teacher’s pets, obedient... To me, all of that represented femininity. I felt powerless, like there was no space for me to be myself in that environment.
summary: Описание трудного перехода из смешанной школы в строгую женскую католическую школу, где авторка чувствует себя чужой из-за конфликта с навязываемой женственностью и потерей возможности выражать свою мужественность.

title: Ритуал, изоляция и начало подавления себя
text: I remember freezing outside every morning, because at 7:00 AM we raised the flag and recited the Angelus prayer, standing at attention. The first real shock came on the first day of school. My reputation as a troublemaker had arrived before I did. During recess, my sister pulled me aside and said, “I don’t want any principal, nun, or teacher coming to me about your behavior. If they do, I will disown you. So you better behave perfectly. Don’t embarrass me.” And just like that, I fell into a deep sadness. I hid. I stopped talking. I stopped expressing myself the way I had in elementary school. My adolescence became a slow disappearance. From eleven to fifteen, I made myself invisible.
summary: Описание того, как жесткие ритуалы и давление сестры привели к полной эмоциональной изоляции и самоизгнанию — авторка перестала говорить и выражать себя, став невидимой.

title: Кризис одиночества и первая попытка самоуничтожения
text: By fifteen, I felt so awful that one day, when I came home during siesta time, with everyone asleep, I walked into the kitchen, grabbed a knife, and pressed it against my heart. I never went through with it. But I still remember that dark, hollow feeling in my body—the sense that life had no meaning if I wasn’t loved by at least one person who mattered to me.
summary: В 15 лет авторка достигает эмоционального дна и пытается покончить с собой, ощущая глубокую пустоту и убеждение, что жизнь бессмысленна без любви значимого человека.

title: Бесполезные сессии у психолога и разочарование в системе
text: As soon as I started at that school, the principal and teachers wasted no time sending me to the school psychologist—a young woman who had just become a mother and handled the “difficult” cases. I clearly remember how every session went: I sat in front of her and stared. I didn’t say a single word. This went on for a year. She kept asking questions, and eventually, she stopped. From then on, I’d go to her office, sit down, and she’d continue with her paperwork. The bell would ring, I’d stand up, and I’d leave. I never understood why she didn’t talk to the nuns about what was going on. Maybe she wanted to keep her job. Maybe she thought I’d speak up eventually. Or maybe she had no idea what to do with me and didn’t want to admit it. Ironically, today I’m an educational psychologist. Sometimes I think I chose this career to make up for that moment in my life—to help girls like I wish she had helped me. I wish she had seen past my defiance, past my silence, past my pride.
summary: Авторка описывает год бесполезных визитов к школьному психологу, которая не смогла установить контакт, и反思 как этот опыт повлиял на её будущий выбор профессии образовательного психолога.

title: Погружение в одиночество и отвержение заботы
text: Shame, religion, and femininity entered my life. Before long, I had become an incredibly sad, silent, and withdrawn girl, completely isolated. I would sit alone, either at the front or the back of the classroom, never speaking to anyone. Some classmates would try to approach me, wanting to talk or sit next to me, but I wouldn’t let them.
summary: Под влиянием стыда, религии и навязываемой женственности авторка полностью закрывается от социума, отвергая любые попытки одноклассников установить контакт.

title: Сюрприз-праздник как наказание: конфликт с добротой
text: It took me a long time to find my place in that new environment. I needed to understand how everything worked—the structure, the system, the key players, who was in charge. I had mapped out all the social groups, who was friends with whom, who didn’t get along, who was worth approaching, and who wasn’t.  The hardest years I remember in school were between twelve and fourteen. My classmates saw how sad I was and decided to throw me a surprise party at N.’s house. But instead of feeling grateful, I felt embarrassed, uncomfortable, and overwhelmed. I was angry at them for their generosity—it made me feel like I owed them something. Deep down, I felt like I didn’t deserve it. No one in our class had ever been thrown a surprise party before, and to me, that privilege felt more like a punishment, putting me under the spotlight of their pity. I remember them all screaming with excitement while I stood there, frozen, unable to react to all that attention. That kind of pure, selfless kindness was completely foreign to me. In that moment, I felt my orphanhood, my deep sense of emptiness. Their affection reached straight into the core of my wound, the vast, hollow space inside me. It’s a black hole, bottomless, impossible to fill. And every time something warm or loving falls into it, it only reminds me of just how empty it really is.
summary: Авторка описывает, как попытка одноклассников устроить ей сюрприз-праздник вызвала у неё не благодарность, а стыд и гнев — её внутренняя пустота сделала доброту мучительной, а внимание — наказанием.

title: Появление M.: начало исцеления через безусловную заботу
text: Fortunately, during that dry and desolate time, M. appeared—a kind, affectionate, and joyful eighteen-year-old novice. Without asking permission, she stepped right into my life, sitting on the empty bench that had been my only companion until then. Her presence completely transformed the way I engaged with my classmates, my studies, my teachers, and even the school principal (who was also her mentor). But more than that, she changed my relationships outside of school as well. Her arrival felt like a rebirth. After my grandmother, she was the first person who made me feel something close to unconditional love. Her joy for life was contagious, and for reasons I never quite understood, she took me under her wing with a warmth and protectiveness I had never known.  I remember the small meeting room in the convent where we would sit together—an austere, gray space without decorations. But the moment she walked in, the whole room seemed to light up. Being around her was like finding a safe haven, a place where I could emotionally rest from all the anger, violence, and aggression. For the first time, I felt like someone was truly looking after me, offering me structure, affection, boundaries, and a sense of joy in simply being alive. I spent every afternoon in the convent studying with her, and looking back now, I see that our relationship set me on a path toward emotional stability—one I’m still walking today.
summary: Появление М., доброй и заботливой novice, становится turning point в жизни авторки — она впервые ощущает безусловную любовь, безопасность и эмоциональную стабильность, что начинает её путь к исцелению.

title: Anonymous cards and academic ingenuity
text:
M. was only three years older than me, but I saw her as an older sister, almost like a mother. From the moment I met her, she helped me see my classmates through a more compassionate lens. And since I had always loved arts and crafts, I started making tiny little cards, decorated with intricate details, each one carrying a quote from Reader’s Digest, a magazine we regularly received at home. Whenever I sensed that one of my classmates was going through something, I would write a quote that felt right for her and quietly leave the card on her desk during recess.

At first, no one knew who was leaving the little cards, and I loved the mystery of it—like some kind of anonymous guardian angel. But eventually, I was found out, and soon people started asking me to make cards for them to give away. At one point, I was so overwhelmed with requests that I couldn’t keep up. By then, I was talking to almost everyone in the class—M. was the principal’s right hand, and in turn, I was hers. I also realized that my knack for tiny, meticulous handwriting had another use: making cheat sheets for exams. I became a total pro, shrinking down entire notes in exchange for candy.

When M. found out about my little side hustle, she gently suggested that instead of writing everything so small—since it was so much work—I should just take proper notes in a notebook. That’s how I started studying with organized notes. Surprisingly, I had really neat handwriting and was great at structuring information. I liked making my notebook visually clear and well-organized—it helped me remember answers to exam questions more easily by recalling the way I had written, highlighted, or outlined them.
summary: The narrator describes how they began making anonymous inspirational cards for classmates, which evolved into a popular service and led to creating cheat sheets for exams. After guidance from M., they shifted to organized note-taking, discovering a talent for clear, structured study methods that improved their learning.

title: Leadership and recognition in youth organizing
text: Being so close to M. gave me direct access to the convent, the nuns, and the priests in ways I hadn’t expected. One of those ways was organizing my first large-scale event at fifteen: the First Youth for Christ Gathering, which we prepared for the Pope’s upcoming visit. We received a ton of praise, and it was a major moment of recognition for me. It felt like I had spent years hidden away in a dark cave and was suddenly stepping into the light, shining. I felt like I had been discovered—a hidden treasure finally brought into the open.
summary: Through their close relationship with M., the narrator gained access to religious networks and co-organized a significant youth event for the Pope’s visit. The successful gathering brought them public recognition and a profound sense of being seen and valued after feeling invisible.

title: Early romantic ideals and shifting desires
text:
Sexuality: a complicated matter

I started taking an interest in boys when I was ten. I always had a crush on more than one at a time—at least one from every group I was part of. Luckily, at that age, it didn’t really matter whether they liked me back. What mattered most was having someone to daydream about rather than actually making those fantasies a reality.

They all had one thing in common: they looked like good boys. If they were attractive, all the better, but the most important thing was that they were kind. Later, as I got further into adolescence, my gaze shifted—more feline, more daring. I wanted to tame wild beasts, to turn a bad boy into a choirboy, all because he had fallen for me.
summary: The narrator recounts the onset of their romantic interest in boys at age ten, emphasizing kind, 'good boys' as ideal objects of affection. As adolescence progressed, their desires evolved to include a fascination with transforming rebellious or 'wild' boys through romantic influence.

title: Contrasting relationships with A. and P.
text:
When I got my period at fourteen, I met two almost completely opposite boys who introduced me to a whole new side of adolescence. Both were three years older than me. A. was a medical student, while P. attended night school for adults. I saw A. as so mature, so responsible, that it felt like an honor that he liked me—that he even noticed me, a skinny, awkward teenager, at least according to the reflection in my mirror. Although, he did make me aware of my curves when his hands traced them in the backseat of his father’s imported car. I still remember the super-tight pink corduroy pants he loved so much. My innocence and his restraint kept us from going any further than kisses and caresses, but to me, it already felt daring. When I got home at midnight and my uncle R. opened the door, I received the hardest slap of my life.

Then I met P., who was almost the opposite of A.—always with a cigarette in hand, a cat-like gaze, few words, and intense passion. He treated me like a little girl, and I felt cared for, protected by someone twice my size. When he hugged me, his arms formed a cocoon around me, making me feel like nothing bad could happen, like he would defend me from anyone.

We met every afternoon. He came from far away; he had to take several buses to get to me, and we took advantage of dark corners to kiss. His kisses were soft, which was surprising for a guy with so much sexual experience—he had experimented in both directions, with his best friend and with several older women. Yet with me, he only kissed me and wiped my tears, which were frequent. Once again, I felt like I was with someone who allowed me to rest from my own aggression, my struggle, my anger. Every afternoon with him had space and time for me to break down and cry. I was so in love… P. was an enigmatic figure with a reputation as a delinquent. His personal situation was complicated, and that complexity was perhaps what attracted me the most, along with his masculinity and protection, which let me be fragile and vulnerable—maybe for the first time with the opposite sex—without being the one who called the shots.
summary: The narrator describes two contrasting adolescent relationships: with A., a responsible medical student whose affection felt honoring but limited by family boundaries, and with P., a passionate, experienced yet tender delinquent who offered emotional safety and protection, allowing the narrator to express vulnerability for the first time.

title: Relationship turmoil and breakup with P.
text:
But as time passed, our relationship became tumultuous. I was emotionally unstable, and he wanted to “settle down” with me. Until then, he hadn’t cared much about studying, but after meeting me, he enrolled in university. He wanted to be a veterinarian, which meant moving to a distant city, Río Cuarto. The distance made things harder. I was very social, always going out with my group of friends, and problems started. He was jealous, and I wasn’t careful with his feelings.

I realized how intense our relationship had become one night when we went dancing at a club. I had confessed to him that I had let another guy kiss me while he was away. And that night, he decided to get even. He started dancing with a very striking, sexy ex-girlfriend of his and kissed her right in front of me. I walked out. He followed me and told me to get in his car—he would drive me home. But once we were inside, he started ramming into parked cars, not caring about the damage he was causing. Then, he dropped me off in the middle of nowhere, alone and without money. Later, he came back and drove me home. I got out without looking back, holding my head high, refusing to acknowledge the fear I had felt. That was the end of our relationship.
summary: The relationship with P. deteriorated due to the narrator's emotional instability and social behavior, triggering P.'s jealousy. After confessing to kissing another guy, P. retaliated publicly, leading to a destructive and frightening car incident that ended their relationship abruptly.

title: Кульминация бурных отношений с П.
text: I realized how intense our relationship had become one night when we went dancing at a club. I had confessed to him that I had let another guy kiss me while he was away. And that night, he decided to get even. He started dancing with a very striking, sexy ex-girlfriend of his and kissed her right in front of me. I walked out. He followed me and told me to get in his car—he would drive me home. But once we were inside, he started ramming into parked cars, not caring about the damage he was causing. Then, he dropped me off in the middle of nowhere, alone and without money. Later, he came back and drove me home. I got out without looking back, holding my head high, refusing to acknowledge the fear I had felt. That was the end of our relationship.
summary: Описание кульминационного момента в отношениях с П., где его ревность привела к агрессивному поведению и окончательному разрыву. Рассказчица пережила эмоциональную бурю, но сохранила внешнее достоинство.

title: Романтическое лето с J. и образ идеального мужчины
text:
The following summer was the most romantic vacation of my youth. My sister’s boyfriend, H., invited both of us to stay at his uncle’s house. The two of them wanted their own space, so without expecting it, I found myself integrated into the family. Everyone knew the plan except me—I only found out at the doorstep. H. introduced me to his uncles, his three cousins, and his female cousin. The youngest cousin, J., was eighteen—tall, broad-shouldered, attractive, and clearly experienced with women.

Although it all came as a surprise, luckily I immediately liked the family. They were affectionate, warm, and cheerful. They showed me to my new room, which was actually J.’s—it was the coolest and the most private in the house. He had moved to the guest room, which gave him an excuse to visit me often, grabbing his clothes and stealing a kiss or a hug. Our relationship was a secret, though it was so obvious!

Suddenly, I had a wonderful new family, and I felt like we had adopted each other. J. and I became inseparable. We had breakfast together, he walked me to the shop where I started working, we went to the countryside, to the pool, even flying in a helicopter… He never stopped surprising me. It was as if he, too, had read every Corín Tellado novel and wanted to bring them to life.

Despite his sexual experience and perhaps because we lived under the same roof, J. was very careful with me. We never kissed in public, only in the car or the dark corners of his brother’s club, where we went dancing. I loved being in his arms, pressed close while we danced. I feel like I’ve repeated this pattern throughout my love life: I look for a good, fatherly, protective man, to whom I give everything—except my sexuality. I constantly seduce, draw attention, and provoke his desire, only to say no. I love seeing and feeling that desire, but without sharing myself. I only want to be someone’s object of desire, not to give myself away.
summary: Описание бурного и романтического лета с J., в рамках которого рассказчица осознает свой повторяющийся паттерн в отношениях: поиск защитного, отцовского мужчины, к которому она проявляет страсть, но отказывает в сексуальной близости, желая оставаться лишь объектом желания.

title: Вступление в Opus Dei и религиозное увлечение
text:
After that summer, I got involved with a religious social research group. The headquarters of the congregation (some might call it a sect) was in the most expensive part of Córdoba’s city center. When I arrived at the enormous, freshly polished carved wooden door, I rang the bell. A woman, who I later realized was the coordinator, opened it. She was so polite and kind that I simply let myself be led through the grand entrance hall, up a beautiful carved wooden staircase, to the room where the group was already gathered. Of course, we were all very young women.

Just like that, I started working with the team. From the very first moment, I felt like I belonged. They explained that our goal was to research the social conditions of street children and propose realistic but creative solutions.

Motivated by my ambition (since the winning project would be presented to the Pope in Rome), I threw myself into the work. From day one, they also assigned me a spiritual guide and gave me a confession manual filled with an infinite list of sins. The first time I read it, I saw sins I hadn’t even known existed. Every week, I would meet with my spiritual guide and confess everything I had done, having previously reviewed the list of sins. And every week, I took communion at two Masses. One at school and one with the Order, as the group was called… which, as it turned out, was none other than Opus Dei.

A large part of my academic development, my study habits, my skills as a researcher, and my desire for lifelong learning, I owe to the people who guided me during that time.
summary: Рассказ о вступлении в Opus Dei после летнего романа: описание структуры группы, личного вовлечения, духовного руководства, исповедей и влияния на академическое и личное развитие рассказчицы.

title: Уход из Opus Dei и поиск новой духовности
text:
But at twenty, when I started dating J., my first serious boyfriend, I left Opus Dei. Weekly confessions became unbearable. I kept failing at the act of contrition! Because the idea was to never sin again, but I could no longer deny myself the possibility of having a boyfriend or keep feeling guilty about it.

However, I still needed to be part of a religious group, so I began participating in the Universal Christian Gnostic Movement, also known as the “no-sex sect.” They recruited us through lectures and courses on Greek mythology, Atlantis, Ancient Egypt, astrology, psychology and self-knowledge, the Mayans, the Celts, the Far East… Gnosis, as knowledge, was presented as a compilation of all the wisdom from ancient schools. Because of this, it became a doctrine of synthesis, dedicated to revealing all the mysteries that had remained hidden from humanity until now. The sect taught that people must awaken their consciousness and strive for harmony, which was achieved through the elimination of the ego, psychological self-examination, meditation, and the use of sexual energy, considered the most powerful energy in human beings.
summary: Описание ухода из Opus Dei из-за конфликта между религиозными обязательствами и личными желаниями, а также присоединения к гностическому движению, сочетающему духовность, психотехники и особое отношение к сексуальной энергии.

title: Учение секты о сексуальной энергии и браке
text: They believed that a perfect marriage was one in which couples engaged in intercourse without reaching orgasm, so as not to spill semen. Virginity and complete abstinence from masturbation were strongly encouraged. According to their teachings, we were to have only one monogamous partner for life because, during sex, we absorbed the other person’s karma, including that of their past lives. This aligned perfectly with the idea of remaining a virgin until marriage, a marriage that would last forever, just like in the romantic novels of my childhood.
summary: The sect promoted a restrictive view of sexuality, advocating intercourse without orgasm, lifelong monogamy to avoid absorbing karma, and lifelong virginity until marriage as ideal.

title: Привлечение секты и осознание внутреннего поиска
text: This perspective was incredibly appealing to my young mind. At last, I felt I had found a religion that validated what I instinctively felt about sexuality. So, I became part of a new religious movement, filled with people who could support its beliefs with intellectual and academic arguments. It took me twenty years to realize that my spiritual search was not necessarily about belonging to a religion or a secular movement, but rather that I was, at my core, a seeker. But I wouldn’t fully grasp that until much later when I met my teacher, Claudio Naranjo.
summary: The narrator found the sect’s teachings personally validating and joined it, but only after two decades realized her true nature as a seeker, not just a religious adherent.

title: Конкуренция как движущая сила жизни
text:
Competing—above all, competing

Competition has always been a driving force in my life. As a child, I lacked order and discipline, so the message was clear: I had to be intelligent above all else. Intelligent and strategic—to survive, to earn my place in the family. And throughout my life, this belief has been reaffirmed in every action, every thought, every relationship, every interaction.

My specialty was always emotions, matters of the heart. I was fascinated by romance, people’s love lives, and the art of rhetoric. I enjoyed listening to conflicts and giving my opinion or offering a solution. I was particularly skilled at making people see their own responsibility in what was happening to them. I called it “seeking justice,” but in reality, it had more to do with how much I loved hearing myself argue, leaving my conversation partner without a counterargument, and, of course, always having the last word.
summary: Competition shaped the narrator’s life from childhood, driving her to excel intellectually and verbally, particularly in emotional and rhetorical domains where she sought to 'win' arguments and gain recognition.

title: Семейные ожидания и борьба за признание
text:
In my family’s competitive environment, standing out was essential. You had to excel in some area. Money was important, but even more so were university degrees, awards, and social recognition. My cousin C., the eldest of all my cousins, has five university degrees: he’s a doctor (like his father, grandfather, and great-grandfather…), holds degrees in Political Science and International Relations, teaches English (as well as French, Italian, and Portuguese), and is also a licensed auctioneer. He set the bar high.

As for me, I started university at seventeen. My aunts had pushed me ahead a year in kindergarten. They could do that because my aunt S. was one of the teachers at the school. It wasn’t easy to get that permission, but my verbal skills left no room for doubt. However, I ended up losing that extra year due to my first university choice: clearly, I wasn’t mature enough yet.

I first began studying Pharmacy at a private Catholic University, which at the time was one of the most prestigious in the country. There were more than a hundred students in my class, and all I could think about was how to get everyone’s attention. So, I started sneezing over and over again. Everyone turned to look at me, and that’s when I stopped—mission accomplished. At the very least, I would be remembered as “the girl who sneezed.”

But I dropped out after my first year. Chemistry wasn’t for me. Fortunately, before I left, I met one of my best friends, M. I came from a religious background where we didn’t even dare to say words like “bisexuality” or “homosexuality.” However, I started going with M. to gay bars. She often stayed over at my house and loved to talk late into the night in bed. Her presence filled me with a deep sense of connection.
summary: Family pressure to excel through academic and social achievement led the narrator to seek attention in university, culminating in a memorable but ultimately unsuccessful attempt at Pharmacy, while forming a deep bond with a friend who challenged her views on sexuality.

title: Развитие чувств и самопознание через дружбу
text: One night, as she tried to get me to open up about my secrets, she confessed hers: she liked women and was going to leave her longtime boyfriend because she was in love with me. I was stunned. I couldn’t believe it. At the time, we were both finishing our degrees, and I was still dating J. I don’t remember if I even had to tell her “no,” but from that moment on, something shifted between us. I no longer felt uncomfortable with her desire to be close to me. Now that I understood what was happening, I could relax and feel even closer to her because we shared a secret. And that made me feel special. She, in turn, felt completely free, and we started sharing everything on a deeper level. She told me she had hope for us because she knew my sex life with J. was a disaster. And that was because I hadn’t tried being with a woman. She was convinced that my real identity would only emerge once I tried it…
summary: A pivotal moment of mutual confession with her friend M. led to emotional liberation and self-reflection, as the narrator began to question her heterosexual relationship and consider her own potential same-sex attraction.

title: Образовательная психология как призвание
text:
Finding my calling: educational psychology

My journey toward finding my vocation began with a newspaper clipping my cousin gave me, announcing that enrollment for the Educational Psychology program was open. She suggested I check it out. I had no idea that I had just stumbled upon the beginning of a professional path that would lead me down many different roads.

From eighteen to twenty-four, I went through a fairly fulfilling period in my life. I had found my place in the world, both in love and in my career. At university, I was once again in a predominantly female environment, both among students and professors. But this time, the atmosphere was completely different: we were there because we had chosen to be. I loved my classes, and with my basic knowledge of philosophy and other subjects, I could afford to challenge professors and ask questions that sparked heated debates in the classroom. Once again, I found myself drawn to generating controversy or even conflict in group settings. Standing out and becoming the teacher’s favorite student in subjects I was passionate about became a constant in my life—and it’s something I still tend to do in certain environments.
summary: The narrator discovered educational psychology through a cousin’s suggestion, found fulfillment in university, and recognized her pattern of seeking intellectual engagement and standing out in academic settings through debate and challenge.

title: Стратегии поведения в академической среде и становление ассистентом
text:
My usual pattern of behavior in institutional and group settings kicked in again. First, I had to identify everyone’s roles. Second, I needed to devise a strategy to win over those who interested me and thus fulfill my needs. As for the faculty, I was only interested in the best. And fortunately, most of them were, with few exceptions.

Soon, I became a teaching assistant for two of my favorite subjects, working with two of the professors I admired most: Philosophy and Ethics, and Vocational and Occupational Guidance. That was when I discovered how much I liked being the right hand of someone who knows what they’re doing. I absorbed their expertise while managing their schedules and resources. Maybe that’s why I later specialized in this field. It was, in the end, a balance between organizing the student’s agenda and designing tailored guidance plans for them.
summary: The narrator describes their recurring pattern in group settings: identifying social roles and strategizing to win over people of interest. They became a teaching assistant in Philosophy and Ethics, and Vocational and Occupational Guidance, valuing the role of supporting experts and organizing student agendas, which influenced their later specialization.

title: Путь к работе с трудными подростками и личностная мотивация
text:
Looking back, it’s interesting to see how each path opened a new one. After summer break, I learned that a new degree program was launching: Teaching Education for Minors in Neglect and Social Conflict (yes, a very Argentinian name). So, alongside my Educational Psychology studies, I enrolled in this new program. Focusing on working with minors deeply connected me to my own childhood. The stories of the children I started supporting resembled my own, except they lacked even the moderately supportive family I had. This gave me a newfound appreciation for all my aunts, uncles, and cousins—thanks to them, I wasn’t in institutional care or living on the streets.

I felt an urgent need to help those children, to give them something of what I had received. That’s why I got involved in every possible internship from my first year, requesting special permissions, since first-year students weren’t allowed to do practical training. But I leveraged the fact that I was in my second year of Educational Psychology to get into institutions. That way, I spent five years working with minors in shelters and juvenile centers.
summary: The narrator enrolled in a program for teaching minors in neglect and social conflict, which resonated with their own childhood experiences. Motivated by gratitude toward their extended family, they pursued internships despite restrictions, eventually spending five years working with youth in shelters and juvenile centers.

title: Академические достижения, романтические фантазии и терапевтический прорыв
text:
I even convinced several professors to allow open-book exams because, juggling multiple degrees, I only had time to read. I couldn’t keep up with taking notes. In my final year, I scored top grades in nearly every subject, and as my family expected, I graduated with an 8.5 GPA. Not quite the 9.9 averages of my cousins, but I was getting closer. [In Spain’s higher education system, the GPA is calculated on a 0-10 point scale.]

When I started the Teaching for Minors program, I developed two platonic crushes on my professors. The first was the program coordinator, a very religious widower with six children, who had it all: he was serious, intelligent, attractive, and morally impeccable. The second was a highly renowned psychoanalyst who worked in the courts; sexy, also intelligent, warm, flexible, charming, and always smiling.

In my fantasies about the first, I became the mother of his children. The second, however, was adored by the entire class, and he enjoyed it. That didn’t fit my fantasy of marriage; only someone exclusively for me was worthy of being imagined that way. Interestingly, I only ever received praise from the first professor. But I discovered that the second was a good listener, and toward the end of my studies, I started therapy with him. That process helped me end my five-year relationship with J., my first real and formal boyfriend.
summary: The narrator achieved academic success with an 8.5 GPA while managing multiple degrees, developed romantic fantasies about two professors — one inspiring a maternal fantasy, the other admired by all — and began therapy with the second, which ultimately helped them end a five-year relationship.

title: Холодная встреча с отцом и начало юридического образования как компенсаторная стратегия
text:
The last time I saw my father

At that time, when I was twenty-four, my father showed signs of life again. He called me at my aunt S.’s house and said he wanted to see me. We met at a bar. He had heard I was now a professional and wanted to congratulate me. I barely remember our conversation, but I do remember him telling me that I had almond-shaped eyes like my mother. The man sitting across from me was a complete stranger. His sweet, seductive voice repulsed me. I don’t recall how long we talked. Maybe an hour. But I didn’t know where he came from or where he was going. He asked about my studies and my future and seemed interested, but it all felt foreign to me. The last time I had heard from him, I was fifteen. These fleeting, meaningless appearances left me cold and indifferent. I wouldn’t reconnect with him until sixteen years later, when I was in a completely different stage of my life.

As if I didn’t already have enough on my plate, I enrolled in law school under the pretext of helping J. study. A mix of camaraderie and competition developed between us, though I couldn’t say in what proportion. But I do remember that when I aced my exams, he stepped up his efforts and started advancing in the program. We spent three years like that, but therapy helped me realize that, on one hand, I was competing with him to prove I was brighter, more intelligent, and more studious. On the other, I had turned law school into a stage to show off with controversial arguments that put certain professors in difficult positions—professors I didn’t find worthy of admiration. I felt they had it coming; after all, why were they even teaching if they weren’t the best? Later, one could say that karma placed me on the receiving end of similar treatment in my own career as a university professor, with students who behaved just as I once had.
summary: At 24, the narrator met their estranged father briefly, feeling alienated by his presence. Soon after, they enrolled in law school nominally to support J., but it became a venue for intellectual competition and performative challenges to authority, later recognizing a karmic mirror in their future teaching experiences.

title: Осознание истинной мотивации в праве и возвращение к педагогической миссии
text: But the real reason I pursued law was that I wanted to be a worthy successor to my mother—to defend children, just as she had. When I realized this in therapy, I dropped law school and focused on finishing my studies in Educational Psychology and Teaching for Minors. It was the right decision, easing the tension in my relationship with J. by placing us in separate professional fields.
summary: The narrator reveals that their pursuit of law was driven by a desire to emulate their mother’s child advocacy. Through therapy, they recognized this motivation, left law school, and returned to Educational Psychology and Teaching for Minors, which eased relational strain with J. by diverging their career paths.

title: Финансовая независимость и образ жизни после разрыва
text:
By then, I considered myself quite a catch: I was pretty, intelligent, professionally accomplished, and financially secure, with a lifelong orphan’s pension (so long as I remained single). If I married, I’d lose it. So, for the first years of our relationship, I covered all the expenses, paid for every whim—his, mine, or ours. I lived in my uncle A.’s house, which was very large and had all the comforts, while J. lived downtown in a small apartment with his brother, with only the essentials: two beds, a table, a couple of chairs, and a bathroom so narrow you had to squeeze in sideways.

I put everything at his disposal, including the car and motorcycle I bought for myself. I was repeating some of my parents’ patterns—the support my mother had given my father in his studies and the financial stability she provided. Except J. was a vastly improved version of my father: kind, loyal, faithful, and generous… And I was a slightly less remarkable version of my mother, because what I had wasn’t the result of my own efforts but something I had inherited from her.

J. graduated a year before I finished my degrees, which put physical distance between us. He returned to his hometown to be with his family, while I stayed in Córdoba with mine. I dreamed of traveling the world, studying abroad, learning languages, and pursuing postgraduate degrees. He wanted to get married, buy a house, get a dog, wash the car on Sundays, and have family barbecues in the countryside.
summary: Автор описывает свою финансовую независимость после разрыва с J., свой образ жизни, сравнивая себя и партнёра с родителями, а также различия в их жизненных целях.

title: Попытка восстановления отношений и окончательный разрыв
text:
A seemingly fresh start

J. suggested I move with him to Metán so we could rebuild our relationship, but just the thought of staying in that town forever made me dizzy. However, I agreed to move to Salta, 150 kilometers away from Metán, and settled into an apartment owned by my uncle. J. visited me every weekend. On the ground floor of my building was a very chic venue where lawyers coming from the courthouse and some members of Salta’s high society would gather. When J. and I started discussing living together, I was overcome with dread. At twenty-five, just imagining a shared life made me want to run for the hills.

Not long after, I told him I was sorry, but we had to break up. He couldn’t believe it and even proposed to me, but by then, I was sure I wanted nothing to do with marriage, children, or being tied down in any way. I bolted.
summary: Автор описывает попытку восстановить отношения с J., переехав в Сальту, но в итоге решает окончательно разорвать связь из-за страха перед браком и привязанностью.

title: Начало независимой жизни и работа с детьми
text:
Now, finally alone, free, and independent, I was entering a new phase of my life. I quickly set up a private practice working with gifted children and teenagers seeking career guidance. I felt safe and comfortable living and working in the same space, only leaving to buy necessities before retreating back home. I still didn’t know anyone in Salta, had no friends, and no family ties. My father’s relatives were likely somewhere in Chile, though I had no idea where. My mother’s family was either in Metán, 150 kilometers away, or in Córdoba, 900 kilometers away.

Working with children and teenagers was an uphill battle. Looking back, I realize my own childhood and adolescence left me ill-equipped to guide others beyond the technical skills I had mastered. My only real strength (the reason I imagine I was able to support my patients at all) was my good rapport with parents and teachers. I soon realized I was more comfortable working with adults than children, and began looking for another path within educational psychology.
summary: После разрыва автор начинает независимую жизнь, открывает частную практику по работе с одарёнными детьми, но осознаёт, что предпочитает работу со взрослыми.

title: Работа в институте Жан Пиаже и растущее чувство принадлежности
text:
For months, I stayed in my cave. But while searching for alternatives, I landed a teaching job at the Jean Piaget Institute, the only one offering that degree at the time. The warm, almost familial welcome from the institute’s owners, a mother and her two daughters, combined with my growing enthusiasm for teaching, gave me a sense of belonging. Suddenly, I had a new, makeshift family with whom I shared more than just a simple work relationship. I felt valued and supported.

But the little worm of ambition is always on the move. The moment I feel like I’m getting somewhere, a voice inside me whispers that I need more. I could have settled for my practice and my teaching job. But no—I was haunted by the idea of going down in history, of achieving greatness, of leaving a legacy, of creating something that would impact the world. A career confined to such a limited social sphere was not an interesting life for me.
summary: Автор устраивается на работу в институт Жан Пиаже, где чувствует принадлежность, но её постоянно мучает амбиция достичь большего и оставить след в мире.

title: Изоляция, самопомощь и поиск утешения в потреблении
text:
While I had this insatiable drive socially and professionally, my personal life was the opposite. I had no close friends and lived in relative isolation. I became a Blockbuster member and spent entire weekends binge-watching movies. My daily ritual involved going to the mall, and my personal therapy consisted of visiting all the fashion stores, trying on every piece of clothing that caught my eye and buying anything that looked good on me.

I ate the same thing every day, completely neglecting my nutrition. I still have this habit as I write this biography. Self-care requires a level of self-love I didn’t have then and still don’t really have now.
summary: Несмотря на профессиональные успехи, автор ведёт изолированную жизнь, компенсируя эмоциональную пустоту потреблением и рутиной, пренебрегая самообслуживанием.

title: Появление близкой дружбы с Л.
text:
Finally making friends

After some time, I met L., an absolutely charming architect who remains one of my closest friends. We had an instant connection. He was so funny, sharp, and quick-witted that I couldn’t stop laughing around him. He introduced me to his friends and took me to the bar owned by his older brother, A. A year older than L., A. was also funny and intelligent but had a world-weary air, as if he’d lived a hundred lives, despite being only three years older than me.
summary: Автор знакомится с Л., харизматичным архитектором, который становится одним из её closest friends, и через него она входит в его социальный круг.

title: Relationship with A. and its unconventional nature
text: Their father was a bit confused by me. He first met me with the younger brother, then, a few days later, saw me with the older one. Fortunately, L. and A. had nothing but love and understanding for each other, and when A. and I started a relationship, there was no resentment from L. And I say “relationship” rather than “romance” because it was unconventional in many ways. For one, I knew his entire family, but he never met mine. And, more importantly, neither of us had any real interest in a sexual relationship—not with each other or with anyone else. We tried a couple of times, but it was a disaster. It just didn’t work, and neither of us insisted again. We were an odd couple, only ever seen together at his bar, where I went daily to keep him company. It was more of a father-daughter dynamic than a romantic bond. We stayed together for two years.
summary: Describes an unconventional, non-sexual relationship with A., characterized by a father-daughter dynamic, mutual respect with L., and a two-year companionship centered at A.'s bar.

title: The first level of ambition: leadership in school administration
text:
At twenty-six, I applied for the principal position at the San Ignacio de Loyola Private School, a school struggling with discipline issues—something I felt prepared for, given my experience working with institutionalized minors. Looking back, it amazes me that I never once doubted myself, even though I was competing against professionals with management experience. The student body’s challenges were quite complex; they resembled institutionalized minors more than typical schoolchildren. That became my key argument for getting the job—I believe my background in youth institutions is what won them over.

My first proposal was to conduct a full assessment by interviewing all the teachers. The results led to my boldest recommendation: replace the entire staff. Most teachers were already looking to leave for a different school, exhausted from years of dealing with a difficult environment. I negotiated their severance packages, and the school owners agreed. Everyone benefited. Teachers got a fresh start, and I could build a new team from scratch, free from the baggage of previous management. So, I launched an extensive hiring process: I prepared a written questionnaire, designed an interview model, and then submitted reports on the candidates’ profiles for the final selection.

Looking back, I marvel at my fearlessness in stepping into the unknown, with no prior experience. Everyone believed I knew exactly what I was doing. The team I selected was very strong, but it was more the result of intuition than reason. The only drawback was that everyone was older than me, which meant I had to work on asserting my authority. That defining moment came in the first week of school when I expelled five students who had broken into the school’s kiosk. That set the tone for both staff and students: I had authority, and I wasn’t afraid to use it to get rid of the worst offenders.

The average age of the teaching staff was forty. That meant there was less of an age gap between me and the troubled students than between me and the teachers. Because of my experience in juvenile centers, the teachers started sending unruly students to my office, which led to two consequences: I no longer had time to manage the educational project, and the teachers, whether out of convenience or inability, completely delegated authority over the students to me. Due to my inexperience, I took on that responsibility entirely because, deep down, it was what I knew how to do. Soon, our school gained a reputation for handling difficult cases and taking in students expelled from other schools.

One skill I did have, however, was knowing how to handle difficult parents, even those whose children I expelled in the first week, for whom I found spots in other schools. This earned me a reputation for being fair, but in reality, I did it because I wanted to be liked by everyone and, more than anything, to present myself as the savior. As I focused more on students and families, things only got worse; I wasn’t actually doing my job as principal. The truth was, I wasn’t the right person for the role. It wouldn’t be the first time I convinced both myself and others that I was capable, only to be proven wrong.
summary: Details the narrator's fearless appointment as school principal, staff overhaul, assertion of authority through disciplining students, unintended shift into behavioral management, and self-awareness of pursuing the role for validation rather than competence.

title: The second level of ambition: influencing provincial policy
text:
I decided it would be a good idea to write a letter to the governor of the province of Salta, outlining the shortcomings of his policies on minors. After everything I had experienced at the school, I had reached out to professionals and institutions and developed some ideas for improvements. To this day, I still don’t know what exactly in that letter caught the attention of the governor’s secretary’s assistant, but I was called in for an interview.

I remember her asking me challenging questions about my letter, and I instinctively adopted a competitive stance. But luckily, she saw something in me beyond my arrogance and display of knowledge. She gave me a wise warning: “I think you could bring fresh air to the Department of Family and Minors, but if you talk to the governor’s secretary the way you talked to me, forget about working in this administration.”

Indeed, the secretary functioned like a prime minister. He was a strategic porteño, feared by everyone, because nothing happened without his approval. The governor didn’t make a move without his consent. I was about to face the highest filter. Fortunately, I had been warned, so I presented myself with great caution and restraint. He then told me I would become the advisor to the Director of Family and Minors for the province. That meant I would be advising the director—a gynecologist—on all programs and institutions for minors. I couldn’t believe it. I had gone from a frustrated school principal to the upper ranks of government.
summary: Describes how a critical letter to the governor led to an interview, a warning about interpersonal style, and ultimately an appointment as advisor to the Director of Family and Minors, marking a rise into provincial government despite initial missteps.

title: Работа в технической команде и осознание влияния внешности
text:
I joined a massive technical team, full of all kinds of people. Some were highly qualified, while others were burned out, resenting the fact that they had to work under a gynecologist who knew nothing about the field—and even more so under a 27-year-old newcomer who dressed like she was going to a party every day, never repeated an outfit, and whose miniskirts and plunging necklines were quite scandalous to the older, heavyset women and mothers who made up most of the team.

Later, I would come to understand just how much my appearance and attitude had contributed to the deep rejection I provoked. But at first, I wasn’t aware of anything or anyone. I was in my own world. I had no idea how intensely seductive I was toward anything that moved, especially authority figures. And since they were men, I got what I wanted. I was aware of my need for attention, but I didn’t see it as seduction, because that would have meant admitting that I needed others to look at me, something I never would have acknowledged.
summary: Автор описывает своё вхождение в техническую команду, где её молодость и provocative appearance вызывали resentment у старших коллег. Затем она осознаёт, как её внешность и поведение провоцировали отторжение, ноInitially она не осознавала своей соблазнительности по отношению к authority figures, особенно мужчинам, и интерпретировала своё поведение как естественное, отрицая потребность во внимании.

title: Третий уровень амбиций: трансформация отдела
text:
The third level of ambition: transforming the department

I started working with strategic planning, an area I was still training in. Of course, I was just playing it by ear. The real experts were S. and C., two specialists trained in Buenos Aires with extensive knowledge and experience in the field. I think we made an interesting team: Through them, I could implement changes effectively, and through me, they had a direct line to the director’s office. That’s how we began a period of transformation within the department.

It wasn’t easy. There was resistance from all sides, especially from the more senior specialists in the department. But I neither saw nor listened to them; I was operating at a different speed. My only goal was to completely overhaul the department, applying the models I was learning from the UN and the IMF. I coordinated with the experts on methodology, delegating tasks to others. I had found my ideal place: overseeing other people’s work, moving from meeting to meeting, and serving as the perfect bridge between politics and technical expertise. I learned a lot, and combined with my ambition, that soon propelled me to even higher levels.
summary: Автор описывает третий уровень её амбиций — трансформацию отдела через стратегическое планирование. Несмотря на сопротивление старших специалистов, она действует как мост между политикой и техническими экспертами, используя знания S. и C. и модели UN/IMF. Её цель — полная перестройка отдела, и она находит своё идеальное положение в координации иDelegating, что ускоряет её карьерный рост.

title: Четвёртый уровень амбиций: Grupo Ferro и личная позиция
text:
The fourth level of ambition: Grupo Ferro

Soon, my name reached the governor’s ears, thanks to a speech on childhood that the Secretary of Social Development had asked me to write. The speech made a great impression, and they wanted to know who had written it. That’s how I was invited to take charge of the methodology behind what would later become Grupo Ferro, a group of young politicians the governor was recruiting for his re-election campaign. Through this, I started meeting lawyers, economists, engineers, doctors, architects, the children of influential politicians, and technical experts from various government sectors. Once again, I was one of the youngest in the group. But since 80% of them were men, I had the advantage of capturing their attention.

At first, their interest was undoubtedly in my physical appearance, but it didn’t take long for me to earn their respect through my professionalism. My advantage was that I had the tools of strategic planning and could channel their knowledge and skills into a common project: reviewing government policies and identifying necessary improvements by region, across every sector.

The governor provided us with a headquarters—an old space near the railways that had been renovated, which is how we got the name Grupo Ferro. We met there every night with different groups, and I coordinated them all. It was an experience that made me well-known among the rising young politicians—many of whom are now ministers, Supreme Court judges, mayors, senators, and congressmen. What stood out the most was that I had no mentor or political sponsor. Yet I spoke to judges, legislators, and ministers as an equal. In fact, I didn’t even feel intimidated by the governor, and now I understand why: I didn’t recognize anyone as an authority. To me, they all seemed unworthy or immoral in some way—I knew their weaknesses, which diminished them in my eyes.

I acted like someone with powerful backing, as if I were untouchable. I voiced my opinions freely, without fear or deference. Someone once told me I seemed like God’s advisor—that I behaved as if I only answered to him… not so he could tell me what to do, but so I could give him orders.
summary: Автор описывает четвёртый уровень амбиций — создание Grupo Ferro, где её профессионализм и инструменты стратегического планирования позволяют ей завоевать уважение несмотря на первоначальное внимание к внешности. Она позиционирует себя как равную властителям, не признавая их авторитета, видя их слабости и действуя как если бы отвечала только высшему принципу, что подчёркивает её независимость и внутреннюю уверенность.

title: Личная жизнь: дистанцирование, конкуренция и переосмысление отношений
text:
Something similar happened in my personal life. Despite receiving romantic advances almost daily, I ignored them all. This kept me in a sort of untouchable, immaculate space. I felt equal to men, and to certain women who had adopted a similarly professional, masculine approach. This, once again, left me isolated in terms of personal connections. My relationships with both men and the women I respected were based on competition. I couldn’t relax with anyone, nor could I show weakness or vulnerability. I was not yet thirty, but I carried myself like a seasoned veteran.

During that time, I met many men—single, engaged, and married. My main interest was feeling desired. I would push the situation to the limit, to the point where they inevitably suggested sex, and that was my cue to leave. Looking back, I see this as a way of preserving a certain “virginity” tied to my disconnection from my own desire—beyond that, I simply couldn’t conceive of sex without love. In fact, I could only consider intimacy if I felt genuinely cared for.

At that point, I had convinced myself that I wasn’t meant to have a romantic partner, let alone children. It helped to think that the traditional Argentine model of life wasn’t for me—especially not in Salta, where women, no matter how professional or accomplished, were still expected to take a step behind men. Women could have careers and hold positions of power, but men were allowed freedoms that they were not. So, I decided my life would be centered around my studies and my career.
summary: Автор описывает свою личную жизнь: избегание романтических связей несмотря на ежедневные advances, сохранение дистанции через конкуренцию и невозможность проявлять уязвимость. Она связывает своё поведение с сохранением внутренней «девственности» и невозможностью интимности без любви и заботы. Отвергая традиционные гендерные роли в Аргентине, особенно в Salta, она выбирает жизнь, сосредоточенную на учёбе и карьере.

title: El Caldero: A Bohemian Haven
text:
Through my many jobs and my uncanny ability to strike up conversations with anyone, anywhere, I had filled my contact list with an incredible mix of people. I lived on the seventh floor of a building with a breathtaking view of the Andean foothills, and I turned my apartment into the perfect setting for legendary dinner parties—bringing together psychics, witches, drag queens, yuppies, therapists, journalists, etc. It was the ideal environment for the next big idea: buying a bar with my friends V. and T. It would be a place where we could bring together people from all walks of life, centralize the city’s nightlife, and put our weekends to productive use.

The bar was beautiful. It was called El Caldero. We became the first venue in town to host live bands from Thursday to Saturday, featuring jazz, blues, and rock. In Salta, a province where folk music reigned, this was a revolutionary concept. Since I was still working for the government, we often had high-profile guests: the Minister of Finance, the governor’s right-hand man, and their entire entourage. Naturally, we’d close the bar just for them.

At the same time, I also co-owned a taxi, purely as an investment, with A., my platonic partner. He also had a bar and started organizing concerts, which turned into direct competition. Business suffered, and for a while, our bar became the go-to spot for musicians after their gigs elsewhere. They called it their favorite bar. That’s when the zapadas—jam sessions—began. Musicians from different bands would show up with their instruments, and new melodies would emerge spontaneously. Those were magical nights. It felt like having a personal soundtrack. It was probably El Caldero’s finest era, when it became a bohemian, artistic haven, the musicians’ home.
summary: The narrator describes creating and running El Caldero, a bar in Salta that became a vibrant cultural hub hosting diverse live music and jam sessions, despite political and professional challenges, before sensing growing toxicity and considering a move abroad.

title: A Pivotal Decision: Leaving for Spain
text:
Meanwhile, I could sense the political climate growing more toxic. A crisis was looming. The beginning of the end was already visible, even if not everyone realized it. I knew I had to explore other options, and that’s when I started seriously considering moving abroad. Spain became part of my plan. It was also a pivotal moment in my professional life. I had reached the top; there was nowhere higher to go that interested me. Climbing any further would have meant deeper commitment to the ruling party, which I refused to do, since corruption was everywhere.

Then came the moment of truth: they officially asked me to join the party. Looking back, I see it as a test of my loyalty to the cause. That’s when I knew—I wanted no permanent ties, no obligations. I also had access to certain information I wanted no part of. So, I announced I was taking a sabbatical year in Spain, to further my studies and bring back new skills. It was believable—at the time, even I didn’t realize I would never return.

I had my family, a house, a name, a place in society and politics. If I had stayed, I would probably hold some high-ranking position today. But something was missing. And I didn’t know what it was.

Until I met Claudio Naranjo.
summary: Facing political toxicity and professional stagnation, the narrator declines a party invitation, takes a sabbatical to Spain, and reflects on what was missing in her life—setting the stage for her encounter with Claudio Naranjo.

title: New Beginnings in Madrid
text:
My beginnings in Madrid

I arrived in Madrid in September 2000. I had enrolled in a doctoral program at the Complutense University, in the Department of Research Methods in Education. At thirty, it felt like being eighteen again. I found an apartment with two roommates, just 200 meters from the university. Financially, I was secure. I had my life savings and my mother’s pension. I didn’t need to work. I could devote myself entirely to studying, becoming, once again, the eternal student.

Then, at the end of 2001, the corralito happened in Argentina. Overnight, all my money was trapped there. Suddenly, I had nothing available to me. I was forced to start over from scratch. I tried working at a Mexican restaurant. I lasted one night.

Since a postgraduate degree wasn’t enough, I had also enrolled in a master’s program at Francisco de Vitoria University and an expertis at UCM. It was just like my university days when I was studying three degrees at once. Now I see my need for intensity. One degree simply wasn’t enough. Fortunately, through my master’s program, I was encouraged to apply for one of the available internship scholarships. This would grant me a residency permit and an income to continue funding my postgraduate studies.

I landed an interview at Soluziona, one of Unión Fenosa’s companies. I started as an intern, and within six months, I was promoted to Education and Training Manager. This came with some drawbacks, as my colleagues typically spent years moving up from intern to junior consultant, then senior consultant, project manager, and finally, manager. It’s as if I carried a deep sense of lack within me, which fueled my false sense of abundance, making me feel the need to fill that void with achievements, control, self-importance, and grandeur… I struggle with knowing where the line is between truth and deception, between what I am truly worth and know, and what I am not suited for or capable of doing. There are moments when I believe the stories I tell others and myself, and others when I realize I’ve managed to deceive people about my abilities.
summary: After moving to Madrid and securing academic opportunities, the narrator faces financial upheaval due to Argentina’s corralito, pursues multiple degrees, gains rapid professional promotion, and reflects on an inner drive to prove worth through achievement, masking a deep sense of lack.

title: Meeting My Husband: A Moment of Grace
text:
Meeting my husband

In 2001, I also met my future husband. The first time I saw him was at his home. I rang the doorbell, and he opened the door. When our eyes met, I swear I heard a heavenly choir of angels singing, and I thought I saw a glow radiating from behind him. The impact was so intense that, for hours, I couldn’t focus on anything else.
summary: The narrator recounts the profoundly spiritual and transformative first encounter with her future husband, describing a sense of divine presence and overwhelming emotional impact upon meeting him.

title: Идеализация мужа и духовный путь отношений
text:
So handsome, with the sweetest gaze I had ever seen. His kindness was written all over his face. Over time, as I got to know him better, his virtues only multiplied: generous, kind, thoughtful, hardworking, organized, a devoted son, a caring brother, a loyal friend… Years later, he would also become the most incredible father. In short, a perfect man. From my idealized perspective, he was an enhanced combination of all the qualities I had admired in different people throughout my life. I was also keenly aware of the long journey I had ahead of me to live up to that idealization.

Eighteen years have passed, and we’ve faced and overcome countless crises, some quite profound. But today, I can say that I would choose him all over again. Thanks to the wisdom I gained later, I now understand that this relationship has been a spiritual journey.
summary: The author describes her idealized perception of her husband as embodying all admired qualities, acknowledges the effort required to live up to that image, and reflects on their 18-year relationship as a spiritual journey strengthened by overcoming crises.

title: Юпи-годы: корпоративный успех и внутренний конфликт
text:
My yuppie years

Working in a multinational company opened me up to a world I already knew—but this time, the European version. It was a small political ecosystem, upheld by the patriarchy, structured around hierarchies, machismo, and power games with opposing factions played from the shadows. Once again, I felt right at home—I understood exactly how things worked. And to blend in with my new environment, I bought suits, handbags, shoes, and sunglasses that matched perfectly with my red convertible, the ultimate “wind-in-your-hair” model.

I fit seamlessly into my new job. I dove headfirst into the corporate consulting world, traveling across Spain to sell and develop projects on quality management, environmental sustainability, and workplace risk prevention. In this fast-growing and highly competitive environment, I had to learn fast—no one asked me how much I knew about quality management; they just sent me straight into organizations to evaluate them.

I specialized in quality management. My official training at the Club de Excelencia CEG allowed me to become a licensed EFQM Model assessor, which enabled me to do what I loved most: listen to problems and propose creative solutions, tell organizations what they were doing wrong, and show them how to fix it. They obeyed me—and even thanked me. Oh, it was perfect! My ego was dancing with joy…

My name began circulating in academic circles, then among study groups, and eventually in public administration. Once again, I was making a name for myself, both technically and politically, by connecting professionals and organizations. One of my key strengths was being a bridge.

But I only lasted two years at Soluziona. Why? The hyper-competitive atmosphere, where I couldn’t win everyone’s admiration; my difficulty relating to women and, therefore, forming bonds with my female colleagues; and the total lack of admiration I felt for my bosses. There was also the lack of motivation—quality management systems didn’t truly transform the people running them; they only improved the formalities and language used to present them.

I left the company after a conversation with one of my immediate superiors, who made me realize that I had climbed too quickly and hit a ceiling once again. In six months, I had gone from intern to manager. But I wanted more. And I was told that wasn’t possible. My superior said, “Do you see any women in the positions you’re aiming for? Well, that’s no coincidence. Your only option is to keep specializing, to manage more and more products. But if I were you, I wouldn’t set my sights any higher.” It was a clear boundary.

So, once again, I started over, this time as a freelancer. Leveraging the connections I had built in the different groups I was part of, I quickly became a trainer, consultant, evaluator, and event organizer for various educational organizations. Within a short time, I was working with over 200 schools across Spain, from early childhood education to universities. My income surpassed my husband’s, which gave me the freedom to travel and be away as much as I pleased. Once again, I was thriving in my ego-driven world.

I traveled constantly, giving training sessions and coordinating conferences and conventions on early childhood education. This allowed me to refine my political, strategic, and communication skills, making me well-known among my peers. I was at my peak—schools kept asking for more training, and I had to invent new courses as soon as I finished the previous ones. People said I injected creativity into their veins, and I was completely happy. I had it all: a partner who admired me and money that was entirely the result of my own efforts, allowing me to indulge in all my whims and even cover his. And yet, as always, something was missing. Not everything was as wonderful or as perfect as it seemed.
summary: The author recounts her successful corporate career in quality management, her rapid rise and eventual departure due to gender barriers and lack of fulfillment, her transition to freelancing in education, and her external success contrasted with an enduring inner sense of something missing.

title: Беременность как источник радости и трансформации
text:
The first “clicks”

At thirty-six, my biological clock suddenly started ticking loudly. It was a critical moment since both of us were at the peak of our careers, but I managed to convince him, and almost immediately, I got pregnant.

We were completely unprepared for it, and I was overwhelmed by a wave of anxiety, lack, and maternal ignorance—something I can clearly see now, but at the time, I was oblivious to it. Being pregnant was the best physical state I had ever experienced. For the first time in my life, I could relax about my body: no need for high heels or tight clothes. My breasts were full, and I constantly felt accompanied. It was wonderful. I didn’t suffer from any typical pregnancy discomforts; I felt better than ever.
summary: The author describes her unexpected pregnancy at 36, initial anxiety and inexperience, and the profound physical and emotional ease she felt during pregnancy, which contrasted with her usual bodily insecurities.

title: Поиск знаний о материнстве и разочарование в теории
text:
To make up for my lack of firsthand experience with motherhood, I turned to books and workshops. I took a course with a pediatrician and an obstetrician-gynecologist, both of whom later became well-known figures in the world of natural childbirth. In fact, the pediatrician’s very first patient was my firstborn child. From that moment on, she became a key figure in guiding and supporting my journey into motherhood, as my son had various symptoms. Through her, I was introduced to the world of homeopathy and met professionals from different fields: etiotherapy, osteopathy, anthroposophic rhythmic massage, eurythmy, Pikler-Lóczy pedagogy, as well as childminders and doulas. I started connecting more with psychological and pedagogical aspects rather than the business world.

Twenty-two months later, my second daughter was born. I didn’t breastfeed either of my children, which I deeply regret. I was completely overwhelmed. I had taken every possible workshop and course on natural parenting, yet I couldn’t translate any of it into my real, day-to-day life. I simply couldn’t embody the knowledge I had acquired.
summary: Автор описывает, как пыталась компенсировать отсутствие опыта материнства через курсы и книги по естественному родительству, познакомилась с альтернативными методами воспитания, но не смогла применить теоретические знания на практике, что привело к чувству перегрузки и разочарования.

title: Авария партнёра как поворотный момент в осознании своей роли
text:
Then one day, suddenly—click! My partner had a motorcycle accident, shattering his left collarbone, the very shoulder where I rested my head to fall asleep.

As a result, he couldn’t take care of himself. He needed help to shower, dress, and even carry out simple household tasks. He also couldn’t lift the kids. That was the moment I realized how absent I had been from my own family. My job required constant travel and long hours; I often came home when the children were already asleep. I had a husband and two kids whom I barely saw and whose needs I didn’t even know. I took the accident as a message from the universe. Meant for him, of course, but also for me. Suddenly, I could see everything he had been carrying on his shoulders while I was out in the world, playing a more masculine role than a feminine one.
summary: Автор описывает, как несчастный случай с партнёром стал прозрением: она осознала свою эмоциональную и практическую отсутствие в семье, несмотря на внешний успех, и увидела, как её партнёр нес бремя заботы о доме и детях в её отсутствие.

title: Встреча с Клаудио Наранхо и начало пути в эннеаграмме
text:
At the same time, I had just received a student project from one of my university classes about contemporary thinkers in education. Most of the authors were ones I already knew (they came up every year), except for one: Dr. Claudio Naranjo. I had never heard of him before. I started researching him and was completely fascinated by his online videos. He had published his book Changing Education to Change the World a few years earlier, and as I was looking into him, I came across a four-and-a-half-day course organized by his foundation called An Introduction to the Psychology of Enneatypes. I decided to sign up. When my colleagues asked me what it was about, I told them, “I have no idea, but I’m going.”

The SAT Program

What I encountered when I arrived at the course was mind-blowing, especially since I was coming from my yuppie world. I walked in wearing my perfectly matched three-inch heels, coordinating handbag, fitted suit, and designer glasses. And suddenly, I found myself in a room where everyone was barefoot. Not only that. They were lying on the floor! Scattered across rugs and cushions. I nearly had a heart attack.

My first thought was, What have I gotten myself into? I urgently looked for a chair. There were very few, considering how many of us were there, but with the short skirt I was wearing, there was no way I was sitting on the floor—good Lord! Then there was how everyone was dressed. They looked like they had stepped straight out of the 1960s: tracksuits, long hair, braids, dreadlocks, beards, gray hair, unshaven legs… My God, these people had clearly never set foot in a proper hair salon. And me? I had just come from Llongueras.

From that moment on, I was caught completely off guard. My mind wasn’t processing any logical thoughts, just waves of emotions rushing in and out, without me even understanding what was happening. I remember some of my colleagues talking to the therapists because they were concerned about how I was reacting to the different exercises. Most of the participants had experience with Gestalt therapy, were therapists themselves, had done family constellations, or had been through other personal development processes. I seemed to be the only one who had no clue what I was doing there.

As the days went by, I became more and more certain that I had stumbled upon something huge. For the first time in my life, I wasn’t just learning intellectually. I was taking notes, but it didn’t matter; this wasn’t about grasping fixed content. My body was understanding, and that kind of understanding wasn’t something I could explain with words. It came out through emotions. I couldn’t remember the last time I had cried so deeply, mourning wounds I hadn’t even realized were still there.

The workshop therapists were Assumpta Mateu and the beloved, dearly missed Ramón Resino. On the last day, I went up to him and said, “Don Ramón, I think Claudio Naranjo would find it interesting to meet me.”

I still remember his face. He was stunned for a moment, then burst into warm laughter. “Of course! I’ll put you in touch with Asunta Hormaechea in Madrid so she can connect you with him.” Then I asked where I could continue my training and which therapist he would recommend for my personal process. He suggested I take the next level of training, SAT 1. He also gave me the names of Paco Peñarrubia, the Madrid School of Gestalt Therapy, and Pedro de Casso. And off I went.

Claudio Naranjo

Shortly after completing the Introduction to the Psychology of Enneatypes course, I traveled to Barcelona to meet the man who would become my teacher, Claudio Naranjo.
